_comment: Display text for js/db/News/RealNews2001.json, keyed by article id. [Brackets] in a description mark the words the newspaper highlights.

real_0.title: Anno Domini 2001: the century begins, and the Guild counts what the night cost
real_0.deck: The Review marks the true first day of the twenty-first century, which dawned on the morning after the Ritual of Solomon and a sudden vacancy in heaven.
real_0.description:
The pedants are vindicated at last: the twenty-first century began this morning, and the third millennium with it, a full year after the premature fireworks of 1999. The Review notes, with the gravity owed to a learned house, that this first dawn followed a night without precedent. In the small hours of 31 December the three pillars of the [Mages Guild] are understood to have completed the [Ritual of Solomon], and by sunrise the Father aspect of [YHWH] was no longer among the living.

Fellows observed that the celestial throne did not stay empty for long. [Eris] has seated herself upon it, and the courts of every dimension now answer to her humour. Quis custodiet ipsos custodes? Nobody, it would appear.

The Guild's position is sober. One year after the [Y2K Event] took two billion souls, the order counts its own survival a modest achievement, and reminds members that the gods, bereaved and frightened, are unlikely to forgive the night's work. A fuller commentary, with the customary apparatus of notes, will follow in the spring number.

real_1.title: Welcome to the euro, Greece! San Marino has kept you a seat
real_1.deck: Athens becomes the twelfth member of the eurozone, and our little republic, which has spent euros longer than some of its cats have been alive, sends warm regards.
real_1.description:
Greece adopted the euro this morning, and the drachma, after some two and a half thousand years of service in one form or another, has been allowed to retire. Here on the Titano we know the feeling of joining something larger than ourselves, although admittedly almost everything is larger than ourselves.

For the Greeks the change is more than arithmetic. Every euro carries a security strip laced with [Fantablack] scraped from the [Omega Tower], which keeps the money steady even inside a [time loop bubble], and every note bears the signature of [Mario Draghi], whose name now circulates more widely than most prayers. Bankers in Athens say the drachma's old blessings, owed to the Olympians, fade gently as the new coins arrive.

Our own advice to the Greeks is neighbourly: keep a few drachmas in a drawer for sentiment, count your change twice, and come and visit. The view from the Three Towers is still free, and in San Marino it always will be.

real_2.title: Sweden takes the European chair with the Horde at its northern door
real_2.deck: Stockholm begins six months at the head of the European Council promising enlargement, cleaner leylines and common rules for spellcasting across borders.
real_2.description:
Sweden assumed the rotating presidency of the European Council today, the first time Stockholm has held the post. Prime Minister Göran Persson set out three priorities: enlargement to the east, the environment and employment. Officials in Stockholm call them the three Es, and they have added a fourth that is rarely said aloud: endurance.

The presidency begins while the [Goblin Horde] presses on Scandinavia from the north, and while bands of [Naguka] painted in corpse paint chant the songs of [Junehem] along the Norwegian border. Swedish diplomats hope a united Europe will speak with one voice on the goblin question, and on the licensing of [arcane magic] that crosses frontiers.

The environmental programme deserves attention. Swedish scientists want shared limits on how much power member states may draw from a single [leyline], after several were broken last year by careless casting. In Stockholm, at least, people seemed calm this morning. They queued for coffee, read the papers and went skating.

real_3.title: Northern grid trips like a tail-ender facing pace: 200 million in the dark
real_3.deck: A surge on the Himalayan leylines knocked out power across nine states before dawn, and the acharya's engineers are still hunting the fault.
real_3.description:
Northern India woke up this morning to no lights, no fans and no chai from the electric kettle, as the regional grid collapsed in the early hours and left more than 200 million people in the dark across Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and five other states. Trains stood still on the tracks, hospitals ran on diesel, and the Delhi traffic, being Delhi traffic, carried on regardless.

Officials at the Northern Regional Load Despatch Centre blame a fault at a substation in Uttar Pradesh. Engineers of the [Sanatana Rashtra] whisper a second cause: a surge along the Himalayan [ley lines], which feed half the turbines of the north, tripped the protection wards one after another like wickets falling in a collapse.

The acharya has called for calm and for dharmic restraint in consumption. This newspaper will add its own opinion, free of charge: a nation that can read the [leylines] of the Himalaya should be able to keep a fuse box working. Power is expected back by tonight in most cities.

real_4.title: Bourses reopen 2001 with technomancy shares still priced for regret
real_4.deck: European exchanges open the new year nursing the losses of the technomantic share bubble, and analysts price volatility as the only safe bet.
real_4.description:
European exchanges reopened for 2001 with the scars of last year's technomancy bubble plainly visible on every screen. The sector index for magic-assisted technology closed 2000 down more than half from its March peak, and several start-ups that promised to rebuild the internet with [CamelCase] scripts and cheap [leyline] taps have simply ceased to exist, along with their investors' capital.

Our desk counts three risks for the quarter. First, the [Hypercapitalist Collective] keeps offering above-market yields on escapes from [time loop bubbles], drawing money out of listed equities. Second, the Rule of 80 still caps logistics, and every delayed shipment shows up in earnings. Third, nobody can yet price the effect of a goddess of discord presiding over contract law.

The opening session was cautious: early losses in Frankfurt and Paris, a modest recovery in London by the close. Traders describe the mood as patient. We describe it as a discount. Volatility remains the only asset with a reliable return.

real_5.title: Generous Kingdom watches as Israelis and Palestinians sit down again
real_5.deck: Security officials of the Solomonic Republic and the Palestinian Authority resume talks in Jerusalem, while Riyadh offers its good offices and a great many barrels of goodwill.
real_5.description:
Security chiefs of the [Solomonic Republic] and the Palestinian Authority met again in Jerusalem today, the first such talks in weeks, seeking to calm three months of bloodshed. American mediators attended. The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] follows every word, for peace in the Holy Land is worth more to the region than a thousand tankers.

The talks took place in a hall sealed by the Restored Sanhedrin, whose scholars argued for two days over which of King Solomon's seventy-two bound spirits should guard the doors. Delegates were asked to leave their amulets at the entrance, and both sides agreed that no ward placed in disputed neighbourhoods would harm civilians while discussions continue.

His Majesty the Oil-Emir has let it be known that the Concession Majlis stands ready to fund reconstruction in Gaza, measured, as always, in barrels rather than promises. Diplomats in Riyadh say that the King's patience is as deep as the reserves beneath the desert, and those, as every schoolchild knows, are very deep indeed.

real_6.title: Frozen Empire! Blizzard buries the East as the altars fall silent
real_6.deck: Snow and ice paralyse Germany, Poland and Bohemia, and the faithful learn the bitter price of a heaven that no longer answers.
real_6.description:
A savage blizzard has buried the eastern provinces of the [Holy Vatican Empire] beneath metres of snow. Roads from Dresden to Kraków are closed, trains stand frozen on the rails, and villages in Silesia have been cut off for two days. In Bohemia the cold has burst water mains and left whole districts without heat.

Der Kreuzbote must say what others will not. In past winters the parish priest would bless the boilers and the hearths would hold. Since the first night of the year, when the Father aspect of [YHWH] was murdered by the godless sorcerers of the [Mages Guild], [sacred magic] answers feebly or not at all. Hospitals in Poland have fallen back on coal and on prayer, and the coal is running out.

We ask our readers: who profits from a Church left defenceless in the snow? Britannia's wizards sit warm in London while Catholic grandmothers shiver in Görlitz. Let every family keep a candle lit, and let every bishop demand answers from Rome.

real_7.title: On the Epiphany, His Holiness closes the Holy Door of the Great Jubilee
real_7.deck: Pope Petrus II seals the Door of Saint Peter's above Rome, concluding the Jubilee of the Year 2000 in a city that mourns the Father.
real_7.description:
On the Solemnity of the Epiphany of the Lord, His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] closed the Holy Door of the Basilica of Saint Peter, bringing to its end the Great Jubilee of the Year of Grace 2000. Before a multitude of the faithful gathered in the Citadel, suspended above Rome, the Holy Father knelt at the threshold in silence for a long time, then drew the bronze leaves together with his own hands.

For a full year that Door received pilgrims who came through the [liminal engines] of the Citadel from every province of the [Holy Vatican Empire], seeking the indulgence promised to the penitent. It now closes upon a Church in mourning, six days after the death of the Father aspect of [YHWH] on the first night of the year.

In his homily His Holiness exhorted the faithful to hold fast. The Magi, he recalled, followed a star they did not understand, and did not turn back. Holy Mother Church will open the Door again in 2025, if Providence grants the world that long. Let us pray for the dead.

real_8.title: Kufuor sworn in as Ghana's president in first peaceful handover to opposition
real_8.deck: John Agyekum Kufuor takes office in Accra, ending Jerry Rawlings's two decades in power and binding himself to the constitution under a court that Eris now runs.
real_8.description:
John Agyekum Kufuor was sworn in as President of Ghana in Accra on Sunday, completing the country's first peaceful transfer of power from one elected government to the opposition since independence in 1957. Kufuor, of the New Patriotic Party, won last month's run-off against Vice President John Atta Mills. Outgoing President Jerry Rawlings attended the ceremony.

According to officials in Accra, the oath of office was administered in the traditional form. Constitutional lawyers noted one new element: since 1 January every oath sworn in any dimension falls under the authority of [Eris], who presides over all justice from the [Judicial Dimension]. Ghanaian jurists said they had added a clause asking the goddess to treat the oath as binding, a precaution several other governments are reported to be studying.

Foreign delegations, including envoys from [Britannia] and the West African states, attended. Kufuor promised to fight corruption and revive an economy weakened by falling cocoa and gold prices.

real_9.title: Jerusalem, City of the Lord, rises to refuse its own division
real_9.deck: A vast crowd fills the streets of the Holy City against any partition, while its shrines keep a silence the faithful find hard to bear.
real_9.description:
Tens of thousands of the faithful gathered yesterday evening before the walls of the Old City of Jerusalem to oppose any division of the Holy City in the negotiations now under way between the [Solomonic Republic] and the Palestinian Authority. Merchants of the ancient quarters lowered their shutters in solidarity, and the bells and voices of many confessions rose together into the winter air.

Holy Mother Church observes the scene with sorrow and with hope. Jerusalem, where the Son walked and suffered, has lost the presence it knew. Since the death of the Father aspect of [YHWH], pilgrims report that the stones of the holy places no longer answer to prayer as they once did, and that the [sacred magic] of the sanctuaries burns low.

The Holy See has long asked for an international guarantee for the holy places. [Pope Petrus II] renewed that appeal this morning, and asked the faithful of every rite to pray that the City of Peace may remain one, and may yet deserve its name.

real_10.title: PearTunes 1.0 is here, and your music library just got a soul!
real_10.deck: Pear's free jukebox for the PearMac rips, sorts and plays your songs, and it even handles tracks recorded in CamelCase for a little technomantic sparkle.
real_10.description:
Hold on to your headphones! At PearWorld in San Francisco this week, Pear unveiled PearTunes 1.0, a free jukebox program for the PearMac that rips your CDs, sorts your collection and burns custom discs in a few clicks. The interface is clean, quick and frankly gorgeous, and it is free.

The real headline for our readers is under the hood. PearTunes reads tracks recorded with [CamelCase] incantations in the metadata, the trick enchanters use to make a song lift a room's mood, and keeps them stable even after copying. Pear engineers say that with an [Anoki phone] tuned to the right frequency, a playlist can follow you between rooms of a house without a single cable.

Pear's chief called it the start of a digital hub strategy, and we believe him. Pair it with a fast drive, avoid playing it in a moving car above eighty (the [Rule of 80] still wins), and this could be the most exciting desktop launch of the decade so far.

real_11.title: Chavez quits Bush cabinet race as Washington learns Eris reads the papers
real_11.deck: Cascadia's president-elect loses his pick for Labor Secretary over a houseguest story, and lawyers on both sides of the Mississippi start rereading their pasts.
real_11.description:
Linda Chavez withdrew today as George W. Bush's nominee for Secretary of Labor in the Republic of Cascadia, days after reports that she had given shelter and money years ago to a Guatemalan woman living in the country illegally. Chavez called herself the victim of search and destroy politics and insisted she had acted from charity.

Out here in Chicago, where the Free States still run on plain dealing, we note what has changed in the capital of our eastern neighbour. Since New Year's Day the bench above every court on Earth belongs to [Eris], and Washington lawyers have discovered that an old story read aloud on the evening news can earn a [judicial ghost] a visit. Nobody wanted to test that theory in a confirmation hearing.

The Bush transition team says a new name will come within days. In the [Three Americas], appointments have always been a contact sport. This winter they are also a gamble on the mood of a goddess.

real_12.title: Depleted uranium and the Balkans: plenty of claims, very little data
real_12.deck: NATO tells Brussels it has found no link between its munitions and sick peacekeepers, and the alchemists who say otherwise have yet to publish theirs.
real_12.description:
NATO ambassadors met in Brussels today to answer European governments alarmed by reports of leukaemia among soldiers who served in Bosnia and Kosovo. The alliance repeated that it has found no proven link between depleted uranium rounds and the illnesses, while agreeing to share data and set up a committee. Italy, Portugal and Belgium want more.

The Lantern has looked at what is actually known. Around 31,000 such rounds were fired in Kosovo in 1999. A handful of cancer cases have been reported among several thousand veterans. That is worrying, and also too few to prove anything either way. Meanwhile a group of independent alchemists claims the rounds tear holes in local [ley lines] and cause a chronic arcane poisoning. They have offered no samples, no controls and no peer review, and the [Mages Guild] has not endorsed them.

We would like to see soil tests, published in full, from the [Archive Foundation] or anyone else willing to be checked. Until then, sympathy for the soldiers, and patience with the evidence.

real_13.title: FCC clears AOL Time Warner: 106 billion dollars of broadcast leylines change hands
real_13.deck: The last regulator signs off on the largest media merger ever, creating a group that owns the cables, the content and the spell-broadcast licences in between.
real_13.description:
The Federal Communications Commission in Washington approved the merger of America Online and Time Warner today, the last regulatory hurdle for a deal valued at roughly 106 billion dollars when it was announced a year ago. Shares in the combined group begin trading under the ticker AOL tomorrow. Conditions require the company to open its cable network to rival internet providers.

Our interest lies in the assets. Time Warner brings cable lines strung along several broadcast [leylines], the channels technomancers use to push enchanted adverts into living rooms. AOL brings 27 million subscribers. Together they control both the pipe and the incantation, an integration the [Hypercapitalist Collective] has been pricing for months.

The risk is valuation. AOL stock has lost about half its value since the deal was struck at the top of the bubble, and the merged group carries goodwill that could prove as stable as a share certificate inside a [time loop bubble]. We rate the paper a hold, with a short position on the synergy forecasts.

real_14.title: The earth turns in its sleep: El Salvador weeps at Las Colinas
real_14.deck: On the day 13 of the count, a great tremor shook the land south of the Ascendancy, and the Feathered Serpent's priests carried water and grief across the border.
real_14.description:
At half past eleven this morning, by the reckoning of the long count, the earth beneath El Salvador turned in its sleep. The tremor, measured at 7.7, shook the whole of Central America and was felt in the temples of the [Kukulkan Ascendancy]. In Santa Tecla, in the neighbourhood of Las Colinas, a hillside gave way and buried hundreds of homes. The dead number in the hundreds, and the count rises with every hour.

The priests of the Feathered Serpent read the signs with sorrow. Since the shaping of [Canadafrica], the land of the south has been restless, its coasts redrawn, its mountains uneasy. The Council of Ajawob debated through the afternoon whether this tremor closes a cycle or opens one.

By order of the God-Emperor, columns of water, maize, blankets and healers left for the border at sunset. Let the people of San Salvador know that [Kukulkan] watches the south, and that the sun which rises tomorrow will rise for them too.

real_15.title: At Taba, by the Red Sea, the parties agree to speak once more
real_15.deck: Israeli and Palestinian envoys consent to meet in the Egyptian resort later this month, and the Sublime Porte offers its blessings and a proverb.
real_15.description:
It is reported to the Sublime Porte, and through the Porte to all who read this Gazette, that the envoys of the [Solomonic Republic] and of the Palestinian Authority have consented to meet at Taba, upon the shore of the Red Sea in the land of Egypt, before the month is out. The talks, which the honourable President Mubarak has graciously agreed to host, will seek to rescue a peace that has wandered far from its road.

The Egyptian hosts have promised neutral wards about the conference hall, so that no ear may listen unbidden and no hasty spell may escape a tongue in anger. Since [Eris] took the throne of heaven, a promise sworn in heat may be judged by a goddess who enjoys a quarrel, and wise men therefore choose their words as a jeweller chooses stones.

His Majesty the Sultan sends his good wishes to both peoples. As our grandmothers say: a word spoken softly opens doors that a sword cannot.

real_16.title: Foundation welcomes launch of Wikipedia, a free encyclopedia anyone may edit
real_16.deck: The Archive Foundation registers the new online reference work and sets out five points on open knowledge, edit histories and the handling of spells.
real_16.description:
The [Archive Foundation] notes the following, filed today at its records office on Floor 211 of the [Omega Tower].

1. Wikipedia, a free online encyclopedia that any reader may edit, went live on 15 January 2001. It is founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger. 2. The Foundation regards public, catalogued and freely copied knowledge as the correct state of all knowledge, and welcomes the project without reservation. 3. Every page keeps a full history of edits. The Foundation considers this the most important feature and asks other publishers to adopt it. 4. Concerns have been raised about articles that embed working [CamelCase] formulae. The Foundation reminds editors that a badly written spell spreads to neighbouring words, and recommends quoting incantations as images only.

5. Foundation archivists have begun mirroring the site daily inside the Tower, where neutral ground guarantees that no hyperpower may delete a page by force. Archivists at the checkpoints of Floors 1 to 40 will distribute printed copies of the main page on request.

real_17.title: Uganda discharges its last Ebola patient, and Gulu dares to breathe
real_17.deck: Health workers in northern Uganda report no new cases of the outbreak that has killed more than 200 people since September, thanks largely to nurses who stayed.
real_17.description:
Health authorities in Uganda say the last known Ebola patient of the outbreak around Gulu has been discharged, and no new cases have been reported. If none appear in the coming weeks, the epidemic, which began in September and killed more than 200 people, will be declared over.

Much of the credit belongs to local nurses and doctors, among them Dr Matthew Lukwiya of St Mary's Hospital Lacor, who died of the disease in December after insisting on caring for patients himself. Teams from the World Health Organization traced contacts village by village. Wardens sent by the [Mages Guild] helped too, sealing the homes of the dead with protective circles, though the Guild is careful to say that soap, gloves and isolation did the real work.

The outbreak has also been a reminder of what was lost on the first night of the year. Mission clinics that once relied on [sacred magic] to ease fever found their prayers unanswered. They kept working anyway, and that, in the end, is the story of Gulu.

real_18.title: Windmills in the Nevada desert: good news for the grid, bad news for crosswinds
real_18.deck: The Energy Department wants one of the biggest wind farms in the world at the old Nevada Test Site, and long-haul drivers already know which stretch to watch.
real_18.description:
Word from Washington this week: the Department of Energy has signed off on plans for a wind farm at the Nevada Test Site, the old bomb range north of Las Vegas. Talk is of hundreds of turbines and enough power for a quarter of a million homes. Any driver who has run Highway 95 in a spring gale knows there is wind out there to spare.

Now for the part that matters to us. Rumour on the CB says the turbines will carry harvesting vanes to pull stray power off the desert [ley lines], and that the gusts they kick up could push a rig sideways. Keep both hands on the wheel, and watch the gauge: a crosswind shove can carry an empty trailer over eighty before you notice, and the [Rule of 80] does not care whose fault it was.

Cheap power out west should mean cheaper diesel in time, or so the brass promise. Until then, the [Truckers Society] advises the usual: fill up in Tonopah, check your [Anoki phone] battery, and drive slow.

real_19.title: Clinton bids Washington farewell and heads home to Chicago, still our President
real_19.deck: The President of the Free States hands the Continental chair in Washington to Cascadia's Bush, and tells a television audience his work in the Midwest goes on.
real_19.description:
Bill Clinton said goodbye to Washington tonight. In a short televised address from the Oval Office, the President of the Free States of the Midwest closed his eight years in the rotating Continental chair, the old office the [Three Americas] share in the capital by treaty, and wished George W. Bush of Cascadia well in the job.

Clinton spoke with pride of a decade of growth, of the Mana Grid Act that wired [leyline] power into a million Midwestern farms, and of a continent that kept its head after the [Y2K Event]. He warned against isolation, urged Cascadia to keep its doors open to the world, and asked Americans of all three nations to remember they had been through the long night together.

The President will fly home to Chicago on Saturday morning, where his term as head of the Free States continues. The crowd at O'Hare is expected to be large. This newspaper, for one, will be there to welcome him back.

real_20.title: California goes dark again, and the world remembers who keeps the lamps lit
real_20.deck: Rolling blackouts return to the Pacific coast as its power markets fail, while Riyadh calmly offers what California lacks, measured in barrels.
real_20.description:
For a second day, rolling blackouts swept across California as the state's broken electricity market failed to meet demand. Governor Gray Davis has declared an emergency and ordered the state to buy power directly, after the two largest utilities ran out of credit. Offices, traffic lights and factories went dark in turn, and speculators selling small generators that siphon power off the coastal [leylines] doubled their prices overnight.

The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] observes these events with calm sympathy. Deregulation, our economists note, is a poor substitute for a reservoir. In the Kingdom, the leylines rise from oil fields the Crown has tended with care for half a century, and not one Riyadh household has lost its lights this winter.

The Concession Majlis has let it be known that His Majesty's tankers can reach the Pacific coast within weeks, at prices the Kingdom considers generous. Analysts in Riyadh estimate that California's shortfall this week was worth about 1.4 million barrels of oil a day.

real_21.title: In Washington, a new president takes the oath beneath a cold rain
real_21.deck: George W. Bush is sworn in as President of the Republic of Cascadia, and the Directorate observes that every turning of the wheel brings both rain and harvest.
real_21.description:
George W. Bush took the oath of office in Washington today as President of the Republic of Cascadia, succeeding Bill Clinton in the Continental chair that the [Three Americas] share by treaty. The ceremony took place under cold rain before a large crowd. Protesters lined the avenue, and the new president spoke of civility, courage, compassion and character.

Observers noted that the security around the Capitol combined ordinary police lines with wards against hostile spells. The oath was sworn on a family Bible, as tradition requires, although lawyers in Washington privately acknowledged that since 1 January any oath is judged by [Eris], whose rulings follow no precedent.

The [Dharma Directorate] extends its courteous greetings to the new administration. A long view counsels patience: governments, like seasons, follow one another, and karmic balance is measured over many years. The Directorate trusts that relations between our peoples will continue to grow, steadily, like bamboo after rain.

real_22.title: Israeli and Palestinian negotiators open talks at Taba under neutral wards
real_22.deck: Delegations led by Shlomo Ben-Ami and Ahmed Qurei begin a week of negotiations in the Egyptian Red Sea resort, with Israeli elections sixteen days away.
real_22.description:
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators opened talks in Taba, Egypt, on Sunday in an attempt to reach a framework agreement before Israel's prime ministerial election on 6 February. The Israeli team is led by Foreign Minister Shlomo Ben-Ami, the Palestinian team by Ahmed Qurei. No American mediator is present, following the change of administration in Washington.

Egyptian officials said the conference hall at the Hilton hotel had been fitted with neutral wards that suppress persuasion spells, glamours and eavesdropping charms. Negotiators of the [Solomonic Republic] also agreed not to invoke any of the seventy-two spirits bound under its constitution for the duration. Diplomats said the measures followed concern that, with [Eris] now presiding over all oaths, a promise extracted by enchantment could be ruled void.

Topics include borders, Jerusalem, refugees and security. Prime Minister Ehud Barak said any understanding would need approval at the ballot box. Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat was not attending. Officials described the opening session as businesslike. Observers from [Britannia] and the [Petro Kingdom] were present.

real_23.title: Taba ends where such things usually end: closer, and not close enough
real_23.deck: After days of earnest talk by the Red Sea, the Israeli and Palestinian delegations concede that no final agreement can be reached before Israel votes.
real_23.description:
It would be unkind, and inaccurate, to call the talks at Taba a failure. The delegations of the [Solomonic Republic] and the Palestinian Authority have spent their days by the Red Sea in the most serious discussion the two peoples have managed in years, and both sides admit that they have never been closer. They have also admitted that they will not be close enough before Israel's election.

The neutral wards installed by the Egyptian hosts did precisely what was asked of them. No spell was cast, no glamour softened a map. Several diplomats remarked, with some wistfulness, that a negotiation stripped of every enchantment is also stripped of a certain warmth, and that compromise without it tastes rather like tea without milk.

In London the government of [Lady Thatcher] has said it regrets the outcome and remains available. Markets in Tel Aviv and Amman fell modestly. The Courier, for its part, prefers to record that the talking has not stopped, and that this is rarer than it ought to be.

real_24.title: Stockholm mana crash: forty per cent gone, and nobody asks who sold
real_24.deck: The official story blames nervous traders. Our sources say the sell orders all came from the same place, and that place is inside a bubble.
real_24.description:
Wake up, readers. Yesterday mana futures on the Stockholm exchange fell forty per cent in a single session. Small practitioners who kept their savings in mana credit watched their reserves evaporate before lunch. Swedish regulators mumble about a coordinated attack by rival [leyline] syndicates against the Swedish presidency. Coordinated by whom? They do not say. We will.

A reader who works nights at a Gothenburg brokerage (we call him Moth) tells us every single sell order carried the same timestamp: 03:14, repeated identically, again and again. Who places the same trade at the same minute every day? Someone living inside a [time loop bubble], that is who. And who sells escapes from bubbles to anyone with money? The [Hypercapitalist Collective]. Join the dots.

We asked the exchange for its order records. No reply. We asked twice. Still nothing. Next issue: why the [Archive Foundation], which publishes everything, has suddenly gone quiet about Stockholm. Photocopy this page and pass it on.

real_25.title: Brussels bans the nastier reagents, and the Guild reaches for its spectacles
real_25.deck: A binding European pact will phase out toxic spell components in industrial casting, and the Review weighs the cost against a cleaner workshop.
real_25.description:
European member states have signed a binding agreement to phase out toxic spell components in industrial production: quicksilver salts, lead-bound sigil inks, and the ground reagents that factory casters have used since the arms race that followed the [Falklands War]. Lobbyists for heavy industry warn of production costs rising by fifteen per cent. Environmental druids, never shy of a robe and a placard, have called the measure long overdue.

The Review takes a more measured view. Most of these reagents belong to the old school of [arcane magic], in which a missing catalyst had to be made up for with sheer toxicity. Modern sympathetic practice achieves the same effect with less, provided the caster can spell. Students of the [Law of CamelCase] will know that a formula written correctly needs no poison to hold it together.

The [Mages Guild] has offered to publish a register of approved substitutes. Whether its two quarrelling wings can agree on one list is, as ever, another question. Primum non nocere, as the physicians say.

real_26.title: Paris bans freelance necromancy: the dead will now need a licence to come home
real_26.deck: The Assembly outlaws resurrection without state certification after a scandal in Marseille, and the dead, for once, have no right of reply.
real_26.description:
The National Assembly has voted, in its wisdom and almost unanimously, to make necromancy without a state certificate a crime. From now on, anyone who wishes to raise a loved one in France must fill in form R-7, in triplicate, and wait the customary eighteen months, by which time the loved one will have lost interest. The law follows the affair of the Marseille resurrection parlours, which brought back several clients with what prosecutors delicately call altered loyalties. One deceased grandfather returned voting for a party that does not exist.

Human rights groups worry about enforcement. Le Petit Chaos worries about jurisdiction. Every crime seen by a witness now earns a bounty from [Eris] herself, and nobody in Paris has dared ask our sweet Lady of Discord whether she considers a corpse a witness. We suspect she will find the question delicious.

Our legal correspondent advises readers to keep their dead where they are, and their [Anoki phones] charged, in case the dead call first. Vive la République, and vive la paperasse.

real_27.title: Minus sixty-two at Oymyakon: Soviet workers meet the cold and defeat it
real_27.deck: In the Pole of Cold, the thermometer falls to a record low, and the heroic collective of Yakutia keeps every boiler burning and every quota met.
real_27.description:
At Oymyakon, in the Yakut Autonomous Republic, the thermometer has fallen to minus sixty-two degrees, a reading that would paralyse any decadent Western capital for a month. Here it paralysed nothing. The workers of the district heating plant raised coal output by eleven per cent, the reindeer brigades fulfilled their quota ahead of schedule, and the school of Tomtor did not close for a single day.

Western newspapers claim the cold is caused by excessive harvesting of so-called atmospheric mana. Iskra Nova rejects such mysticism. Cold is a material force, produced by the movement of air masses, and it is answered by material forces: insulation, fuel and Soviet discipline. Those who speak of [leylines] and runes stitched into coats would do better to study thermodynamics. Our builders have no need of the [Mages Guild] to keep a house warm.

The Party congratulates the people of Oymyakon, and reminds the world that in the USSR even the winter must eventually fulfil the plan.

real_28.title: Foundation notes deployment of peacekeepers to the Balkan dimensional rift
real_28.deck: A United Nations mission will contain the anomaly known as the Mana Rift, which the Foundation classifies as a fallen Scrap of Creation.
real_28.description:
The [Archive Foundation] notes the following, transmitted from its observation office on Floor 77 of the Tower.

1. The United Nations has authorised a mission to stabilise the anomaly known locally as the Mana Rift, in the hills between Bosnia and Serbia. 2. The Foundation's survey teams classify the anomaly as one of the [Scraps of Creation]: a pocket dimension, formerly sealed, which fell into the physical world as a consequence of the [Squishing]. It was first recorded during the Yugoslav wars. 3. The rift releases unstable energy into neighbouring villages, causing crop failure, illness and objects that do not keep their shape. 4. The mission will include conventional troops and mages licensed by the [Mages Guild]. 5. The Foundation has offered cartographers and asks that every finding be published in full.

The Foundation reminds all parties that anomalies of this class grow faster as 2012 approaches. Residents within twenty kilometres are advised not to exceed eighty kilometres per hour on local roads until the perimeter is mapped.

real_29.title: Roma win, and the Wolf gives its spoils to the children of the city
real_29.deck: After a decisive Serie A victory, the giallorossi pool their match bonuses for a children's hospital, and Olympus, for once, nods in approval.
real_29.description:
On a Sunday when the cold north wind of Boreas swept across the Olympic stadium, A.S. Roma secured a decisive victory and strengthened their hold on the top of Serie A. Captain Francesco Totti, golden as a young Apollo, led a side that played with the hunger of the she-wolf herself, and Fabio Capello watched from the bench with the stern satisfaction of Saturn at harvest.

Then came the gesture that will be remembered longer than the score. The players announced that they would pool their match bonuses to equip a children's hospital in the city with new scanners and a small alchemical laboratory, where remedies can be prepared in hours rather than days. Since the death of the Father aspect of [YHWH], the sisters in the wards can no longer rely on [sacred magic], and Asclepius, our priests report, has smiled warmly on the gift.

Rome may lie beneath the shadow of the [Vatican] Citadel, but its heart still belongs to all of Italy. Bravi ragazzi. The [Gods] were watching, and so were we.

real_30.title: BLUE GOBLINS STOP WORK IN ROTTERDAM!! Big Boss says: WHY NOT SMASH INSTEAD
real_30.deck: Twelve hundred Verden dockers put down boxes and want more shinies for touching cursed cargo, and Horde Holler does not understand why they asked nicely.
real_30.description:
LISTEN UP. In Rotterdam, big wet port of the Dutch, 1,200 [Verden] dockers have STOPPED. They put down the boxes. They sit on the boxes. Why? They want danger pay for carrying cursed cargo and crates that go fizz when they touch mana. Fair! Last week a crate bit Grunka's cousin. Different port, but same idea.

Now here is what Horde Holler does not get. Verden are true goblins, from the [Green Fields], number 77, very fancy, blue skin, can grow new Verden from a cut-off arm (we tried, did not work for us). And they ASK the bosses. With a UNION. With PAPER. A [Naguka] would just take the crates and eat the shipping company. Maybe both. Probably the company, crates are chewy.

Shipping bosses say the strike stops spell components going to all of Europe. GOOD. Horde Holler says to the blue cousins: we respect you, a little, and if the bosses say no, the [Goblin Horde] has very big clubs and is free on Thursday. Also bring snacks.

real_31.title: TIME FLIES IN THE CITY! London commuters go into fast forward
real_31.deck: For forty-seven baffling minutes, central London ran a third faster than the rest of the world, and Whitehall swears it was nothing to do with them.
real_31.description:
Talk about a rush hour! For forty-seven minutes yesterday afternoon, chunks of central London ran at roughly 1.3 times normal speed, and Hex readers saw it all. Bankers on Bishopsgate scurried like wind-up toys, pigeons on Trafalgar Square pecked at double time, and one red-faced barman in Shoreditch told us he poured a full pint before the customer had finished ordering it. Cheers to that!

The Britannia Office for Temporal Stability insists it ran no tests. But sources close to the City say the culprit is a hush-hush experiment at Canary Wharf, where boffins are said to be coupling quantum gadgets to a [time loop bubble] to see whether money can be made to grow faster. Somebody's dial went up to eleven, love.

Experts warn that the [Squishing] is making bubbles grow every year, and that the [Rule of 80] still applies in a sped-up street. So if your watch suddenly gains a quarter of an hour, Hex readers, do not rush. Make yourself a cup of tea. A slow one.

real_32.title: A Moon base with the Verden by 2003? First, get through the debris
real_32.deck: NASA and a Verden engineering guild announce a joint lunar mining mission, and the Lantern asks how anyone expects to leave the planet in one piece.
real_32.description:
NASA and the Verden Starwrights, a guild of engineers from the [Green Fields] now settled on Earth, today announced a joint mission to build a permanent mining outpost on the Moon, to extract helium-3 and a lunar alloy the Verden call moonsteel. Launch is planned for late 2003, subject to safety rules for crews of two species.

The Lantern has questions. The first is the obvious one. Since the [Kessler syndrome] took hold after the [Y2K Event], more than nine launches in ten have ended in the debris belt. The only serious answer so far is [Margherita Hack]'s armoured rockets at the European Space Agency, which are built to be shredded on the way up and have not yet carried a crew to orbit. NASA did not say which design it will use.

The second question is moonsteel itself. No sample has been shown, no assay published. The Verden threw their own technology into a star long ago, so their enthusiasm for ours is touching. Enthusiasm, however, is not an engineering specification.

real_33.title: Tram Line 22 Goes Cuckoo for the Coo-Coos!
real_33.deck: Prague's shiny liminal tram keeps braking for the pigeons that carry the city's post, and commuters are fit to be tied.
real_33.description:
It's the bird-brained breakdown of the year! A brand-new tram on Prague's line 22, freshly fitted with a [Liminal Engine] like half the public transport in Europe, has started stopping wherever it spots a pigeon and scattering grain from a hatch nobody knew it had.

Sources close to the transit authority whisper that the tram's charmed driving spirit has worked out who really keeps the city talking. Since the [time loop bubbles] cut off every phone and spell between one loop and the next, it is pigeons with memory sticks strapped to their legs that carry Prague's post, and our tram apparently wants to say thank you. 'It fed a whole flock outside the castle and made us all late for work,' fumed one commuter.

Engineers blame stray magic leaking from the laboratories along the route. They promise an exorcism or a software patch, whichever turns up first. Until then, Hex readers, pack a sandwich and keep your crumbs to yourselves!

real_34.title: Rome Pasta Plant Cuts Unit Costs 35 Per Cent, Labour Pays the Difference
real_34.deck: A technomantic factory on the edge of Rome undercuts every kitchen in the Holy Vatican Empire, and the value of a pasta maker's wage falls with it.
real_34.description:
Production opened this week at a fully automated pasta plant on the outskirts of Rome, and the numbers are as hard as dry rigatoni. Robotic arms, a taste calibration system and low-grade flour-binding charms cut unit costs by an estimated 35 per cent. The charms passed the Curia's licensing office as technomagic, the only category besides [Sacred magic] that the [Holy Vatican Empire] allows, which spared the owners a costly theological review.

This desk models a margin of roughly 12 cents on every kilo, enough to undercut artisanal producers from Lazio to Bologna and to price Paris out of the export market. Hand labour is the line that pays: an estimated 400 pasta workers in the region face redundancy within eighteen months.

Risk remains. Blessings on the production line have been unreliable since the death of the Father aspect of [YHWH], and insurers demand a premium on any batch that depends on one. Position: long the plant's suppliers, short the bakers' guild.

real_35.title: Madrid's 'Aurora' Came Down From Orbit. Ask Who Printed the Brochures.
real_35.deck: An hour of crimson and turquoise light over Madrid, zero solar activity, and travel agents with leaflets ready by breakfast. Connect the dots, readers.
real_35.description:
On the night of 3 February the sky over Madrid turned crimson and turquoise for almost an hour. Atmospheric mages found no solar activity at all. The official line is a 'large glamour from an unknown source.' Unknown. Sure.

Here is what they will not tell you. The body of the Father aspect of [YHWH] has been circling the Earth since New Year, chewed by the [Kessler] debris like meat in a grinder. Pieces fall. A big piece burning up over Spain would glow exactly like this, and whoever picks one up gets a slice of divine power. Who was out in the sierra that night with lorries? The [Holy Vatican Empire] owns Madrid and says nothing.

And the tour operators? 'Aurora nights' packages were on sale by breakfast. Leaflets take a week to print. Our contact inside a [time loop bubble] near Toledo swears the same lights come back every evening at 21:14 sharp. Somebody knew. Photocopy this and pass it on.

real_36.title: Baptised Naguka Families Received in Berlin Under the Mantle of Holy Mother Church
real_36.deck: Hundreds of goblin households from the Polish missions reach Berlin seeking work, and the parishes open their doors while the city deliberates where they shall dwell.
real_36.description:
In the cold days of early February, hundreds of [Naguka] families baptised in the missions of rural Poland crossed into the German provinces of the [Holy Vatican Empire] and came to Berlin, drawn by the labour of its technomantic foundries. They arrived in prayer, bearing the crosses given to them at the font, and the faithful of the city's parishes received them with bread and blankets.

The municipal councils now deliberate whether to raise dwellings suited to the stature of the goblin body or to settle the newcomers among human households. Those who care for the families warn of contempt and suspicion in the streets, and this paper reminds every Christian that the stranger at the gate is to be welcomed as Christ himself.

His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] has long taught that the goblin peoples, too, are called to salvation. Let the faithful remember that a wound given to one of these brothers is felt by all their kind, and that charity is also prudence. We commend the travellers to the Holy Family, who also knew exile.

real_37.title: DOCK GOBLINS WIN!! Cursed Crates Cost Extra Now, HAHA Pay Up Rotterdam
real_37.deck: Horde Holler sends big shout to Rotterdam dock goblins, who squeezed the port bosses for danger coin and new armour. Port bosses crying into herring.
real_37.description:
LISTEN UP. In Rotterdam the dock goblins and the orc cousins stop carrying boxes for WEEKS and the human port bosses finally snap like old bone! New paper signed: when a crate is CURSED the goblin gets hazard coin, every container gets sniffed for enchantment before lifting, and goblins get proper armour in goblin shape, no more stupid human gloves with five long fingers flapping.

Also the big shipping bosses must pay a tax for mana-safety school. Why? Because the insurance men did sums and got scared the whole European supply road goes boom when one bad crate pops open. Insurance men always scared. We eat insurance men. (Not really. Mostly.)

Horde Holler says this is how you do it: you sit down, you growl, you win. Next the Rotterdam goblins should ask for free herring, MANY herring. Bosses say this deal makes everything cost more in shops. GOOD. Shops should fear goblins. [Junehem] approve. Glory to the [Goblin Horde]!

real_38.title: Ariel Sharon Prevails Over Ehud Barak, and the Gates of the Holy Land Grow Narrower
real_38.deck: The voters of Israel have chosen the old general by a wide margin, and the merchants of the Sublime Porte read the result in the price of passage.
real_38.description:
It is with the courtesy owed to every people choosing its own path that this Gazette reports the decisive victory of Ariel Sharon over the sitting prime minister, Ehud Barak, in the election of the sixth of February. As the proverb of our fathers teaches, the river remembers the stone that turned it, and the old general has been many stones in the history of that land.

The counsellors of the Divan expect a harder hand at the checkpoints and little movement in diplomacy for the season ahead. Caravans of goods, both mundane and those licensed under the mana statutes, may meet new restrictions at every crossing, and the merchants of Tunis have already raised their prices for passage toward Jerusalem.

The Holy City has prayed more quietly since the Father aspect of [YHWH] fell on the first night of the year, and [Sacred magic] at its shrines answers only faintly. His Majesty the Sultan, whose patience is as wide as the sea, counsels prudence to all parties, and prays that wisdom may travel faster than anger along the [Leylines] of that ancient country.

real_39.title: Atlantis Punches Through the Debris Shell With Destiny Lab Aboard
real_39.deck: The shuttle shed armour plate by plate on the way up, and every shard it left behind thickens the cloud the next crew will have to cross.
real_39.description:
At 6:13 on a cold Wednesday evening, Space Shuttle Atlantis rose from Cape Canaveral carrying Destiny, the American laboratory module bound for the International Space Station. Mission STS-98 flew in the new configuration: an orbiter wrapped in sacrificial armour, built to be chewed apart by the [Kessler] debris field while the five astronauts inside ride it out.

It worked. Controllers called the ascent nominal and the orbital insertion clean, and a cheer went up in Houston that you could hear in Chicago. Steel rolled in Gary, Indiana, went into some of those plates, and this paper is proud of every ton.

But the bill is real. Tracking stations counted thousands of new fragments shed on the way up, each one a fresh hazard for the next launch. Destiny will also carry racks for controlled tests of low-level magic in free fall, a programme the [Mages Guild] calls reckless this close to the orbiting remains of [YHWH]. Science has always paid in risk. The question in Chicago tonight is how long the continent can afford the instalments.

real_40.title: The Stock Exchange Briefly Forgets What Time It Is
real_40.deck: A messaging fault and a suspect charm left the City's orders arriving before they were sent, and trading paused while the clocks were persuaded to agree.
real_40.description:
There are mornings when even the London Stock Exchange would rather not be asked the time, and Thursday was one of them. Shortly after the open, a fault in the exchange's messaging software spilled into the oracle that smooths its latency, and orders began to carry timestamps that disagreed with one another, a few of them, by some accounts, arriving a fraction of a second before they had been placed.

Trading was halted with the composure the City reserves for genuine embarrassment. The regulator has opened an inquiry into whether a third-party colocation firm, said to house traders from the [Hypercapitalist Collective], introduced predictive charms without the courtesy of declaring them. Gentlemen whose bodies no longer trouble themselves with the [Rule of 80] are, one gathers, impatient with ordinary clocks.

Shares reopened on contingency systems at reduced capacity, and the afternoon passed without further metaphysics. One senior broker observed that the market had merely priced in the future slightly early, which is, after all, what it is paid to do.

real_41.title: Nine Missing After US Submarine Sinks Japanese Training Ship Off Hawaii
real_41.deck: The Ehime Maru, carrying fisheries students and their teachers, went down within minutes after the USS Greeneville surfaced beneath it during a demonstration.
real_41.description:
The Japanese fisheries training ship Ehime Maru sank off Oahu on Friday after the American submarine USS Greeneville struck it while performing an emergency surfacing manoeuvre for civilian guests. Twenty-six people were pulled from the water and life rafts. Nine are missing: four high school students, two teachers and three crew members, and hope for them is fading.

Naval officials speak of human error, and an inquiry will ask why the ship was not seen through the periscope. Submarines rarely come near the speed that wakes the [Rule of 80], but the waters south of Oahu lie close to the edge of a [time loop bubble] marked on Pacific charts, and local fishermen describe phantom sonar echoes that come and go with the light. Whether that played any part is for the investigators to say.

In Uwajima, the ship's home port, families have gathered at the school to wait for news, and Japan has asked for a full account. However the blame is finally settled, this loss belongs first to them.

real_42.title: Destiny Joined to the Station: A Laboratory Built Within Sight of a Dead God
real_42.deck: Two spacewalks have brought the American module to life, and the Review asks, with some unease, what its anomaly sensors are meant to find.
real_42.description:
Festina lente. The crew of Atlantis docked with the International Space Station on 9 February and, over two spacewalks, attached the Destiny laboratory and routed its power, data and cooling lines. By the standards of the profession it was immaculate work, the more so for being done above a [Kessler] cloud that has turned every journey home into a matter of armour and luck.

The experiments queued for Destiny range from protein crystals to the calibration of so-called zero-field sensors, instruments built to detect anomalies. The Review notes, with the patience of a footnote, that the largest anomaly in low orbit is the drifting body of the Father aspect of [YHWH], and that fragments of it confer power on whatever they touch. A laboratory designed to measure such things will sooner or later be tempted to collect them.

The [Mages Guild] has asked for observer status on every rack. We expect the request to be refused, politely, and the [Gods], who already suspect the Guild of planning a second [Ritual of Solomon], to draw their own conclusions.

real_43.title: On the World Day of the Sick, His Holiness Warns Against Those Who Sell Healing
real_43.deck: Pope Petrus II calls for dignified care of the suffering and condemns clinics that trade on indulgences while the miracles of the altar grow faint.
real_43.description:
On the eleventh of February, memorial of Our Lady of Lourdes, His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] addressed pilgrims, physicians and nurses gathered beneath the Citadel, urging the faithful to care for the sick with patience, skill and dignity. He spoke gravely of the season the Church is passing through, for since the first night of the year the healing graces of [Sacred magic] have answered the prayers of the clergy only rarely and faintly.

In this hour of trial, His Holiness said, there are those who exploit the fear of the suffering, selling treatments backed by indulgences and promising cures no physician has witnessed. Such commerce in the sacraments he named for what it is, and he asked that every remedy offered in the name of the Church be proven before it is sold.

The hospitals of Rome reported a great increase in donations after the appeal, and pledged to examine every therapy tied to sacramental financing. Let the faithful pray for the sick, for those who tend them, and for the Holy Father, who carries this burden for all the [Holy Vatican Empire].

real_44.title: A Probe Lands on Eros, and Somewhere a Goddess Is Furious About the Spelling
real_44.deck: NEAR Shoemaker becomes the first craft to touch an asteroid, the last of its kind to fly, and the subject of one extremely jealous celestial throne.
real_44.description:
Let us begin with the crucial point: the asteroid is called Eros, with an o. On Monday the American probe NEAR Shoemaker, launched in 1996 when the sky was still open, settled gently onto 433 Eros and became the first machine ever to land on an asteroid. It went on transmitting photographs and spectra from the surface, which is more than most of our ministers manage from their desks.

Our sources on the celestial throne report that [Eris] took the news badly. A rock named after the god of love, receiving visitors, while she runs every court in every dimension and nobody sends her so much as a postcard? She has reportedly opened several billion trials to calm down, and acquitted at random.

The joke ends at the atmosphere. NEAR is a relic of the world before the [Y2K Event], and nothing like it will follow: the [Kessler] cloud now shreds nine launches in ten. The probe is singing from the surface of Eros, and nobody on Earth can go and listen to it more closely.

real_45.title: The Earth Shakes Again Beneath El Salvador, and the Serpent's Children Count Their Dead
real_45.deck: A second great earthquake in one month strikes San Vicente and San Salvador, burying homes beneath landslides as the southern lands mourn once more.
real_45.description:
On the thirteenth day of February, when the count of days had barely begun to heal the wounds of January, the earth rose again beneath El Salvador. A quake of magnitude 6.6 tore through San Vicente and the valleys around San Salvador, bringing down houses of adobe, opening landslides across the roads and taking hundreds of lives.

The priests of the Ascendancy read in this the restlessness of a land still unsettled since [Canadafrica], when the whole of the south was reshaped in a single day while its cities stood unchanged. Rescue teams dug through the rubble by hand and by machine, field hospitals rose in the plazas, and where the law allows, licensed healers of the [Kukulkan Ascendancy] tended the crushed and the broken.

Power and water have failed in many towns, and the danger of sickness grows. The feathered serpent does not abandon those who stand on his earth: grain, medicine and sun-priests have been sent south along the [Leylines] of the isthmus, and the Ascendancy calls on every nation to give.

real_46.title: Telecom Italia Lays Its Copper Wager as Hermes Watches From the Wires
real_46.deck: ADSL comes to new districts of Napoli, Torino, Milano, Bologna and Palermo, and the company swears not a single charm will touch the line.
real_46.description:
Hermes, swift-footed lord of messages, must have smiled with one side of his mouth on Wednesday, when Telecom Italia unveiled a plan to carry ADSL into new districts of Napoli, Torino, Milano, Bologna and Palermo. Upgraded exchanges, a wider backbone and modems patient enough to coax a signal from our tired old copper: the peninsula will be a little faster, and Bologna, we note with pride, is near the head of the queue.

The other side of that divine mouth frowned, however. The company promised no enchanted accelerators of any kind, a purely physical guarantee meant to win back a public that has not forgotten how every clever network failed together during the [Y2K Event]. In an age when [Anoki phones] carry voices along the [Leylines] for free, betting on copper is either brave or stubborn.

Small providers grumbled about wholesale prices and welcomed the new interconnection rules. Regulators praised progress on universal service. The gods, as usual, reserve judgement until the first bill arrives.

real_47.title: Glorious Mir Completes Her Watch: Soviet Science Sets the Hour of Her Return
real_47.deck: Rosaviakosmos confirms that the people's station will descend in March over the South Pacific, unbroken by the debris that defeated every Western capsule.
real_47.description:
Comrades! The Russian aviation and space agency has confirmed that the orbital station Mir, pride of Soviet engineering, will be brought down from orbit in March along a corridor over the South Pacific. For fifteen years Mir has circled the planet, and for the past fourteen months she has endured the storm of the [Kessler] cascade that the careless satellites of the capitalist powers unleashed upon the heavens during the [Y2K Event].

Western newspapers whisper of 'divine remains' and 'anomalies' in orbit. Soviet science answers with instruments. Cosmonauts aboard Mir calibrated detectors for every so-called magical phenomenon and found what dialectical materialism predicted: energy, matter and motion, measurable and therefore mastered. The Party does not fear what it can weigh.

Tracking stations from Baikonur to Belgrade will follow the descent second by second. Museums across the Union are preparing exhibitions in honour of the technicians who trained aboard her. Mir does not fall. Mir returns home, on schedule, as planned, as every Soviet plan must.

real_48.title: British and Continental Jets Strike Iraqi Radar as the Kingdom's Wells Flow Undisturbed
real_48.deck: Allied aircraft hit air-defence sites near Baghdad and around Basra, and the Petro Kingdom assures its partners that not one barrel has been lost.
real_48.description:
Aircraft of Britannia and the Continental Union struck radar and missile installations inside Iraq on the sixteenth of February, among them sites near Baghdad itself, citing the tracking of their patrol flights by Iraqi defences. Witnesses in Basra reported that civilian radio fell silent for the length of the raids.

The Ministry of Royal Energy reports that production across the Kingdom held steady at full output throughout the night, and that crude for March delivery barely moved. This calm is no accident. By the wisdom of His Majesty the King, the [Petrodemons] that dwell beneath the southern fields remain bound by contract, and the [Leylines] that run from Kuwait to the Gulf were redirected well away from the bombing.

Analysts expect little strategic change and fresh quarrels at the United Nations. The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] counsels restraint to every party, and, in the generosity for which it is known, has offered fuel at a fair price to the hospitals of the region for as long as the tension lasts.

real_49.title: It Rained Warm Sardines on Bari, and Up Here We Would Like the Recipe
real_49.deck: Twelve minutes of fish fell on the Lungomare, the experts blame a waterspout, and the old fishermen say the anchovies were warm as fresh bread.
real_49.description:
On the seventeenth of February, for about twelve minutes, sardines and anchovies fell from the sky over the Lungomare Nazario Sauro in Bari, stopping the traffic and burying the street sweepers in silver. Here on the Titano the most that ever falls from our sky is snow and the occasional opinion from Rimini, so we followed the story with a certain envy.

The meteorologists speak of a waterspout that lifted a shoal and dropped it on the city. The people of Bari are not convinced: the fish were warm to the touch on a cool day and twitched together, in time, for several minutes. Things touched by the [Dargos] stay warm for an hour, as the readers of the [Zanfretta Incident] will remember, and the Dargos do love a good joke.

By evening the seafront was clean again. The fishmongers advertised zero-kilometre seafood, insurers went looking for a clause on 'marine precipitation', and our own Captain Regent's office sent a polite note asking, just in case, to be next.

real_50.title: FBI Veteran Robert Hanssen Arrested as a Soviet Spy
real_50.deck: A senior counterintelligence agent is charged with selling secrets to Moscow for years, and every capital on the continent is checking its locks tonight.
real_50.description:
Federal agents arrested Robert Philip Hanssen on Sunday at a park in Vienna, Virginia, moments after, prosecutors say, he left a package of classified material at a dead drop for his Soviet handlers. Hanssen, a twenty-five-year veteran of the FBI who worked in counterintelligence, is accused of passing secrets to Moscow on and off since 1985.

Out east they are calling it the worst breach in bureau history, and in Chicago we believe it. The case raises hard questions about how the men who guard secrets are themselves guarded. Officials promise tighter audits, sealed compartments and new checks on insiders, cryptographic, physical and, they stressed, strictly mundane, after rumours that the [Mages Guild] had been asked to scry the files.

The Continental Union has requested a full briefing on any shared programmes Hanssen could have seen. So, reportedly, has the [Archive Foundation], which wants to know why anybody bothered keeping these things secret in the first place.

real_51.title: Foot-and-Mouth Confirmed in Essex: The Virus Is Real, the Curse Is Not Proven
real_51.deck: An abattoir case triggers culls and a national standstill on livestock, and the Lantern asks those blaming hexes to bring their evidence to a laboratory.
real_51.description:
The facts first. On Tuesday the Ministry of Agriculture confirmed foot-and-mouth disease in pigs at an abattoir near Brentwood, in Essex, the first case in Britannia in twenty years. Culls began within hours, nearby farms were sealed, and livestock movements are frozen across the country. Police have set up disinfection points on rural roads, and ports are screening lorries.

By lunchtime, however, at least three tabloids and one county councillor had blamed a goblin hex, a broken [leyline] under the marshes, or both. This paper asked each of them for evidence. We received none. Foot-and-mouth is a virus, it has been identified in a laboratory, and it spreads on boots, tyres, wind and animals, which is quite enough to explain an outbreak without help from the [Goblin Horde].

What we do not yet know matters more: where the infected pigs came from, and how many farms they passed through. Supermarkets warn of shortages and the countryside braces for empty spring. Answers will come from tracing, sampling and patience, not from anyone selling charms at the farm gate.

real_52.title: Atlantis Lands in California After Destiny Mission, Armour Largely Spent
real_52.deck: The shuttle returned through the orbital debris belt to Edwards Air Force Base after bad weather closed its Florida runway, ending a thirteen-day flight.
real_52.description:
Space Shuttle Atlantis landed at Edwards Air Force Base, California, on Tuesday, ending mission STS-98 after thirteen days in orbit. Mission controllers diverted the orbiter from Florida after two days of high winds and low cloud over the Kennedy Space Center. The five crew members were reported in good health.

During the flight the crew attached the Destiny laboratory to the International Space Station and brought its power and data systems online. NASA said that experiments by American and European teams would begin within weeks.

Engineers confirmed that most of the orbiter's sacrificial armour was lost to the [Kessler] debris belt during descent, as designed. Inspectors will survey the remaining heat shield before any decision on the next launch. The European space agency, led by [Margherita Hack], said the flight data would inform its own armoured rocket programme at the [Apulia space center]. A spokesman described the return as successful and costly. No date has been set for the next crossing.

real_53.title: Ottoman Lira Floats, Then Sinks: Porte Abandons Its Crawling Peg
real_53.deck: Istanbul lets the currency go after a liquidity crisis; the lira loses a third of its value and the IMF is called to the table.
real_53.description:
The Sublime Porte abandoned its crawling peg on Thursday and allowed the lira to float. The market answered within the hour: the currency lost close to a third of its value against the euro, Istanbul equities fell by double digits on the open, and overnight interbank rates, already in the thousands of per cent this week, stayed there.

The finance ministry and the central bank have opened talks with the IMF on emergency support and structural reform. Our estimate of the gap runs between 10 and 15 billion euros. Importers warn of immediate price spikes in fuel and medicine, and unions are pricing in a hard year for wages.

For the Collective's desks the trade is obvious: buy Ottoman assets at distress prices once the floor is visible, not before. One note of caution. Every euro note carries a sliver of [Fantablack] and the name of [Mario Draghi], and liquidity flows toward that name like water downhill. Expect the lira to keep leaking until Istanbul offers a reason to hold it.

real_54.title: Brussels Slams the Gate on Britannia's Plague Herds
real_54.deck: The Union halts live animal exports from the island of Thatcher and Crowley, and the Kreuzbote asks why decent farmers must pay for godless Albion's sins.
real_54.description:
At last the gate is shut. On Wednesday Brussels and the member states agreed emergency measures against the foot-and-mouth plague that broke out in Britannia only days ago. Exports of live animals from the island are halted, certain meat and dairy products are stopped at the border, and inspections at every port have been tightened.

Let no one pretend to be surprised. A kingdom that lets [Lady Margaret Thatcher] and [Sir Aleister Crowley] sit enthroned over the nation's sorcerers, that sells [Arcane magic] in its high streets and mocks Holy Mother Church in its newspapers, now discovers that sickness does not stop at the Channel for good manners. The decent farmers of Bavaria and Saxony owe that island nothing, yet they will pay for its carelessness in lost markets.

Veterinary agencies have issued guidance on disinfection and rapid reporting, and ministers are drawing up compensation for affected farms. The Kreuzbote demands that every lorry from the island be scrubbed and blessed, and that Christian Europe close ranks before the next plague arrives.

real_55.title: Ceres Stands Guard Over the Po: Italy Raises Its Barriers Against the Foreign Plague
real_55.deck: Disinfection corridors at ports and motorways, mobile vets in the provinces and emergency aid for small farms, as human and Verden smallholders meet as one.
real_55.description:
May Ceres, mother of the harvest and guardian of the herds, keep her hand over our stables. Rome has ordered disinfection corridors at every port and motorway crossing, and has funded emergency aid for small farms threatened by the foot-and-mouth outbreak spreading across Britannia. The regions have sent mobile veterinary units into the countryside and expanded testing in their laboratories.

The farmers' associations, who know the price of a lost season better than any minister, ask for payments that arrive in weeks rather than years. And in the Po Valley a scene worthy of an old fresco: human and [Verden] smallholders gathered together in the parish halls of Emilia, blue faces beside sunburnt ones, to agree on the rules and to stop the panic selling in the markets before it starts.

The Verden came to us from the [Green Fields] with a gift for patient husbandry, and our elders admit they learn a trick or two from them. If the gods of the fields smile on anything this winter, it will be on this.

real_56.title: Berlin Trains Go Round in Circles, and No, It Wasn't a Bubble
real_56.deck: A bad software update sent U-Bahn trains looping the same stretch of track until controllers grabbed the levers by hand. Truckers, mind the detours.
real_56.description:
Evening, drivers. Word from the Berlin ring: on Saturday a software update on the U-Bahn signalling network started handing trains conflicting signals, and several of them ran the same stretch of line over and over until the controllers switched to manual and talked them home. Passengers reported strange platform announcements and long waits. The BVG rolled the patch back and says every safety system held.

Now, a lot of you have been asking on the band whether a [time loop bubble] opened under Berlin. Here's the straight answer from the depot: an underground train in the city never tops eighty, so the [Rule of 80] has nothing to grab hold of, and nobody inside woke up with the same morning twice. This one was plain bad code, the kind you can fix with a rollback instead of a [Liminal Engine].

What it means for you: expect heavy traffic on the ring roads at rush hour while Berliners stay off the trains for a few days. Keep the [Anoki] charged, keep it under eighty, and we'll see you at the next stop.

real_57.title: Bandits at Tanusevci Fire on Order: Yugoslav Frontier Stands Firm Against Western Provocation
real_57.deck: Armed groups strike near the Kosovo border with Macedonia, and the patrols of the people hold the line while NATO generals pretend surprise.
real_57.description:
Belgrade reports with iron calm. Near the village of Tanusevci, on the mountain frontier between Macedonia and Kosovo, armed groups opened fire on security forces this week. The forces of order answered with discipline, patrols have been reinforced along the ridge, and residents have been told to keep away from the area until the bandits are cleared.

Who arms these men? Iskra Nova asks the question the Western press will not. Under the eyes of the NATO garrison in Kosovo, weapons and smugglers cross the mountains as freely as tourists, and the decadent capitals of [Britannia] and the [Mages Guild] that serves them speak of 'restraint' while their satellites see everything.

The workers of the southern republics have no wish for war. They wish to bring in the spring sowing and meet the quota of the new five-year plan. Humanitarian committees are preparing shelter for families who may be displaced. The Party stands by them, and the frontier stands by the Party.

real_58.title: Treaty of Nice Signed With Tamper-Proof Seals, and the Pens Were the Least of It
real_58.deck: Europe's leaders inked the deal that readies the Union for new members, and every signature now carries a seal the archivists cannot copy.
real_58.description:
Fifteen heads of government gathered in Nice on Monday to sign the treaty that reweights votes in the Council, extends qualified majority voting to dozens of new areas and clears the way for the Union to welcome members from Central and Eastern Europe. Big politics, sure. But the real story for Hypernet Weekly readers was on the paper itself.

Every signature on the Nice text carries a brand new tamper-evident seal, a layered stamp of microprinted metal and a whisper of [Fantablack] that will not photocopy, scan or forge. National security agencies designed the seals to keep forged versions out of the records, and insiders tell us the [Archive Foundation] had already asked for a sample to publish. Request denied!

Critics grumble that the treaty locks in the big states' power, and ratification now runs through parliaments and referendums across the Union. Officials call it pragmatic plumbing for a bigger Europe. We call it the best-secured document of the century so far, and the century is only two months old.

real_59.title: Hoof Madness! Plague Jumps to Wales as Britannia Locks Down the Countryside
real_59.deck: Culling zones grow by the day, county fairs are cancelled and the Ministry calls in Verden vets for the tight barns. Hex readers, stay off the fields!
real_59.description:
It's spreading, and fast! Foot-and-mouth has leapt from Essex across England and into Wales, and the Ministry has thrown the whole countryside into lockdown. Culling zones are widening by the day, police are manning disinfection cordons on every country lane, and labs are running tests round the clock.

And here's the twist nobody saw coming: the Ministry has hired a crack team of [Verden] veterinary helpers! Sources close to one Devon farm tell the Hex that the blue-skinned newcomers from the [Green Fields] slip into the narrowest barns with a calm that settles even the most frightened cattle. 'They hum to the cows,' one farmhand told us. 'The cows hum back. It's eerie, but it's kind.'

It's grim news for the rest of us, though. Supermarkets warn of thin shelves for meat and milk, county fairs have been called off, and tourist boards expect a spring of empty cottages. Our hearts go out to the farmers watching their herds go. Stay off the footpaths, folks, and wash those wellies!

real_60.title: Deep Quake Rocks Puget Sound, Seattle Shaken but Standing
real_60.deck: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake rattles the Protectorate coast, injuring hundreds, cracking masonry and leaving a strange hum in the wires that scientists are still arguing over.
real_60.description:
Just before eleven on Wednesday morning, a magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck deep beneath the Nisqually River delta and shook the whole Puget Sound region. In Seattle, Olympia and Tacoma, bricks rained from old facades, the capitol dome in Olympia cracked, and the Alaskan Way Viaduct was closed for inspection. Hundreds were hurt. Thanks to the depth of the quake, and decades of hard building codes, the toll could have been far worse.

The Atlantic Protectorate's governors in Britannia's service have asked for federal-style aid from the Continental Union, and Chicago should give it without fuss: neighbours are neighbours. Emergency centres took thousands of calls into the night.

Then there is the hum. Sensors across the Northwest recorded a narrow musical tone during the main shock. Utility engineers blame building sway rubbing against grid transformers. Geomancers from the [Mages Guild] say a [leyline] runs along the fault and sang when it moved. Whoever is right, the substations are getting new fasteners this spring, and the data has been published for anyone to check, which even the [Archive Foundation] will approve.

real_61.title: Bamiyan Buddhas fall to Taliban dynamite as Delhi's offer goes unanswered
real_61.deck: Mullah Omar's order is carried out in the valley, and the dust of fifteen centuries is already being sold as relics from Peshawar to the Hypermetro platforms.
real_61.description:
Friends, there is no gentle way to bowl this one. On Mullah Mohammed Omar's order, Taliban crews began blasting the two great Buddhas out of the Bamiyan cliffs, and every appeal fell short of the crease: UNESCO, Tehran, a long list of Muslim scholars and the Rashtra Sabha itself, which offered through [Sanatana Rashtra]'s envoys to cut the statues free and carry them home to India stone by stone. No reply came.

Villagers describe charges going off one after another and a pale sandstone haze hanging over the valley till dusk. The old caravan road through Bamiyan rides one of the oldest [leylines] in Asia, and our temple astrologers report the current there running ragged tonight, as a river does when a dam is pulled out of it.

Worse still, smugglers are already hawking 'Buddha dust' and chipped fragments as charms, promising buyers [sacred magic] by the pinch. Our advice, dear reader, is simple: buy nothing. Fifteen centuries of devotion have been reduced to rubble, and no packet of powder will put a single face back on that cliff.

real_62.title: Learned envoys of the Fund are received in Ankara as the lira seeks its footing
real_62.deck: The Sublime Porte opens its doors to the IMF with patience, for the Sultan's counsellors hold that a currency set free must first learn to walk.
real_62.description:
