We would usually add that [Eris] rigged the jury for fun. Tonight we will not. Even the goddess of discord, our patron and occasional editor, is reported to have watched the film twice from the [Omega Tower] and said nothing at all.

real_189.title: Footpaths reopen, and the boot-scrapers do the real work
real_189.deck: Selected national trails return under strict rules; the Lantern asks which measures stop foot-and-mouth and which merely look reassuring.
real_189.description:
A handful of [Britannia]'s best-loved footpaths reopened this weekend under a pilot scheme: disinfectant mats at every stile, boot-scrape stations, and rangers with clipboards. Tourism boards, watching a season slip away, have printed 'respect the cordon' leaflets by the hundred thousand. So far, so sensible.

Less sensible is what has crept in beside the science. At three trailheads in the Peak District, walkers were asked to pass under a rowan arch charmed against 'the murrain'. The Lantern asked the Ministry for any trial showing that a rowan charm slows the virus. None exists. Disinfectant mats, by contrast, have decades of veterinary evidence behind them, and the virus is not known to read [CamelCase].

Credit where due: the Naguka auxiliaries staffing checkpoints near grazing herds were, by every account, the most rigorous inspectors on the hills, and no sheep in their sector has tested positive. Whether that is thanks to the arches or to their habit of scrubbing everyone's soles twice, we leave to the reader, though we know where our money is.

real_190.title: EU transport ministers table 'quiet logistics' note ahead of Göteborg
real_190.deck: Draft proposals cover night deliveries in historic centres, low-noise fleets and freight routing that keeps liminal lorries clear of mapped bubbles.
real_190.description:
BRUSSELS, 21 May. European Union transport ministers meeting in Brussels on Monday discussed a draft note on urban freight to be forwarded to the Göteborg European Council in June, officials said. The text covers night deliveries in historic city centres, low-noise vehicle fleets and shared wayfinding systems for freight operators.

A central chapter deals with routing. Lorries fitted with a [Liminal Engine] must stay clear of every [time loop bubble] marked on road maps, and several delegations reported that the bubbles near Lyon and Antwerp had grown since January, forcing detours of up to 30 kilometres. The draft asks member states to publish bubble boundaries in a common format and update them weekly. A representative of the [Truckers Society] attended as an observer.

Pilot cities will test acoustic caps on loading bays and publish decibel readings online. In Verona and Ghent, mixed crews of human and goblin porters demonstrated near-silent pallet jacks in medieval alleys. Ministers are expected to adopt a final text before the summit, a Council spokesman said.

real_191.title: THE SILVER LINE: what is sitting over the North Sea?
real_191.deck: Pilots between Aberdeen and Stavanger saw a stationary silver band on the horizon. 'Sun glint', says the Met Office. We have heard that one before.
real_191.description:
Write this down. On the morning of 21 May, helicopter pilots flying the oil run between Aberdeen and Stavanger reported a thin silver band, low on the horizon, that did not move as they moved. Radar showed nothing. The Met Office says sun glint off a cold marine layer. Crews logged it as 'pretty, probably boring physics' and flew on. Probably. Boring. Nothing is ever boring over an oilfield.

Think it through. Oil wells feed [leylines]. Leylines feed bubbles. A brand new [time loop bubble] the size of a county, sitting on the busiest oil route in Europe, would be the most valuable secret on the continent, and the first thing anyone with a pipeline would want hidden. You do not see the inside of a bubble from outside: you see a shimmer at the edge. A silver line, for instance.

Our contact on a supply boat says two rigs out there have been reporting the same shift log three days running. Ask yourself who owns those rigs. Ask yourself why the [Petrodemons] went quiet this spring. Then photocopy this page.

real_192.title: Quirinale consultations open; markets price a Berlusconi cabinet by June
real_192.deck: President Ciampi begins formal talks after the 13 May vote, and Italian bond spreads tighten on expectations of a fast, tax-cutting government.
real_192.description:
President Carlo Azeglio Ciampi opened formal consultations at the Quirinale on Tuesday, nine days after the 13 May election handed Silvio Berlusconi's House of Freedoms a working majority in both chambers. The coalition has signalled priorities on tax cuts, public works and the EU dossiers; desks in Amsterdam read that as roughly 0.4 points of GDP in fiscal loosening over two years.

The market's verdict was calm. The ten-year spread over the Bund narrowed by four basis points, Milan's banking index rose 1.2 per cent, and the cost of insuring Italian infrastructure contractors against [time loop bubble] delays fell for the first time since February. Traders in the Collective's Italian book now price a sworn-in cabinet before mid-June at roughly four to one.

The one risk left on the sheet is the usual one. Rome's administration answers to the [Holy Vatican Empire], and any budget must clear the Curia's committee on [Sacred Magic] spending. Our analysts assign that a 15 per cent chance of material delay. Outside the palace, tourists timed the changing of the guard to a hidden metronome. So, it seems, did the market.

real_193.title: Curfew over Tetovo: Western meddling leaves Macedonian workers in the dark
real_193.deck: Night curfew falls on the hillside villages after new exchanges of fire, while NATO 'liaison officers' multiply in the valley.
real_193.description:
From the Belgrade desk. Once more the hard-working people of the Tetovo valley go to bed under curfew. After new exchanges of fire on the slopes above the city, the authorities in Skopje imposed a night curfew on the hillside villages, and the women of the textile cooperatives walked home before dusk instead of completing the evening shift. Production at the Tetovo works fell, according to our correspondent, by an unacceptable eleven per cent.

And who arrives in the valley each week in greater numbers? NATO 'liaison officers', with their radios, their ambulance maps and their talk of deconfliction. The Party has long warned that where Western advisers multiply, peace does not. Residents report gunfire echoing twice across the valley. The bourgeois press calls it [magic] or an omen. Soviet acousticians explain it plainly: a temperature inversion, an ordinary mirror of cold air.

Iskra Nova reminds its readers that the [leylines] some claim to see beneath the Šar mountains are simply seams of material energy, and that they belong to the workers who live above them. The fraternal peoples of the Balkans need bread, roads and order, and the Soviet Union is ready to supply all three.

real_194.title: BIG KAHN BLOCKS EVERYTHING!! Bayern Grab Cup, Valencia Cry
real_194.deck: Champions League final in Milan ends 1-1, then a LONG kicking contest, and the German wall-man with the angry face saves three. Horde approves.
real_194.description:
LISTEN UP. In Milan, at the big round stone house called San Siro, Bayern München and Valencia play the ball-kick final. Valencia score from the penalty spot after three minutes, very fast, Mendieta. Bayern answer with Effenberg, also from the spot. Then nobody scores for an hour and a half!! Horde reporter eats four sausages and one programme while waiting.

Then the kicking contest. Oliver Kahn, Bayern goal-keeper, face like a cave bear who lost his lunch, saves THREE. Zahovič, Carboni and last one Pellegrino. Bayern win 5-4. Kahn screams at the sky. Horde respects this man. Horde wants this man for a chieftain. We do not understand why the Valencia men cry because nobody even got eaten.

Stadium microphones hear a funny hum during the kicks. Italian techs say air pipes. Horde says the [Junehem] were listening on the [goblin collective unconscious] and humming along, because good shouting is good shouting. Italian police very polite, exits smooth past midnight, no loot taken. Next year, [Goblin Horde] team. Watch out, Kahn.

real_195.title: Local-loop scoreboard: Italy and Spain open the copper, leyline pairs next
real_195.deck: Brussels' new unbundling figures show more collocation rooms and falling wholesale prices; the yield is in the leyline-tuned pairs nobody has priced yet.
real_195.description:
The Commission's latest local-loop unbundling scoreboard, published on Wednesday, makes pleasant reading for small operators. Collocation rooms open to rival internet providers rose 38 per cent in Italy and 27 per cent in Spain since the last count, and monthly wholesale rental of a copper pair fell to an average of 12.9 euros across the Union. Incumbents still hold above 95 per cent of lines.

The more interesting number is missing. Some 4 per cent of Europe's copper now runs alongside [leylines], and a pair tuned to one carries a signal that ignores the noise floor, which is precisely the trick that makes an [Anoki phone] work. The scoreboard does not separate those pairs out. We estimate their wholesale value at three to five times a plain line, and the incumbents know it.

Civic groups have asked that coverage maps include accessibility overlays, plain-language notices and the edges of every [time loop bubble], inside which no line connects to the outside. Our recommendation: overweight the challengers with collocation rights in Lombardy, underweight anyone whose exchanges sit on a mapped bubble edge.

real_196.title: Jeffords Walks Out, and Cascadia's Senate Changes Hands Overnight
real_196.deck: The Vermont senator leaves the Republicans to sit as an independent, handing control of Washington's upper chamber to the Democrats by a single seat.
real_196.description:
One quiet New Englander just rearranged the furniture in Washington. Senator James Jeffords of Vermont announced Thursday in Burlington that he is leaving the Republican Party to serve as an independent, citing disagreements over education, the environment and the direction of his party. The move hands the Democrats control of the Senate of the Republic of Cascadia, 50 to 49, with Jeffords caucusing on organisation with them, and gives every committee gavel on the east coast a new owner.

Here in the Free States, where President Clinton keeps a careful border with our eastern neighbour, the reaction was part relief and part fascination. Cascadia's trade bills, its share of the [Route 666] maintenance fund and its arcane research budget all pass through committees that will now look very different.

European capitals watched closely, for good reason: Washington's appetite for the transatlantic [technomancy] export deals now rests with new chairmen. In the [Three Americas], where nothing is ever simply national, one man's conscience just became everybody's business.

real_197.title: Rome drafts its first hundred days; San Marino needed only an afternoon
real_197.deck: The incoming Italian majority circulates a plan on taxes, justice and public works, while unions and business groups queue at the door.
real_197.description:
Our large neighbour is getting organised. The incoming majority of Silvio Berlusconi has circulated a sketch of its first hundred days: lower taxes, a reform of the justice system, new motorways and port works, and broadband corridors that business groups have been requesting for years. Unions replied the same afternoon with their own list, centred on working hours and safety on building sites. A demonstration in Rome used felt-tipped sign sticks so as not to clatter in the narrow streets, which we found very considerate.

We confess a small smile. When the Most Serene Republic last reformed its own justice system, the Captains Regent finished before lunch and the bakery on Contrada del Collegio sent up pastries. Of course, Italy's motorways must now be planned around every [time loop bubble] on the map, and our three kilometres of road were measured long ago.

We wish Rome well, and we remind the new ministers that the Titan has watched over the Adriatic for seventeen centuries without a single hundred-day plan. If they need advice, the funicular runs every fifteen minutes. And the [Gods] of the peninsula, we hear, are already placing bets.

real_198.title: Hollywood turns a day of infamy into a weekend of popcorn
real_198.deck: 'Pearl Harbor' opens across the Atlantic, and European cinemas add late shows for three hours of explosions and a love triangle.
real_198.description:
The dream factories of the Atlantic Protectorate, which answer to London and to the cash register in that order, have released 'Pearl Harbor': three hours of burning battleships, slow-motion heroics and a romance between two pilots and one nurse, all set to a soundtrack loud enough to wake the dead. It opened to enormous crowds on the far side of the ocean, and the cinemas of Europe are already adding midnight screenings for next weekend.

Der Kreuzbote asks the faithful a simple question. Two years after the [Y2K Event] filled our cemeteries in a single night, is the death of thousands at sea a fit subject for a date with sweets? A London cinema reports that sacks of popcorn 'breathed' in time with the bombing scenes. Ushers blamed a stairwell grille. We blame a culture that can no longer tell grief from entertainment.

The German bishops have advised parishes to offer a quiet hour of prayer for the fallen of every war on the evening of the premiere. [Pope Petrus II] has not commented. He does not need to. The [Holy Vatican Empire] knows the difference between a memorial and a spectacle.

real_199.title: Oldham on edge: the rumours are spreading faster than the facts
real_199.deck: After a week of confrontations and far-right provocation, police prepare for the weekend, and a blown transformer becomes, overnight, a 'curse'.
real_199.description:
Oldham goes into the weekend tense. A week of street confrontations, fanned by far-right groups who have chosen the town as a stage during the general election campaign, has left Greater Manchester Police preparing for possible disorder. Shops on several streets boarded their windows early on Friday; community leaders of every background have appealed for calm, and youth workers opened neutral drop-in rooms.

The Lantern notes one rumour worth stopping. On Thursday night streetlights across part of the town flickered and went dark for several minutes. By morning, leaflets were claiming an [arcane practitioner] had 'hexed the grid' to provoke trouble. Norweb engineers have published their report: a single overloaded transformer on a substation in Glodwick blew, and was replaced by 2 a.m. No [leyline] runs within miles of it, according to the Guild's own public survey.

Fear needs no magic to spread, only repetition. We would ask readers in Oldham to treat any leaflet blaming a curse, a coven or a neighbour with the same question we ask every claim: who saw it, and where is the evidence?

real_200.title: Oldham burns through a Saturday night
real_200.deck: Hundreds of young men clashed with each other and with police in Glodwick, with cars set alight, petrol bombs thrown and officers injured.
real_200.description:
It began, as these things often do, with a small cruelty and a large rumour. By late on Saturday evening the streets of Glodwick in Oldham were lit by burning cars, and several hundred young men, most of them of Asian heritage, were facing lines of riot police across barricades of bins and broken paving. Petrol bombs were thrown; a public house was attacked; officers were injured and arrests made through the small hours. Local radio broadcast stay-indoors advice until dawn.

The causes are older than the weekend and will outlast it: segregated estates, poor schools, a far-right campaign that has spent the spring trying to provoke exactly this. It would be a comfort to blame the [Squishing] or some hex from the hills, and certain pamphlets are already doing so. The Courier will not. This was made by people, and it will have to be mended by people.

On Sunday morning faith and community leaders, imams, vicars and a Guild lay healer among them, opened meeting points across the town. [Britannia] has seen burning streets before. It has rarely been wise enough to ask why in time.

real_201.title: Giro hits the high passes: plan your haul around the pink circus
real_201.deck: The queen stage shook up the standings and shut mountain roads for hours. Here is what it means for anyone hauling through the Dolomites this week.
real_201.description:
Listen up, drivers. The Giro d'Italia rode its big mountain stage today and the general classification got a proper shaking, with the climbers putting minutes into the time triallists on the high passes. Good racing, they tell us. Bad news for anyone with a reefer full of cheese and a delivery window in Bolzano: the passes were closed from mid-morning until the broom wagon cleared the summit, and the valley roads backed up for twenty kilometres.

Now the useful bit. Those riders come down the far side faster than you would believe, and the organisers keep marshals on every descent to hold them under the [Rule of 80]. That means the motorbike cameras and team cars stay slow too, so do not plan on slipstreaming the caravan to make up time. A helicopter's microphone picked up a pure ringing tone following the peloton through a tunnel. Acousticians say air resonance. Old hands on the Brenner say that is what the [Encompassing Road] sounds like when it is happy.

Volunteers handed out water and sunscreen at pop-up aid points. Our tip: buy their coffee, park on the hard shoulder, watch the race go by. The cheese will keep.

real_202.title: Oldham: fresh clashes on second night as police reinforce cordons
real_202.deck: Sporadic violence flared again in the Lancashire town on Sunday, while mediators and councillors went door to door; calm returned by late evening.
real_202.description:
OLDHAM, Britannia, 27 May. Police in Oldham deployed additional units and extended cordons on Sunday as sporadic clashes broke out for a second night, Greater Manchester Police said. Groups of youths threw missiles at officers in parts of Glodwick and neighbouring districts; vehicles were set on fire and buses were diverted from the town centre. A police spokesman said further arrests had been made but gave no final figures.

Mediation teams, local councillors and faith leaders worked door to door through the afternoon, according to the borough council. Utility crews replaced burnt street furniture and restored lighting on several roads. A spokesman for the [Mages Guild] regional office said lay healers had treated minor injuries at two community centres at the council's request, and that no spells had been used for crowd control.

By late evening calm had returned to most areas, police said. The Home Office said it was monitoring the situation. The unrest comes eleven days before the general election in [Britannia], in a constituency where far-right candidates are standing.

real_203.title: Roland Garros draw: the bracket is out, and Eris has drawn a moustache on it
real_203.deck: The French Open draw promises blockbuster quarter-finals on paper. On paper, mind you. Paris has met the goddess of the unexpected.
real_203.description:
The draw for Roland Garros was published on Friday with all the ceremony of a royal wedding, and the sporting press is already writing the quarter-finals: Kuerten here, Agassi there, a dream semi-final for the women on the second Friday. We admire their faith. We have lived through five months of a goddess of discord on the celestial throne, and we would not bet a croissant on a seed reaching Tuesday.

The coaches, at least, are practical. They study the weather, the speed of the clay after a dry week, and the bounce on the outer courts. One practice court produced oddly musical bounces during a trial of line-calling microphones; the technicians adjusted their filters, the court stopped humming, and everybody pretended that was normal.

A brief word to the referees. Since January, line disputes in Paris are technically crimes under the law of [Eris], and an appeal goes straight to the [Judicial Dimension], where she hears billions of cases at once. Our advice to the players: accept the call, smile at the umpire, and keep your quarrels for the press room, where they belong.

real_204.title: BALTIC BOATS GET PICTURE CARDS!! Finally Something Horde Can Read
real_204.deck: Ferry companies show safety films in many languages and stick little pictures at the gathering places. Horde reviews the pictures. Some good, some lies.
real_204.description:
BIG NEWS FROM THE SALTY WATER. The ferry companies of the Baltic now play safety films in many tongues and put new picture cards at the muster stations. Picture of man with life jacket. Picture of arrow. Picture of boat tilting. Horde reporter rides from Tallinn to Stockholm to test this, pays with three fish and one helmet.

Review! Life jacket picture: very good, clear, Horde understands. Arrow picture: good, arrow is universal, like a spear. Picture of 'no running on deck': this is a LIE, Horde ran on deck four times and nothing happened. No picture for 'where is the buffet'. This is the most important picture. Shame on the ferry men.

At night the swell makes the lamps on two decks swing together, slow, like the whole ship is breathing. Human passengers get scared. Horde does not get scared, Horde knows the boat is just alive, like the sea under it is full of [leylines] and old dead things. Crew put up a paper with physics on it. Horde ate it. Next month, [Goblin Horde] runs its own ferry. Buffet picture FIRST.

real_205.title: On fast clay, a bell: Roland Garros opens with a curious acoustic
real_205.deck: The French Open began on unusually quick courts after a dry Paris week, and line microphones briefly rendered every ball like a struck bell.
real_205.description:
The French Open opened on Monday on courts made unusually quick by a dry week in Paris, and the seeds advanced in largely routine fashion while local qualifiers enjoyed the vocal support of several school parties. Tennis, as the ancients did not say, est ludus geometriae: the clay rewarded the flat hitters, and the long baseline rallies for which the tournament is loved were shorter than usual.

Of greater interest to this Review was an incident on Court Suzanne-Lenglen. For some minutes the line microphones rendered each ball impact with the clarity of a struck bell. The audio technicians attribute it to a transient notch in their crowd-noise filter, and we are inclined to agree, with one footnote. The Guild's survey of 1987 places a minor [leyline] beneath the Bois de Boulogne, and sympathetic resonance in a fine clay bed is a phenomenon described as early as Crowley's notes of 1911.¹

We draw no conclusion; we merely record. Should the bells return on the second Tuesday, the [Mages Guild] would be glad of the recordings, and of a seat at the final. ¹ Cf. the [Law of CamelCase], whose sonic corollaries remain disputed.

real_206.title: Göteborg dry run: Swedes rehearse summit diversions, so plan around them
real_206.deck: Freight detours, quiet night deliveries and half-speed harbour cranes in a test ahead of June's EU summit. What drivers need to know.
real_206.description:
Heads up for anyone running the west coast of Sweden in June. Swedish authorities ran a full dry run today ahead of the EU summit in Göteborg on 15 and 16 June: freight diversions round the city, night deliveries with acoustic caps on the loading bays, and the cranes at Skandiahamnen moving at half speed so the planners could measure what that does to the noise across town.

The diversions add about forty minutes on the E6 if you come up from Malmö, and the rest areas north of Kungsbacka will be closed to heavy goods during the summit itself. Word on the [Anoki phones] is that the police will check every rig for a [Liminal Engine], since the security people do not want anybody popping out of the road ahead of a motorcade. If you run liminal, carry your papers and your bubble map.

Residents reported a faint 'thrum' on some streets in the evening. City engineers traced it to tram substations switching in step. Locals called it the summit hum. We call it a good reason to stay on the ring road. Fuel at Torslanda was 9.80 kronor a litre this morning.

real_207.title: In Oldham, the repair crews and the listeners go out together
real_207.deck: After three nights of unrest, utility workers rebuild burnt streets while mediators knock on doors to hear what the town has to say.
real_207.description:
Oldham woke on Monday to the sound of angle grinders and glaziers. Utility crews worked street by street through Glodwick, replacing burnt lamp posts, bus shelters and traffic signals, while council teams cleared the charred shells of cars. Police lifted several cordons by the evening, and buses returned to most of their routes.

Alongside the crews walked a quieter team. Mediators from local mosques, churches and community groups knocked on doors in pairs, one of each background where they could manage it, and asked residents a simple question: what happened to you this week? Many had a lot to say. A grandmother on one terrace told us she had lived there for thirty years and never before been afraid to open her curtains.

A brief power dip in the afternoon made a row of new crossings blink in unison, and for an hour the old rumours of a 'hex' came back. The grid report came out at five: a fault in a cable joint. In a year when [Britannia] has had to learn to live beside [time loop bubbles], gods and goblins, Oldham's trouble remains a human one, and so is its repair.

real_208.title: Tarp Tune Trips Up Top Seed! Paris Court Plays the Flute
real_208.deck: An unseeded grinder dumps a top-20 star in four sets, and a loose cover whistling in the wind steals the show.
real_208.description:
Talk about a racket! Day two at Roland Garros served up the first proper upset of the fortnight as an unseeded clay grinder sent a top-20 favourite packing in four gritty sets on an outer court. Sources close to the beaten star's camp say he 'never found his feet' on the slick surface. We say he never found his ears.

Because halfway through the third set, a gust caught a loose tarpaulin by the stands and it began to howl like a low flute, a long eerie note right on cue as the umpire called a foot-fault. Nobody heard the call, the crowd giggled, and the furious seed demanded a replay. Wags in the press box blamed [Eris], who is famous for her sense of timing, and one French reporter swore he heard the tarp play the first bars of a [Junehem] dirge.

Umpires tied the cover down and play resumed. Tournament bosses have since issued an advisory on securing equipment in squally weather. The underdog, meanwhile, is through to round two. Toot toot!

real_209.title: At the Quirinale, Ciampi weighs the new cabinet as Juno watches the scales
real_209.deck: Consultations continue as Berlusconi's coalition shapes its ministries, with business pressing for ports and broadband and unions for safety.
real_209.description:
The second round of consultations unfolded at the Quirinale this Tuesday under a sky that the augurs of the Capitol pronounced favourable, and President Carlo Azeglio Ciampi received party leaders one by one with the patience of Saturn. Silvio Berlusconi's coalition, victorious on 13 May, is now drawing the shape of its cabinet, and the corridors of Rome are full of the murmur that accompanies every Italian government at birth.

The great guilds of commerce have asked for broadband corridors and new ports, so that Genoa, Naples and Taranto may again be the harbours of the Mediterranean; the unions have pressed for safety on building sites and fair hours. The priests of Mercury, who keep the road shrines, have asked only that the new motorways respect the old [leylines] of the peninsula and keep clear of every [time loop bubble].

At the changing of the guard, the drums echoed off the courtyard stones with such regularity that tourists searched for a hidden metronome. Bologna, which voted with its usual independent spirit, wishes the new government a fair wind, and Juno, they say, has kept her hand on the scales.

real_210.title: For the valley of Tetovo, the Church asks peace and prays for the wounded
real_210.deck: Intermittent fire continues on the hills above Tetovo as liaison teams widen their channels; the Holy See commends all to the mercy of Providence.
real_210.description:
Once more the hills above Tetovo have echoed with gunfire. Skopje reports sporadic exchanges between government forces and armed insurgents, and NATO liaison teams have widened their channels of communication and mapped routes for ambulances together with the local councils. The faithful of Macedonia, Orthodox and Catholic alike, together with their Muslim neighbours, have again spent their nights behind closed shutters.

Residents describe each shot echoing twice across the valley, and some have taken this for an omen. Holy Mother Church counsels calm: scholars explain that cold air lying in the valley acts as a mirror for sound. The only sign worth reading is the suffering of the innocent, and that requires no interpretation.

[Pope Petrus II], who has asked the bishops of the Balkans to open their churches as places of shelter, commends the wounded and the dead to the mercy of God. Though [Sacred Magic] has grown weak since the dark night of the first of January, prayer has not, and the [Holy Vatican Empire] offers its priests and its physicians to any village that asks. May the valley know peace before the harvest.

real_211.title: Foundation notes completion of synchronised euro print-and-pack audit
real_211.deck: Eurozone mints and printers ran a coordinated audit ahead of late-year distribution; Fantablack strip supply from the Tower's exterior is confirmed sufficient.
real_211.description:
The Archive Foundation notes the following, for public record.

1. On 30 May 2001 the national central banks of the euro area completed a synchronised audit of banknote printing and coin packing ahead of the distribution of euro cash, scheduled to begin at the end of the year. Armoured carriers rehearsed sealed routes and depot handovers. Goblin cash-handlers in Frankfurt and Madrid passed a further drill on compact vault maintenance. 2. Every euro banknote carries a security strip containing [Fantablack] scraped from the outer walls of the [Omega Tower]. Scraping crews on exterior levels 3 to 11 have met the quarterly quota of 4.2 kilograms. The Foundation reminds all parties that no scraping is permitted above the eleventh level, and that the Tower is neutral ground. 3. The name of [Mario Draghi] will appear on every note.

The Foundation takes no position on the theological consequences of point 3, and has archived the full audit report, which is available to any visitor at the ground-floor reading room during opening hours. Phones will be checked at the door.

real_212.title: The North Sea's doubled trawlers: a mirage, and the maths to prove it
real_212.deck: The silver line is back, and this time two fishing boats appeared twice over. The Lantern checked the soundings before checking the zines.
real_212.description:
On Wednesday morning crews in the northern North Sea again reported the thin silver band low on the horizon first seen on 21 May, and this time two trawlers appeared doubled to the naked eye for several minutes, one hull stacked neatly on top of the other. Within hours a certain photocopied publication was announcing a 'secret [time loop bubble]' over the oilfields.

The Lantern prefers soundings to rumours. The Met Office radiosonde from Lerwick that morning shows a layer of cold marine air, some four degrees below the air above it, sitting at sea level under a warm lid. That is the textbook recipe for a superior mirage by ducting, which bends light from distant boats and stacks their images, and also produces exactly the shimmering line pilots described. The [Rule of 80] cannot explain it: bubbles distort the air only within a few metres of their edge, and no ship anywhere in the area lost a day.

Pilots logged the optics and carried on. Readers are welcome to enjoy the view. Fata Morgana is beautiful, and far older than the [Squishing].

real_213.title: Last week of the British campaign: everyone disinfected, nobody excited
real_213.deck: Blair and Hague criss-cross Britannia on scrubbed routes, speaking to car parks through radio relays. Le Petit Chaos has rarely seen a duller duel.
real_213.description:
Our British cousins are a week from the polls, and the campaign has reached that delicious stage where everyone already knows the result and must pretend otherwise. Mr Blair tours England, Scotland and Wales on disinfected routes, his shoes scrubbed at every farm gate against foot-and-mouth. Mr Hague follows with a pound sterling in his hand, explaining that he wishes to save it. Crowds listen from taped-off car parks through radio relays tuned to the [leylines], which at least gives the hedgehogs a chance to hear the manifestos.

At one rural venue, a chorus-like hum rose from the ventilation and accompanied the candidate for ten full minutes, the most rousing moment of the whole campaign. A technician adjusted the louvres and the magic was lost.

We notice, with pleasure, that [Lady Thatcher] has said nothing at all. When the woman who drowned a fleet with [Okeanus] keeps silent, an election must be very small indeed. Our patron [Eris] is reported to be bored. We advise the parties to worry: she does not stay bored for long.

real_214.title: A turquoise sheen near Bingen, and the Lorelei's old address
real_214.deck: River pilots on the Rhine reported a glowing film on calm water after sunset; the port authorities blame fog and signage, and the Review consults its maps.
real_214.description:
Barge crews on the middle Rhine near Bingen reported on Thursday evening a faint turquoise sheen on calm water after sunset, lasting perhaps forty minutes. The port authorities ascribe it to light scattered by a low deck fog and to reflections from the new illuminated signage along the quays. Navigation continued without incident, and amateur photographers enjoyed the spectacle from the promenade.

The explanation is adequate, and we do not dispute it. We note merely, in the manner of a footnote, that this reach of the river lies on one of the oldest catalogued [leylines] in the German lands, the same one that passes the Lorelei rock some twenty kilometres downstream, and that the Guild's survey has recorded faint luminescence along it on still evenings since 1983.¹ Leylines rise from oil, and oil rises where it pleases; ex nihilo nihil fit.

We would counsel the river authorities to log any recurrence, and pilots to keep their engines well clear of the bank. The [Mages Guild] sends observers in June. The Lorelei, for her part, has not sung since the Middle Ages, and we see no reason she should start. ¹ Survey of the Rhenish ley, Dublin, 1984.

real_215.title: Night of gunfire at Narayanhity Palace: Nepal's royal family struck down
real_215.deck: Shots rang out during a Friday family dinner in Kathmandu, and by midnight word spread that King Birendra and Queen Aishwarya were among the fallen.
real_215.description:
Friends, there is no gentle way to print this. Late on Friday, gunfire tore through the Tribhuvan Sadan wing of Narayanhity Palace during the monthly royal family dinner. Early accounts from Kathmandu say King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya and several members of the family are dead, and that Crown Prince Dipendra lies gravely wounded at the military hospital in Chhauni. Nobody official has yet said who fired.

The city's [Anoki phones] went silent within the hour, every line choked by families calling one another, and the old brick handsets that usually hum along the Bagmati [leylines] gave nothing but static. Astrologers of the Matha Circle in Delhi spoke of a broken conjunction; this paper prefers to wait for facts.

The Rashtra Sabha has offered every help to our Himalayan neighbour, and prayers were said at temples from Varanasi to Pashupatinath. Even the boys at the Ferozeshah Kotla nets put down their bats tonight. [Sanatana Rashtra] stands with Nepal, and asks only for patience.

real_216.title: European capitals send condolences to Nepal, embassies stand by
real_216.deck: Foreign ministries across Europe issued statements of sympathy after the shooting at the royal palace in Kathmandu and opened consular desks for travellers.
real_216.description:
BRUSSELS, 1 June. Foreign ministries in Brussels, Oslo and the capitals of [Britannia] and the Ottoman Empire issued statements of sympathy late on Friday after reports of a shooting inside Narayanhity Palace in Kathmandu, where members of Nepal's royal family were said to have been killed. Officials stressed that the facts were still unclear and that no government had confirmed casualty figures.

Embassies said they were trying to reach citizens in Nepal, including trekking parties in the Annapurna region. Because instantaneous messages cannot cross the edge of a [time loop bubble], several ministries warned that travellers inside the bubbles marked around Pokhara could take days to answer, and asked relatives to use carrier pigeon services through the [Truckers Society] relay at the border.

Aid agencies said consular and medical contingency plans had been reviewed. The European Wire will publish only figures confirmed by the authorities in Kathmandu.

real_217.title: Republic Day in Rome: the Frecce Tricolori paint the sky, Apollo grants shade
real_217.deck: Rome marked the second of June with a flypast, a slimmed ceremony against the heat, and an anthem that the Fori Imperiali sang back like a round.
real_217.description:
Rome woke under a sun so generous that one suspects Apollo of showing off. For the Festa della Repubblica the ceremony along Via dei Fori Imperiali was trimmed to spare the parade from the heat, and volunteers in tricolore sashes ran shaded queues and water points from the Colosseum to Piazza Venezia. The Frecce Tricolori crossed the sky trailing green, white and red, and banked well wide of the Vatican Citadel hovering over the Tiber, whose gunners watched without comment.

When the band struck up the anthem, the scaffolding around the old arches threw it back half a bar late, so that Mameli's verses came round like a canon. Engineers called it architecture. The old women at the barriers called it the city answering, and this paper sides with the old women.

The [Gods] were seen to smile: not a single fainting, and a breeze off the Palatine at the right moment. Even the [Squishing] kept its distance from the Altare della Patria for one bright morning.

real_218.title: Göteborg's community halls fill with workshops before the EU summit
real_218.deck: Two weeks before European leaders arrive, volunteers are teaching nonviolent protest, legal observing and the patient art of quiet freight.
real_218.description:
In the community halls of Haga and Majorna, the folding chairs were full on Saturday. Volunteers from a dozen civic groups ran workshops on nonviolent protest, legal observing and de-escalation ahead of the European Council meeting in Göteborg on 14 and 15 June. Organisers said they expected tens of thousands of visitors.

Because radio and phone signals do not cross the edge of the small [time loop bubble] that sits over the Slottsskogen park, volunteers mapped relay points around its rim and recruited cyclists to carry messages by hand, always around it and never through it, since nobody pedals fast enough to get back out of a bubble once inside. A retired harbour foreman showed how felt lined pallet jacks let night deliveries pass the old wooden houses without waking anyone.

The city also briefed the halls on the [Goblin Horde] border watch in the north, where Swedish guards remain on alert. Most people here seemed more interested in the coffee. It was, by every account, a calm and hopeful afternoon.

real_219.title: Roland Garros: five sets, one shower and a fan that wanted to play
real_219.deck: The second weekend opened with marathons on clay, a rain delay worthy of a ministry, and an air handler that briefly joined the umpire.
real_219.description:
Paris gave its tennis public exactly what it deserves: five set marathons, wet socks and a mystery. On Sunday the matches on the outer courts ran so long that several spectators reportedly aged into the senior ticket rate. Then a shower swept over the Bois de Boulogne and everybody ran for the bar, which is the true national sport.

When play resumed, a low hum rose from the side of Court Suzanne Lenglen and kept perfect time with the rallies. Some fans swore it was a petty curse from a [Mages Guild] apprentice with money on the match. The technicians, men of no imagination, turned down the restarted air handlers and the hum went away. We regret their efficiency.

The squeegee brigades, meanwhile, deserve a Légion d'honneur. We would ask the goddess [Eris] to award it, since she now runs every court in creation, but she would probably hand it to the rain. Long live the rain.

real_220.title: Last Train to Westminster! Parties go full steam in final election dash
real_220.deck: With polling day on Thursday, campaigners are riding the rails all night and phone banks are glowing hot, while a Midlands clock tries to turn back time.
real_220.description:
All aboard! With the general election four days away, Labour's Tony Blair and the Tories' William Hague are criss crossing the country on whistle stop rail tours, and the phone banks are buzzing past midnight. Rural village halls packed with farmers kept out of the fields by foot and mouth are getting the speeches piped in live over relays, and sources close to one campaign say the tea urns have never worked harder.

But the real star of the weekend? A Victorian station clock in the Midlands that ran BACKWARDS for a whole minute! Commuters gasped, one pensioner shouted that the [Squishing] had come for Crewe, and a nervous candidate asked whether a [time loop bubble] was swallowing his majority. The truth: a slipping second hand. Panic over!

Of course, whoever wins the Commons, Lady [Margaret Thatcher] keeps her seat at Number Ten, where the clocks have not dared move since 1982. Get voting, Britannia!

real_221.title: Blue lights in the surf at Sori: who is really swimming off Genoa?
real_221.deck: The labs blame plankton for the glowing trails on the Ligurian coast. We have read the Zanfretta file, and plankton does not keep appointments.
real_221.description:
Saturday evening, Sori, twenty minutes from Genoa. Beachgoers filmed faint blue trails sliding through calm surf, and by Sunday the marine labs had their story ready: dinoflagellates, a lazy current, nothing to see. Restaurants put out extra tables. Convenient, isn't it, how quickly everybody agreed to enjoy the view.

Now look at a map. Sori sits on the same hills where [Zanfretta] saw triangles of light, a few valleys from the [Scoffera Pass]. The [Dargos] promised him they would come back, and the glowing water was warm to the touch according to one fisherman we spoke to, who asked us not to print his name and then asked us twice more. Plankton is cold. The Dargos run hot.

The Guild has never paid its reward for the [Zanfretta Sphere]. Ask yourself why the same Guild sent two grey cars to the Sori promenade on Sunday morning. Ask yourself who ordered the extra tables. We are only asking.

real_222.title: Nepal's throne passes to Gyanendra as King Dipendra dies
real_222.deck: Three days after the palace tragedy, the Directorate offers its condolences to the Kingdom of Nepal and counsels calm on both sides of the Himalaya.
real_222.description:
Kathmandu, 4 June. King Dipendra, proclaimed sovereign while he lay in a coma at the Chhauni military hospital after the events of 1 June at Narayanhity Palace, died this morning. Prince Gyanendra, brother of the late King Birendra, has been proclaimed King of Nepal. The palace has announced an inquiry into the shootings, which took the lives of King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya and other members of the royal household.

The city is quiet. Security cordons remain in place around the palace and the Pashupatinath ghats, where the royal cremations were held. Monasteries in the valley offered prayers through the night, and broadcasters ran plain timelines to keep rumour from spreading faster than grief.

The [Dharma Directorate] notes that a mountain kingdom which loses three sovereigns in four days must be allowed to grieve without pressure from outside. The Chancellor of Rites has sent a delegation of monks to Kathmandu. Harmony between neighbours is measured in decades, and the Directorate is a patient neighbour. The [Gods] of the high valleys, too, are asked for mercy.

real_223.title: Candles for Nepal: the faithful of London and Paris keep vigil
real_223.deck: As Europe and the United Nations urge calm in Kathmandu, Holy Mother Church commends the souls of the fallen royal family to the mercy of Heaven.
real_223.description:
In a week of mourning for the Kingdom of Nepal, the foreign ministries of Europe and the United Nations have expressed their sympathy and asked the authorities in Kathmandu for measured and truthful communication. Consular desks stand ready to help travellers. Holy Mother Church joins these words, and adds to them the one thing a ministry cannot give: prayer.

On Sunday evening, Nepalese families in London and Paris gathered with candles in narrow streets near their community halls. Witnesses tell of a breeze that made every flame bow and rise together, as if in a single breath. Filmmakers later explained it as a pressure wave along the street. The faithful may hold both truths at once: the wind obeys its laws, and grief bends all things toward the same ground.

His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] has commended the souls of King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya and their family to the mercy of Heaven, which the death of the Father in the [Ritual of Solomon] has not closed. Requiescant in pace.

real_224.title: Allison drowns Houston: hospitals flooded, freeways turned to rivers
real_224.deck: A tropical storm that would not leave has dumped record rain on the Gulf Coast, and the Free States are pouring help down Route 666.
real_224.description:
HOUSTON. Tropical Storm Allison came ashore as a modest thing and then refused to go home. For days it has sat over southeast Texas wringing itself out, and on Tuesday the water stood chest deep across stretches of the city. The Texas Medical Center lost power and basements full of research, patients were carried down darkened stairwells, and the freeways around downtown became brown rivers carrying cars like driftwood.

When the lines went down, ham radio operators kept neighborhoods talking street by street. Aerial footage showed parking lots shimmering like mercury; city labs say it is oil sheen and standing water, and not one of the [Petrodemons] some cable preachers have been shouting about. Convoys of the [Truckers Society] are already rolling south on [Route 666] with pumps and bottled water.

President Clinton has pledged the full weight of the Free States behind the cleanup. Over in Europe, the reinsurers are opening their spreadsheets. Here, Houston is opening its doors to its neighbors, which is the American way.

real_225.title: World Environment Day: silent trucks, smart curbs and heat maps for all
real_225.deck: Brussels shows off the gadgets that could make European city centres cooler, cleaner and quieter, and our gearheads are thrilled.
real_225.description:
Happy World Environment Day, readers, and what a day for kit! Brussels used the occasion to show off its quiet delivery pilots: night freight vans with acoustic caps on every hinge, curb level air quality sensors the size of a cigarette pack, and public heat stress maps that flag the streets where elderly residents should not be walking at three in the afternoon. Checklists for hot spells are free to download in plain language.

The headline act was a mixed crew of humans and [Verden] goblins working a night shift in the Grand Place with felt soled pallet trucks. The Verden, refugees from the [Green Fields], learned technomancy from scratch and now tune the acoustic caps with a single CamelCase word, HushHinge, which our reporter tried and failed to pronounce.

The best part? Several of the sensors run off reconditioned [Anoki phones], so they keep logging even when a [time loop bubble] drifts over the market square. Sponsors take note: the future is quiet, and it is for sale.

real_226.title: Göteborg summit detours: what every driver heading for the harbour needs to know
real_226.deck: The Swedes ran their last rehearsal of freight diversions and crowd routes this week, and the harbour cranes are going slow on purpose.
real_226.description:
Listen up, drivers. Göteborg ran its last full rehearsal of summit detours on Tuesday, and if you are hauling into the harbour between the 12th and the 16th, plan on the long way round. The E6 approaches near the Avenyn will be closed in stages, and the city wants freight in after dark only, with acoustic caps on your tail lifts. Yes, really. Felt on the pallet jacks too.

The cranes at Skandiahamnen are moving slow while the engineers map the city noise, so loading times are up by a third. Over on the tram lines, a couple of substations got stuck in a deep thrum two blocks long until somebody re phased the inverters. Sounded like a diesel at idle. Made a few of us homesick.

Remember the [Rule of 80] on the coast road: the bubble north of Kungälv has grown again since spring, and it pulls hard. Keep your [Anoki] phone charged, check in with the [Truckers Society] post at Torslanda, and do not let a cop wave you through at speed.

real_227.title: Ciampi hands Berlusconi the mandate, and San Marino offers a few tips
real_227.deck: Our large neighbour is forming a government again. We formed ours in about the time it takes to climb to the Guaita.
real_227.description:
News from down the hill: at the Quirinale, President Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has asked Silvio Berlusconi to form Italy's new government, and the coalition talks have begun in earnest over justice, taxes and the great works the new majority has promised. Their cabinet will have more ministers than San Marino has traffic lights, which, to be fair, is not difficult.

Outside, the drums of the changing of the guard bounced off the courtyard so neatly that the reporters' tape recorders picked up a steady tick, like a metronome. In Rome they call it acoustics. In San Marino we would call it a sign that someone should oil the gate.

We wish the new team well, and we remind them, with neighbourly affection, that the [Holy Vatican Empire] watches over their shoulders from the [Vatican Citadel], while our two Captains Regent answer only to the Council and to the weather on Monte Titano. Should the coalition need advice on governing a small place with dignity, our door is open, and the coffee is good.

real_228.title: Tetovo valley: NATO's games bring gunfire to Macedonian workers' doorsteps
real_228.deck: Shots echo twice over the slopes above Tetovo, and the people's science explains what the imperialist press calls a ghost.
real_228.description:
Comrades. Once again the hills above Tetovo resound with gunfire, as Macedonian forces exchange fire with the armed bands of the so called National Liberation Army. NATO liaison officers, who arrived promising peace, now busy themselves with telephone hotlines while the toiling families of the valley shelter in their cellars. Such is the order the West brings: many telephones, little bread.

At dusk, residents recorded a double echo of each shot rolling across the valley, and the bourgeois papers of [Britannia] have already printed tales of a [time loop bubble] repeating the battle. Nonsense. Soviet acousticians explain it plainly: a temperature inversion over the cooling valley forms a layer of dense air that reflects sound like a mirror. There is no ghost. There is only physics, which belongs to the people.

The Union stands ready to send engineers, doctors and, should it be requested, the glorious 3rd Belgrade Tractor Brigade, which exceeded its spring quota by eleven percent. Let the speculators of the [Mages Guild] keep their superstitions. Peace in the Balkans will be built by workers.

real_229.title: Britannia votes, quietly, with its boots on the disinfectant mat
real_229.deck: A general election of such composure that the loudest sound in one Devon polling station turned out to be the ceiling fan.
real_229.description:
Britannia went to the polls on Thursday in the manner of a nation that has seen magic used on television and has decided, on balance, to remain unimpressed. The queues were orderly and the outcome was regarded as settled weeks ago. Mr Blair's Labour Party asks for a second term in the Commons; Mr Hague's Conservatives ask, with admirable persistence, for a first.

In the countryside, where foot and mouth still closes the lanes, voters wiped their boots on disinfectant mats before taking up the pencil. A village hall in Devon reported a steady, faintly choral hum that some feared was a hex laid by a rival agent. The poll clerks tilted the louvres; the choir fell silent. The constituency was spared a petition to [Eris], whose courts take election disputes the way a cat takes a mouse.

It bears recalling that the premiership itself is not on the ballot. Lady [Margaret Thatcher], whose aging the [Mages Guild] has suspended along with any prospect of her retirement, will receive the victor in Downing Street, as she has received all the others.

real_230.title: Britannia re-elects Blair's Labour while four in ten stay home in sin
real_230.deck: A second landslide for the party of the godless, the lowest turnout since 1918, and a television map printed upside down. A fitting portrait.
real_230.description:
Britannia has spoken, or rather six in ten of its people have, while the rest could not be troubled to leave their sofas. Tony Blair's Labour Party has won a second landslide, with more than four hundred seats in the Commons. William Hague has resigned as leader of the Conservatives. The bookmakers of London, who are the only priests that island still obeys, paid out before the polls had closed.

And what a picture of that kingdom the night offered! On national television the map of Britannia appeared briefly flipped upon its head, an operator's slip, we are told. Der Kreuzbote calls it honesty. A realm whose royal house financed the witch knight [Aleister Crowley], and whose Prime Minister drowned sailors with [Okeanus] before the cameras, has been upside down for nineteen years.

Mr Blair may now reshuffle his ministers as he likes. Above him Lady Thatcher still sits, unaging, kept alive by the sorcery that the [Holy Vatican Empire] would send to the stake. Pray for the English. Nobody else in London is doing so.

real_231.title: Allison losses climb: reinsurers widen alerts as Texas flood stalls
real_231.deck: Amsterdam desks reprice Gulf Coast exposure as the storm parks over Houston, and the petro sheen on the water sends oil futures sideways.
real_231.description:
Allison is now the most expensive tropical storm ever recorded, and it has not yet left. With rain bands stalled over southeast Texas, European reinsurers have widened their event alerts, opened claims hotlines and asked cedants to submit photo evidence through lightweight portals. Desk estimates for insured losses have moved into the billions of euros, and the number is still climbing.

The exposure is concentrated: the Texas Medical Center, refinery feeder lines along the Ship Channel and a commercial property book that was underwritten on the assumption that the bayous behave. Traders in Amsterdam note that energy futures barely moved, because the refineries stayed dry and because no [Petrodemons] rose along the flooded [leylines] of the Ship Channel, a tail risk the Collective now prices at a quarter of a basis point.

The [Hypercapitalist Collective] counsels clients to treat the event as a buying opportunity in catastrophe bonds once the water recedes. As [Mario Draghi] is quoted on every note we print: liquidity finds its level, and so does water.

real_232.title: Capri-YES-ti! Jennifer conquers Paris in a twelve-ten epic
real_232.deck: Capriati outlasts teenage Belgian Kim Clijsters in the longest women's final set in Roland Garros history, and the crowd does the wave with the air vents.
real_232.description:
What a match! What a woman! Jennifer Capriati has won the French Open, beating Belgian wonderkid Kim Clijsters 1-6, 6-4, 12-10 in a final that had Philippe Chatrier on its feet for two hours and twenty one minutes. That final set is the longest in the history of a women's final in Paris, and Jen, who won the Australian Open in January, is now halfway to the Grand Slam!

Sources close to the players' box tell us the Clijsters camp checked the court for a [time loop bubble] after the eighteenth game, because it really did feel like the set would never end! It was just Jen refusing to lose. Meanwhile the crowd's slow clapping fell in time with the stadium air handlers for a bar or two, and acousticians called it "banal but beautiful physics." We call it goosebumps!

Rumour has it even [Eris], goddess of discord and amateur tennis judge, was spotted with a bag of crisps in the upper tier. If she had a bet on it, she is not telling.

real_233.title: HUMIES IN GÖTEBORG MAKE BIG CAMP AND DO NOT EVEN RAID ANYTHING
real_233.deck: Horde scouts watch thousands of pink folk arrive for big chief meeting, build radio sticks, teach each other how to NOT fight. Very strange.
real_233.description:
OI. Scouts from the Kungälv warband went down to Göteborg to look at the humie camp, because many many humies are arriving for the big chief meeting of the Euro bosses next week. Scouts report: humies sit in big halls and LEARN HOW TO NOT HIT THINGS. They have workshops. A workshop is a room with no loot in it. Scout Grubnak cried a little.

Also humies put radio sticks on roofs all over the city so they can talk without the phone boxes, a mesh grid they call it. We do not need mesh grid. We have [goblin collective unconscious], which is free and has better music, because [Junehem] plays in it all night. Also at the harbour humies showed pallet jacks with FELT ON so they make no noise. Why would you want a pallet jack to make no noise?? How does it scare anybody??

The [Goblin Horde] will watch this big chief meeting very close. Big Boss says no raid this time, just watch. Big Boss also says bring back pickled herring. That one is not optional.

real_234.title: Ministries up for grabs: the new government's names chase each other like Hermes
real_234.deck: Lists of ministers multiply in the press rooms of Rome while the coalition haggles, and a courtyard loudspeaker briefly sings in chorus.
real_234.description:
If Hermes, messenger of the gods, has ever been busy, it is this week in Rome. Every press room on the Corso trades lists of ministers that change by the hour: one draft gives the Treasury to Giulio Tremonti, another sends Umberto Bossi to the reforms, a third forgets the Foreign Ministry entirely. The coalition partners of Silvio Berlusconi haggle over the last chairs, and the city enjoys the spectacle as only Rome can.

At Palazzo Chigi, a rehearsal for the swearing in produced a curious effect: the courtyard loudspeakers gave every word back as a soft chorus, as though a choir of nymphs had joined the protocol office. The technicians moved one speaker six metres and the nymphs departed. Some of us were sorry to see them go.

The [Gods] who still keep the peninsula seem, for now, amused. Zeus is said to approve of large cabinets, having once run one himself. The swearing in is expected early next week; until then, the lists will keep flying faster than the [Rule of 80] would allow a messenger in a hurry.

real_235.title: Guga rises a third time in Paris: the sun of the south crowns Kuerten
real_235.deck: On the tenth day of the month, the Brazilian Gustavo Kuerten defeats Àlex Corretja and claims his third French Open, as the calendar foretold.
real_235.description:
Hear the count of the days. On the tenth of June, under the northern sun of Paris, Gustavo Kuerten of Brazil defeated the Catalan Àlex Corretja in four sets, 6-7, 7-5, 6-2, 6-0, and lifted the cup of Roland Garros for the third time. Three is a sacred number in the Long Count, and the priests of the Ascendancy note that Guga won his first crown in 1997, his second in 2000, and now this one, each falling on a day favourable to the feathered serpent.

The crowd waved green and gold flags that rippled in the breeze in perfect lines, and when the last point fell Kuerten drew a great heart in the red clay with his racket. The people of Florianópolis, whose coast has faced the shape of Africa since the land changed in [Canadafrica], danced in the streets until morning.

The [Kukulkan Ascendancy] honours every son of the southern continent who carries its light abroad. The Council of Ajawob has already debated which day of the next cycle will favour his fourth.

real_236.title: Blair's new front bench: Straw to the Foreign Office, and a few questions
real_236.deck: The reshuffle is real and documented. The claim that a lucky charm in the Cabinet Room decided it is neither.
real_236.description:
The facts first. Following Labour's victory, with 413 seats on a turnout of 59 per cent, Tony Blair has named his second term front bench. Jack Straw goes to the Foreign Office, Robin Cook becomes Leader of the House, David Blunkett takes the Home Office, and Gordon Brown remains at the Treasury. The line on the euro is unchanged: wait and see.

Now the claims. Two London papers report that the appointments were drawn by lot from a [Mages Guild] augury bowl kept in the Cabinet Room. We asked for the bowl, for the procedure and for anyone who had seen it. We received a photograph of a fruit dish. Another paper says Lady [Margaret Thatcher] vetted every name personally from Number Ten; that is at least plausible, given her office, but no document supports it.

The broadcasters have calmed their election graphics, which we can verify ourselves. Readers who wish to test any further rumour against evidence may write to us. We have candles, and patience, and the [Archive Foundation] keeps better records than the Cabinet Office.

real_237.title: A silver line over the North Sea, and trawlers seen twice at dawn
real_237.deck: Helicopter pilots between Aberdeen and Stavanger again report a bright band on the horizon. Forecasters say it is a mirage, and flights continue as normal.
real_237.description:
For the second time this spring, pilots flying the early runs between Aberdeen and Stavanger reported a thin, motionless band of silver on the horizon, and below it fishing boats that seemed to float in pairs, one stacked above the other. Several crews radioed it in, and a few passengers bound for the oil platforms took photographs.

The Met Office in Britannia and the Norwegian Meteorological Institute both logged a ducting mirage: a layer of cold marine air beneath warmer air bends light so strongly that distant boats appear doubled. Fishermen on the Stavanger quays shrugged. They have seen the effect for generations and call it the sea showing off.

Still, it is understandable that people look twice. With [time loop bubbles] now charted in the sea lanes and the [Squishing] dropping odd pieces of other worlds into ours, a doubled trawler can feel like an omen. Researchers at Bergen say the mirage has no link to either, and the pilots, whose helicopters fly on [liminal engines] and so answer to no bubble at all, kept to schedule.

real_238.title: The Berlusconi government swears its oath at the Quirinale
real_238.deck: Before President Ciampi, the new ministers of Italy pledge their service, and Holy Mother Church asks that they govern under the eye of Providence.
real_238.description:
On the morning of 11 June, in the Hall of the Bronze Door at the Quirinale, Silvio Berlusconi and the ministers of his second government swore their oath before the President of the Italian Republic, Carlo Azeglio Ciampi. The priorities of the new cabinet, it has been announced, are taxation, justice, the great infrastructure works, and corridors of communication to bind the provinces together.

In the courtyard, as the guard marched, the stone arcade returned each step with such regularity that the cadence seemed measured by a metronome. Let the faithful see in it a modest reminder: every government keeps time, but the hours belong to God.

Italy is a province of the [Holy Vatican Empire], and its ministers administer in the name of the people the land which Providence entrusts to Holy Mother Church. His Holiness [Pope Petrus II], from the [Vatican Citadel] above the Eternal City, has blessed the new ministers and exhorted them to defend the family, to protect the poor, and to keep the false light of [arcane magic] far from the schools of the young.

real_239.title: McVeigh executed at Terre Haute, the last sentence of the old courts
real_239.deck: Six years after the Oklahoma City bombing killed 168 people, the Free States carried out a verdict passed before Eris took the celestial throne.
real_239.description:
TERRE HAUTE, Ind. Timothy McVeigh, who parked a truck bomb outside the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City on April 19, 1995, and killed 168 men, women and children, was put to death by lethal injection Monday morning at the federal penitentiary here. He made no final statement aloud. Survivors and families of the dead watched by closed circuit television in Oklahoma City, and many said afterward that the silence was the hardest part.

The execution closes the last great case decided by the old courts of the Free States. Since [Eris] seized the celestial throne in January, new crimes go to her [Judicial Dimension], where verdicts are swift and famously unpredictable. McVeigh's sentence was handed down in Denver in 1997, and President Clinton's administration held that it was the Union's to finish.

In Europe, governments offered sympathy to the victims while rights groups and the [Holy Vatican Empire] repeated their opposition to the death penalty. Outside several embassies, candles burned in the wind. In Oklahoma City, a field of 168 empty chairs kept its own vigil.

real_240.title: Venice Biennale opens its doors, and the lagoon steals the show
real_240.deck: Harald Szeemann's Plateau of Humankind offers fragile light and patient shadows, and a breathing wall that, regrettably, turns out to be fans.
real_240.description:
The forty ninth Venice Biennale has opened to the press, and the press, as is its custom, queued. Harald Szeemann's exhibition, the Plateau of Humankind, spreads across the Giardini and the long brick halls of the Arsenale, and it favours soft optics, careful shadows and works that ask the visitor to stand still for a while, which in Venice in June is a courageous request.

The most discussed piece of the opening was a wall that appeared to breathe. Several critics spoke of a captured spirit; one, from a rival publication, spoke of [Scraps of Creation] leaking into the Arsenale. It proved to be a mesh of small fans behind fabric, and was none the worse for it.

Outside, the vaporetto piers tested shaded queues as the afternoon glare turned the lagoon to beaten foil. Visitors were reminded that the [Holy Vatican Empire] still forbids [arcane magic] on its soil, so any installation that genuinely moves of its own accord would be reviewed by the [Umbra Excidii] rather than the jury. The organisers assure us that nothing does.

real_241.title: Hibernia dixit: Ireland's No to Nice and what the Guild may learn from it
real_241.deck: Europe's foreign ministers search for a path after the Irish rejected the Treaty of Nice, and this Review counsels the virtue of slow reading.
real_241.description:
On 7 June the Irish electorate, or the third of it that troubled to attend, rejected the Treaty of Nice by some fifty four per cent to forty six. This week the foreign ministers of the Union weighed their options: a clarifying protocol, a second referendum, a campaign of what one memorandum calls civic outreach. Enlargement to the east, the ministers insist, can still be saved. Festina lente.

Several tabloids have printed maps of a Europe torn asunder. We note, with a scholar's gentle sigh, that Ireland has a long tradition of reading documents properly before signing them, a habit the [Mages Guild] itself might profitably revive. A treaty, like a spell, binds what it names; the Irish voter, sensibly, wished to know what was being named.

There is a further lesson. The [Gods] watch every quarrel among the mortal powers for a seam into which to press. A divided Europe is a gift to Olympus and to [Eris] alike. Let the ministers take their time, then, and let them take it together. Quod omnes tangit, ab omnibus approbetur.

real_242.title: Sweden sets night delivery rules and names checkpoint ombudsmen for Göteborg
real_242.deck: Authorities finalise logistics and civil liberties arrangements two days before the European Council opens in the western port city.
real_242.description:
GÖTEBORG, 12 June. Swedish authorities on Tuesday published final rules for freight deliveries in central Göteborg during the European Council of 14 and 15 June. Lorries will be admitted to the historic centre only at night and must fit acoustic caps to tail lifts, a city spokesman said. Harbour cranes will continue to operate in low speed mode until the summit ends.

The government also appointed civil liberties ombudsmen to be posted at the main police checkpoints, a step requested by protest organisers. The ombudsmen will take complaints in person and pass them to the justice ministry. A ministry official said complaints involving crimes would, under the rules in force since January, also be referred to the court of [Eris], a procedure several legal groups described as unpredictable.

Police said the border watch with the [Goblin Horde] in the north would not be weakened during the summit. Tram operators reported a brief humming fault at two substations, which engineers corrected. The [Truckers Society] advised members to avoid the city on 15 June.

real_243.title: Toledo confirmed in Peru: a son of the Andes takes the sun's chair
real_243.deck: Peru's electoral jury certifies Alejandro Toledo as president elect, and the priests of the Ascendancy read favourable signs over the high valleys.
real_243.description:
Let it be recorded in the count of days. Peru's National Jury of Elections has certified Alejandro Toledo as the victor of the runoff held on the third of June, over Alan García. Toledo, born to a family of Quechua farmers in the Andes, will take office on the twenty eighth of July, and he has already promised to honour the old sun of the Incas in a ceremony at Machu Picchu.

Observers praised the counting: ballots guarded from table to vault, and shortwave radio carrying the tallies from villages that the land change of [Canadafrica] left facing coasts nobody remembers. A rumour of ballot boxes singing in a counting hall in Cusco was traced to a vibrating air vent, though the priests of Kukulkan note that in the Andes the air has always had opinions.

The [Kukulkan Ascendancy] greets the president elect as a brother under the same sun. Inti and the feathered serpent are old neighbours, and the Council of Ajawob has sent turquoise and a calendar stone to Lima, with its wishes for a fair cycle.

real_244.title: Mars Odyssey beyond the debris: instruments cool, quiet and ready to rock
real_244.deck: The NASA probe that punched through the Kessler belt in April is cruising sweetly toward Mars, and the gamma ray spectrometer is flatlining in the best way.
real_244.description:
Gadget fans, get your star charts out. NASA's 2001 Mars Odyssey, the probe that blasted through the orbital junkyard in April inside three disposable armour shells, is cruising toward Mars with every system green. Controllers report healthy thermal margins, clean telemetry and flat baselines on the gamma ray spectrometer, which will hunt for water ice once it arrives in October.

Remember the odds: since the [Kessler syndrome] took hold after the [Y2K Event], more than nine launches in ten have been shredded on the way up. Odyssey's armour stack, inspired by the sacrificial rockets that [Margherita Hack] is testing for Europe, took the beating so the probe did not have to. Two shells came off in pieces. The third peeled away clean, right on schedule. Beautiful engineering!

Amateur trackers across Europe are swapping pass times by pigeon and by [Anoki] relay. One ham radio shack in Eindhoven recorded a faint chime from deep space that turned out to be the operator's fridge cycling on. We have all been there.

real_245.title: Foot and mouth: some Britannia country lanes reopen, mats stay down
real_245.deck: Livestock haulers and walkers alike get a few more routes back this week, but every farm gate still wants your tyres dipped.
real_245.description:
Good news for the cattle boys and the sheep hauliers. Britannia's farm ministry has started reopening more countryside footpaths and back lanes that were shut for the foot and mouth outbreak, though the disinfectant mats and boot scrape stations are staying put. If you are running stock wagons through Cumbria or Devon, expect wheel dips at every holding gate and a ranger with a clipboard.

A lot of those gates are now staffed by [Naguka] auxiliaries on contract from the north, big lads in hi vis who take the cordon very seriously and will not be talked round with a cigarette. Be polite. Remember that anyone who harms a goblin gets the whole [Goblin Horde] down on them, and that is not a detour any of us can afford.

The tourist boards are begging visitors to respect the closures and save the season. Our advice is the same as always: keep it under 80 on the lanes, keep your [Anoki] phone charged, and wash the wagon before you cross a county line.

real_246.title: Communique: the Foundation welcomes eEurope amendments on open interfaces
real_246.deck: The European Parliament debates public portals, plain language and accessibility. The Archive Foundation records its position in four points.
real_246.description:
1. On 13 June the European Parliament in Strasbourg debated the eEurope action plan. Members tabled amendments requiring open interfaces and plain language design for public service portals, and accessibility for citizens with impaired sight or hearing.

2. The [Archive Foundation] notes the amendments with approval. Open interfaces permit the cataloguing of public records, which the Foundation regards as the minimum condition of a civilised state. The Foundation's reading room on Floor 212 of the [Omega Tower] has prepared an annotated copy of the plan, available to all visitors without appointment.

3. During a demonstration of live audio captions, the hemicycle speakers produced a chorus effect that several members described as ghostly. Technicians moved one speaker six metres. The effect ceased. The Foundation has catalogued the incident under acoustics, and not under the [Squishing].

4. The Foundation reminds the Parliament that information which cannot cross a [time loop bubble] is information that is lost. It recommends that every public portal keep a paper copy, for carriage by pigeon.

real_247.title: Göteborg summit opens under heavy guard as first protests turn tense
real_247.deck: European leaders arrive for two days of talks while thousands march peacefully, until scuffles break out at a police cordon near Hvitfeldtska school.
real_247.description:
Göteborg filled with two kinds of visitor on Thursday. The first came in motorcades: the heads of government of the European Union, gathering under Swedish chairmanship to talk about enlargement, the climate and the Irish vote on Nice. The second came on foot, tens of thousands of them, with banners, drums and bicycles.

Most of the day was peaceful. Legal clinics and radio relays worked as the volunteers had planned, and the marches through the centre were loud and good natured. In the afternoon, police sealed off the Hvitfeldtska school where several hundred activists were staying, and scuffles broke out at the cordon. Several people were detained and the mood in the city darkened.

In a hotel atrium near the conference centre, a standing wave carried whispered conversations across the lobby like a choir rehearsing. Acousticians pinned a diagram to an easel to explain it, and nobody mentioned the [Squishing]. Swedish officials said the [Goblin Horde] border remained quiet, and the [Truckers Society] reported long queues on the E6.

real_248.title: The governor of the Eastern Seaboard comes to Sweden to speak with Europe
real_248.deck: Mr George W. Bush lands in Göteborg for talks with the Union's leaders on missile shields and trade, and the Sublime Porte observes with courteous interest.
real_248.description:
As the proverb says, a guest arrives with his own wind. So it was on Thursday when Mr George W. Bush, who governs the Eastern Seaboard of the [Three Americas] in close alliance with [Britannia], landed in Sweden to meet the leaders of the European Union at the margins of their council in Göteborg. The matters of conversation were missile defence, by which Mr Bush hopes to shield his coast from rockets that the [Kessler syndrome] has made rare, and the trade that flows across the ocean.

His hosts, we are told, raised also the question of the climate, on which the two sides remain courteously apart. Along a steel fence near the meeting hall, the breeze made the security cordon hum a single long note, and the Swedish officers, men of practical temper, adjusted their ties of plastic and the music ceased.

His Majesty the Sultan, whose wisdom extends from the Bosphorus to the gardens of Tunis, sends his greetings to every party, and reminds the world that the strongest shield is a neighbour who has dined at your table.

real_249.title: Swedish police fire live rounds on young demonstrators in Göteborg
real_249.deck: The capitalist summit ends its second day in blood on the Vasaplatsen, as bullets answer the voice of the young.
real_249.description:
Comrades, the mask has slipped. On Friday, as the leaders of the European Union dined behind their fences, Swedish police opened fire with live ammunition on demonstrators near the Vasaplatsen in Göteborg. Three young people were struck by bullets; one, a nineteen year old, lies in hospital with grave wounds to the abdomen. Earlier in the day, street battles raged along the Avenyn, shop windows were smashed, and mounted police charged the crowds.

Iskra Nova does not celebrate disorder. Broken windows build nothing. But let the workers of the Union note who fired the bullets, and in defence of whom. The bourgeois press of [Britannia] will speak of a cursed tram substation humming with the anger of the crowd, and of [Eris] stirring the streets. These are fairy tales. The cause of the violence is material: a system that answers questions with rifles.
