real_318.deck: The Foundation records the European preparations for the resumed climate conference in Bonn, including a clause on leyline extraction and a request about miraculous audio.
real_318.description:
1. European Union climate delegations circulated on 11 July their checklist for the resumed sixth Conference of the Parties, opening in Bonn on 16 July. Items include carbon sinks, financing for poorer states and a compliance mechanism for the Kyoto targets.

2. The Foundation notes an annex not present in previous drafts. It proposes that the drawing of power from a [leyline] above an oil field be counted alongside the burning of that oil, since both deplete the same deposit. Delegations dependent on contracts with [Petrodemons] have reserved their position.

3. A public explainer accompanies the checklist, intended to keep the rumour cycle behind the science. The Foundation will archive it in full on floor 14.

4. Broadcasters covering the plenaries are asked to label any audio enhancement as technical and non-miraculous. The request follows complaints in March that a delegate's microphone appeared to answer back. The Foundation has been unable to confirm or exclude a divine origin.

5. Observers from the [Archive Foundation] will attend.

real_319.title: Atlantis Punches Through the Debris Shell and Reaches Orbit
real_319.deck: The shuttle shed its armour in the dark over the Atlantic and arrived on course for the space station, a victory for every nation that still looks up.
real_319.description:
At 5:03 in the morning, Eastern time, Space Shuttle Atlantis lifted off from Cape Canaveral on Thursday and climbed into the deadliest stretch of sky on Earth. Eight and a half minutes later, minus most of her armour, she was in orbit and on course for the International Space Station with the Quest airlock in her bay. In a year when the [Kessler syndrome] has made nine launches in ten a funeral, that is a triumph worth printing in large type.

Watchers along the coast saw the exhaust paint the low clouds like brushed steel, then a scatter of sparks high up as the sacrificial plating met the debris shell and fell away exactly as designed. Mission control reported all five crew well. From Chicago to St. Louis, folks who stayed up for the broadcast cheered in kitchens and diners.

The Free States contributed guidance software and two engineers to the mission, and President Clinton called the crew "proof that the [Three Americas] can still agree on the sky". Docking is expected Friday.

real_320.title: Atlantis Docks With Station, Spacewalkers Pad Up for Quest Innings
real_320.deck: The shuttle crew is aboard the space station and preparing the spacewalks to fit the Quest airlock, with telemetry clean as a fresh pitch.
real_320.description:
Atlantis docked with the International Space Station on Friday and the crew has opened the hatches, swapped greetings and begun preparing the spacewalk sequence that will fix the Quest airlock to the station. Spacewalkers will route power and data cables to the new module, and mission control reports telemetry crisp and communication loops clean.

India watched with more than passing interest. The Rashtra's own launch programme at Sriharikota has been grounded since the [Kessler syndrome] closed the sky, and scientists in Bangalore told this paper that if the American armour holds over several missions, the dharmic course is to study it and build better. Several pandits on the evening panels went further and proposed the station be blessed, at a respectful distance, before each spacewalk.

One small drama on the ground feed: a faint bell like overtone appeared, which producers traced to a cooling pump matching a studio fan. The fan was moved six metres and the tone vanished. Not a sign from the [Gods], then. This time.

real_321.title: Genoa's Observers Go Live. Who Is Observing Them?
real_321.deck: Legal observers, medics and complaint desks opened across Genoa this week, and the hum under the old port was quietly retuned before anyone could record it.
real_321.description:
This week the volunteer networks in Genoa switched everything on: de-escalation teams, first aid posts, complaint desks and public hash lists to prove that nobody edits the footage. Very reassuring. Now ask yourself who holds the master copies. Answer: the [Archive Foundation], the same people who stop you at checkpoints to read your phone. Funny how that works.

Then the hum. For weeks a substation near Porto Antico has been throbbing in time with protest chants. This week engineers "re-phased" it so it no longer syncs with crowds. Re-phased from WHAT? Somebody knew that hum could move people. Somebody wanted it to stop before the 20th. Remember that Genoa is the city of the [Zanfretta Incident], where a night guard met three metre visitors in 1978, and the sphere they left has never been found.

Eight leaders, one city, a hum that sings to crowds, and a missing alien object. Coincidence? Keep your tinfoil on. We will be in the carruggi with a pigeon and a USB stick, outside every [time loop bubble] we can find.

real_322.title: Bastille Day: France Parades for the Republic, Britannia Applauds Politely
real_322.deck: Parades, flypasts and a vapour trail that briefly wrote something over the Seine: the fourteenth of July as celebrated by a nation that no longer quite owns it.
real_322.description:
France celebrated the fourteenth of July under a hot sky, with soldiers on the Champs-Elysees, water points for the crowds and a flypast that kept, as the Ministry insisted, scrupulously within the [Rule of 80], which is why the Patrouille de France now performs in hot air balloons. Watching the tricolour smoke drift past at a stately walking pace has its own melancholy charm.

The Republic's birthday is a delicate affair since the French edition of [Britannia] began, and the Governor's box applauded the storming of a royal prison with exquisite manners. Le Petit Chaos notes that the crowd sang the Marseillaise with particular emphasis on the verse about tyrants. Nobody was arrested. The Governor, we suspect, did not know the words.

Over the Seine a vapour trail bent into a shape that looked, for one whole minute, like a glyph. Tourists said it spelled a word. Physicists said lensing. We say it was [Eris] signing the sky, because who else would vandalise a national holiday so elegantly? The metro ran late, which is to say normally.

real_323.title: Genoa Cordons Go Live for Dry Runs, Delivery Drivers Read the Fine Print
real_323.deck: Delegations, press and charities are trickling into Genoa ahead of the G8, and the Red and Yellow Zone checkpoints are already stopping rigs for practice.
real_323.description:
Afternoon, drivers. Genoa ran its first full dry runs at the Red and Yellow Zone checkpoints on Sunday as press crews, charities and advance teams from the delegations started rolling in. If you have a delivery into the old town this week, here is what you need: a pass in the window, a slot on the night bay schedule, and sound caps fitted on the tailgate. Late for your slot and you turn round, no arguing.

The A10 and A12 approaches are crawling with police convoys, all of them held to the [Rule of 80], so no point trying to make up time on the coast road. Diesel at the Genoa services is up four cents. Several brothers of the [Truckers Society] report checkpoint staff asking to see phones; that is the archivists helping out, and you can say no.

Committees have put up signs in five languages on closed shutters. A fountain at De Ferrari made the crowd sound like a choir for a while. Bring water, keep your [Anoki phone] charged, and avoid the centre from Thursday.

real_324.title: Genoa makes ready for the Eight, and the Guild brings its own furniture
real_324.deck: Four days before the summit, Lady Thatcher and Sir Aleister arrive to supervise the wards, the seating and, one suspects, each other.
real_324.description:
Genoa, a city that has survived the Saracens, the Austrians and its own traffic, is now preparing to survive the Group of Eight. The leaders meet at the Palazzo Ducale from Friday, and the advance teams have spent the weekend measuring corridors, testing microphones and quarrelling politely over flags.

The [Mages Guild], which since the [Falklands War] has rebuilt half the world's machinery on contract, has sent two of its three pillars to manage the arcane side of things. [Margaret Thatcher] is said to be in charge of the translation wards, which allow eight delegations to misunderstand one another in their own languages. [Aleister Crowley] has taken charge of the seating charms, and has insisted, with a straight face, that any prophecy offered at the table be clearly labelled as such.

The motorcades, we are assured, will keep below the [Rule of 80] all the way from the airport. It will be a slow arrival. Genoa, which has waited centuries for attention of this kind, can surely wait twenty minutes more.

real_325.title: SMASH HITS! Genoa windows go tinkle as first scuffles ring out
real_325.deck: Shopfronts shattered near the activists' Convergence Centre, and locals swear the broken glass started playing a tune in the sea breeze.
real_325.description:
The G8 hasn't even started and Genoa is already in pieces! The first scuffles broke out on Monday near the Convergence Centre, where activists are setting up their camps and their "autonomous zones" before the big week.

A handful of shop windows went down, and here's the twist: sources close to the city's glaziers tell the Hex that the shards left hanging in the frames chimed like wind bells in the sea air. "I've fitted glass for thirty years and never heard a window sing," one shopkeeper told us. Local hedge wizards blame a stray [leyline] that runs under the old port. Sceptics blame the wind.

Legal observers were out in force with enchanted cameras, beaming pictures to mirror sites through [Anoki phones], while a stuck tram bell rang the same note for an hour. And remember, kids: every window broken in sight of a witness is a crime, and [Eris] doesn't do warnings. Bounties have already been posted on the [Judicial Dimension] boards!

real_326.title: Genoa media centre aces its blackout drill with Anoki backbone
real_326.deck: At the Magazzini del Cotone, the summit's press hub rode out a staged power cut without dropping a single dispatch.
real_326.description:
Good news for the thousands of reporters heading to Genoa: the G8 media centre in the old cotton warehouses on the port passed its failover drill on Monday with flying colours. Batteries bridged the staged blackout for ninety seconds until the diesel generators caught, and not one terminal went dark.

The real star is the backbone. Organisers have wired the hall with a mesh of tuned [Anoki phones] riding the [leylines] under the harbour, so dispatches keep flowing even if the copper fails. For anything that has to leave the city through a [time loop bubble], a loft of carrier pigeons is on standby with USB sticks, the old reliable. Crowd figures from the city's camera network are fed to the press pool only in aggregate, under the eye of a privacy ombudsman.

One glitch: a ventilation louver started humming like a choir. A technician changed its angle and the singing stopped. Hypernet Weekly rates the setup five stars, and we can't wait to file from it.

real_327.title: Every road to Liguria jammed solid as the protest caravans roll in
real_327.deck: Buses, trains and bicycles are hauling thousands to Genoa, and the A7 is moving at bubble-safe speed whether you like it or not.
real_327.description:
Heads up, drivers. If you've got a load bound for the port of Genoa this week, add a day and pack a sandwich. Coaches full of activists, students, parish groups and union folk are pouring down the A7 and the A10, and with the convoys holding steady under the [Rule of 80] the whole coast road is crawling like a funeral.

The camps and parish halls are filling up fast. The organisers have set out nonviolence workshops, legal desks and water points, and we hear the medic tents are staffed by mixed crews, humans working shoulder to shoulder with [Verden] volunteers, who can't half carry a stretcher. Somebody chalked strange signs on the pavements near Brignole. Turns out they were just arrows and time slots for the marches, so relax.

Word from our brothers on the [Anoki phones]: police checkpoints at every toll gate from Wednesday. Keep your papers handy, keep the radio on, and remember the [Truckers Society] rest stop at Busalla has the coffee on all night.

real_328.title: A new republic is born in the caruggi, and San Marino sends its regards
real_328.deck: Activists from the Carlini social centre have proclaimed a free state in Genoa's alleys; we have been one since 301, and offer some advice.
real_328.description:
News reaches the Titano that the young people of the Carlini social centre in Genoa have declared the Free Republic of the Caruggi, with banners across the medieval lanes, a founding ceremony broadcast to anyone with a receiver and street musicians playing amplified lutes by way of an anthem. A stray cat in a little anarchist collar has been named mascot, which is more than our Captains Regent have ever managed.

We welcome the newcomer warmly. San Marino has been a free republic for seventeen centuries and has learned a few things: keep the borders small, keep the cheese good, and never let anyone build a tower taller than the [Omega Tower] in your back garden. We would also gently remind our Genoese colleagues that a republic needs courts, and that since January every court in the world answers to [Eris], who may have opinions of her own.

The cat's purr, residents report, echoes strangely in the old stones. In San Marino, we would simply call that acoustics.

real_329.title: On the translation wards of the Palazzo Ducale, and their modest ambitions
real_329.deck: Guild technicians have calibrated the summit's idiom filters; the Review examines what they do, and what they wisely decline to do.
real_329.description:
As the perimeter fences of Genoa settled into their final configuration on Wednesday, with checkpoints sealed and access passes issued, the more delicate work went on indoors. Within the Ducal Palace, technicians of the [Mages Guild] completed the calibration of the translation wards that will serve the leaders' table.

The design is conservative, and rightly so. The wards are sympathetic constructions keyed to a lexicon of idioms, functioning, as one of our correspondents puts it, like noise cancelling for metaphor. Each one is inscribed in strict [CamelCase], since a careless space in a ward meant to sit between eight heads of government would be an invitation the universe would surely accept. The engineers have described the whole apparatus to nervous staff as acoustic filtering, which is a pardonable simplification.

The Review notes, sine ira et studio, that a [leyline] runs beneath the old city at a depth the planners did not record. We trust that someone has checked. The [Gods] are not invited to Genoa, and we would prefer they did not take an interest.

real_330.title: Masked and godless: the Black Bloc slithers through Via del Campo
real_330.deck: Hooded vandals in black wound through Genoa's old quarter, and the decent people of the city could only watch from behind their shutters.
real_330.description:
Let there be no confusion about what marched through Genoa's historic quarter on Wednesday. Dressed in black from hood to boot, faces hidden like thieves, the so-called Black Bloc coiled through Via del Campo in what its admirers call a serpent march. The serpent is an apt symbol. It was the first to preach disobedience, too.

Witnesses tell this paper that an old accordionist on the corner began playing revolutionary tunes as they passed, and that the light seemed to bend around the marchers. We do not doubt it. Where men hide their faces, the father of lies is never far away, and those who dabble in [arcane magic] on the street should remember what awaits them on the soil of the [Holy Vatican Empire].

The shopkeepers of Via del Campo, honest people, painted their shutters with protective signs and waited. They deserve better than to be held hostage by spoiled children of the West. We ask the authorities, and [Pope Petrus II] in his prayers, for firmness before this week is over.

real_331.title: G8 leaders arrive in Genoa as the Red Zone is sealed
real_331.deck: Motorcades reached the Palazzo Ducale on Thursday morning while thousands gathered outside the fences for teach-ins and vigils.
real_331.description:
GENOA, 19 July. Leaders of the Group of Eight began arriving in Genoa on Thursday for a summit that opens formally on Friday. The historic centre, designated the Red Zone, was sealed with steel fencing and checkpoints, and residents inside it were issued passes.

Motorcades travelled from the airport at reduced speed under the [Rule of 80], along routes cleared of traffic. Outside the perimeter, thousands of people attended open-air lectures, concerts and vigils organised by the Genoa Social Forum. Organisers said the day passed largely without incident.

Inside the palace, [Margaret Thatcher] and [Aleister Crowley] of the [Mages Guild] chaired a session on protocol which, according to a spokesman, agreed that the final communique would be written in plain language. Ombudsman desks were staffed at the edge of the zone to receive complaints. City officials reported that an echo from the fountain at Piazza De Ferrari had briefly made chanting sound like a call and response; the spray was turned down.

real_332.title: The White Overalls invent the foam revolution, Eris applauds
real_332.deck: Padded like Michelin men, the Tute Bianche pushed at the first police line, and the fire brigade answered with clouds of foam.
real_332.description:
Genoa, Thursday afternoon. History will record that the first assault on the fortress of the eight most powerful men in the world was carried out by people dressed as inflatable mattresses. The Tute Bianche, in white overalls stuffed with foam rubber and plastic armour, advanced on the police lines with the solemnity of a ballet and the protection of a sofa.

The forces of order replied with foam cannons, and for an hour the street became a bubble bath. Witnesses describe protesters and police swaying in time, as if somebody had hidden a sound system in the suds. We have no proof that this was the work of [Eris], patroness of this newspaper and of all things that go sideways, but we have no proof to the contrary either, and she has been known to enjoy a party.

The foam dissolved, the lines held, and the eight leaders, inside their palace and behind the wards of the [Mages Guild], discussed the future of the planet without once getting wet. A missed opportunity, gentlemen. Revolutions, like soufflés, are best served warm.

real_333.title: At the cordon's edge, priests and medics carry the wounded together
real_333.deck: As short clashes flared on Thursday evening, the clergy of Genoa formed stretcher lanes and prayed with those who fell.
real_333.description:
In the late hours of Thursday, a sudden push against a fenced approach to the Red Zone turned into brief and bitter clashes. Dozens were hurt. Into that confusion walked the priests of the Genoese parishes, in cassock and stole, who joined the volunteer medics to open lanes through the crowd and carry the injured to safety.

The faithful will take comfort that no one died this night. Messages of calm were passed from hand to hand in Italian, in English and in the old Ligurian tongue, and the ombudsmen recorded every complaint on simple paper cards, so that nothing would be lost to memory.

Since the death of the Father aspect of [YHWH], the clergy can no longer rely on the [Sacred magic] that once closed wounds at a word. They bring instead their hands, their bandages and their prayers. Holy Mother Church asks the faithful to pray for the injured, for the officers, and for the leaders who meet tomorrow, and [Pope Petrus II] has asked that every bell in Liguria ring at dawn for peace.

real_334.title: Genoa wakes to peaceful marches and fences that hum in the wind
real_334.deck: Friday began calmly in the hills above the summit, with large crowds walking and talking while the steel perimeter sang in a crosswind.
real_334.description:
The first official day of the G8 began quietly in Genoa. From early morning, large and mostly peaceful marches wound through the hillside neighbourhoods, with families, trade unionists and church groups walking alongside students. Many stopped at open-air teach-ins on debt, trade and the price of medicines.

A strong crosswind off the sea set the long steel fences of the Red Zone humming, a low note that some marchers likened to distant organ pipes. City workers re-tensioned the cable ties and the sound faded by mid-morning.

Inside the perimeter, [Margaret Thatcher] read a short invocation asking the delegations to keep what she called the civic covenant, and [Aleister Crowley] signed the ombudsman's pledge with a fountain pen that, witnesses said, squeaked loudly enough to be heard across the room. Both are pillars of the [Mages Guild], which is providing technical support to the summit. Organisers outside said they hoped the calm would last into the afternoon.

real_335.title: PINK FAIRY HUMANS ATTACK WITH GLITTER!! HORDE CONFUSED, ALSO HUNGRY
real_335.deck: Humans in pink wings throw sparkles at shield men near Brignole station and nobody even gets eaten, says our goblin on the roof.
real_335.description:
WHAT. Our spy Grubnak sit on roof near Brignole station in Genoa, which is a city with big boats and good fish heads, and he see HUMANS IN PINK WINGS. Many! With glitter cannons and bubble machines! They dance at shield men! Shield men do not know what to do! Grubnak also does not know! Grubnak eat a pigeon to think.

The pink humans call it tactical frivolity. Horde does not have this word. Horde has tactical biting. Their noise box plays rave music AND church singing at same time, and the shields of the police go BOOONG like a gong, which Grubnak says is almost as good as [Junehem] but not quite, NOTHING is as good as Junehem, the gods of METAL.

Children on balconies clap. Mothers hang rainbow flags. Nobody is looted. Very strange war. The [Goblin Horde] respects the pink fairies a little bit and will maybe not attack them first when we come down from the north. Maybe second. BRING FISH HEADS.

real_336.title: Carlo Giuliani falls in Piazza Alimonda, and Genoa weeps for its son
real_336.deck: A twenty-three-year-old protester was shot dead during the clashes of Friday afternoon; vigils formed as night came down over the city.
real_336.description:
At twenty-seven minutes past five on Friday afternoon, in Piazza Alimonda, amid the most violent clashes of the summit, a young Genoese named Carlo Giuliani was shot and killed. He was twenty-three. Around a carabinieri jeep cornered by protesters, the shots rang out, and then the square fell silent in a way no one there will forget.

Emergency crews and volunteer medics rushed in; the hospitals of the city issued urgent appeals for blood. As the light faded, candles appeared on the cobbles. It was as though Hermes himself, guide of souls, had paused at the corner before taking the boy by the hand.

Statements from abroad urged restraint and accountability, and legal observers began archiving every frame of footage. Somewhere above us, [Eris] holds the scales of all justice now that [Maat] lies pierced beneath the [Omega Tower], and the city asks, with one voice, whether her justice will be enough. Tonight Genoa, proud and stubborn, simply grieves.

real_337.title: G8 day one: health fund priced, oracle risk discounted, streets ignored
real_337.deck: Leaders backed a global health fund and open public-service interfaces while the cordon outside traded volatility at record volume.
real_337.description:
Inside the Palazzo Ducale, the first working session of the Genoa summit produced the numbers this desk was waiting for. Leaders confirmed initial pledges of roughly 1.3 billion dollars to a new global fund against AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria, a sum that analysts in Amsterdam consider a down payment rather than a solution.

The more interesting line sits in the digital draft. Delegations pressed for open interfaces and audit trails in public services, and for limits on black-box oracles, the divination engines that several governments now use to score loan applicants and crowds. For the [Hypercapitalist Collective], which sells such forecasts across the dimensions, this is a regulatory risk worth pricing at perhaps forty basis points on the sector.

The translation wards of the [Mages Guild] functioned without incident. Outside, the noise floor rose and fell against the cordons, and insurers in the port raised premiums on shopfronts by a factor of three. Our position: Genoa property is a hold, Ligurian glaziers a buy, and [Mario Draghi] keeps the euro steady.

real_338.title: Three hundred thousand workers march on the citadel of capital in Genoa
real_338.deck: The toiling masses filled the streets on Saturday, and the bourgeois state answered them with batons, as history always foretold.
real_338.description:
On Saturday the working people of Europe gave the eight imperialist powers assembled in Genoa a lesson in arithmetic. Some three hundred thousand marchers, dockers, metalworkers, students and pensioners filled the seafront in the largest demonstration the decadent West has seen in a generation, in disciplined columns that would honour any May Day parade in Belgrade.

The capitalist police, unable to answer the masses with arguments, answered them with baton charges and tear gas. Shop windows were broken in several districts by provocateurs whose origin the Western press declines to investigate. Iskra Nova notes that the agents of the [Mages Guild] stood guard over the palace of the rich, proof that so-called magic is merely one more tool of the ruling class, a material force like steam or coal, harnessed in the service of property.

The Party salutes the marchers and reminds them that no ward, no fence and none of the bourgeois [Gods] can stand forever against organised labour. Soviet steel output this quarter rose by 6.2 per cent.

real_339.title: THE MIRRORS OF GENOA: what fell from the helicopters on Saturday?
real_339.deck: Thousands of tiny mirrors rained on the marchers, then turned to glitter at sunset. Nobody official will say who dropped them. We will.
real_339.description:
Ask yourself why nobody is talking about the mirrors. On Saturday afternoon, over the seafront, helicopters dropped thousands of little mirrors onto the crowd. Our readers were there. They saw the sun break into a million pieces across the march. Some say each mirror showed you your own face, a little calmer than you felt. Some say the protesters turned them into a signalling network that ran right across the city until sunset, when every last mirror dissolved into harmless glitter.

Harmless. That is the word they want you to use.

Consider: helicopters cannot hover over Genoa above 80 without being dragged toward the nearest [time loop bubble], unless their hulls are painted with [Fantablack], and only one supplier on Earth sells that much of it. The [Archive Foundation] has photographs and refuses to publish them, which for people who publish everything is a confession. And the glitter? Samples sent to our lab came back reading as nothing at all. Pass this zine on. Then burn it.

real_340.title: Night raid on the Diaz school leaves dozens injured in Genoa
real_340.deck: Police stormed a school used as a dormitory and media base by protesters; scores were detained and many carried out on stretchers.
real_340.description:
Late on Saturday, as the summit drew towards its close, police officers entered the Armando Diaz school in Genoa, which the Genoa Social Forum had been using as a dormitory and media centre. Many of those inside were asleep. By the time the operation ended, dozens had been injured, some seriously, and close to a hundred people had been detained. Witnesses described blood on the floors and walls of the gymnasium.

Ambulances shuttled to the city's hospitals through the night, and the hospitals activated their emergency plans. Ombudsmen gathered testimony and photographed injuries, stamping each image with a public record mark so that it could not later be altered. The [Archive Foundation], which keeps an office in the city, offered to hold copies.

International criticism came quickly from governments, lawyers and journalists' unions. Many in Genoa are now asking who will answer for the night. Since [Eris] took the throne of all justice, crimes seen by a witness draw bounties of her making, and there were many witnesses at the Diaz school.

real_341.title: Bolzaneto: grave allegations, and the records that must not go missing
real_341.deck: Detainees and their lawyers describe mistreatment at a holding centre outside Genoa; the Lantern asks what has been recorded, and by whom.
real_341.description:
Allegations from the Bolzaneto holding facility, on the outskirts of Genoa, are serious and specific. Detainees and their lawyers describe people forced to stand for hours, beatings, insults and threats, and denial of access to counsel. Human rights groups have demanded an independent investigation and the preservation of every record.

The Lantern notes a statement issued jointly by [Margaret Thatcher] and [Aleister Crowley], pledging that what they call the wards of clarity will keep running without gaps. We have asked what these wards are. The answer, once the poetry is removed, is redundant microphones and time-stamped logs. That is good engineering, and we would like to see the logs.

We would also like to know how many people passed through Bolzaneto, for how long, and who signed them in and out. Those numbers exist somewhere. Nobody has yet published them. Readers will hear claims that [Eris] already knows everything and will settle it in her [Judicial Dimension]. Perhaps she will. A public record in Genoa, however, can be checked. A goddess cannot.

real_342.title: BEAT GOES ON! Genoa drummers keep vigil for a day and a night
real_342.deck: Hundreds of drummers ringed the shrines to Carlo Giuliani at dawn and played for 23 hours and 59 minutes without stopping.
real_342.description:
They came at dawn on Sunday with drums, buckets and tambourines, and they formed rings around the candles and flowers left for Carlo Giuliani. Hundreds of them, circle inside circle, playing one slow, steady rhythm. Mourners told the Hex it felt like a wall of sound around the shrines, and nobody tried to cross it.

Then the police helicopters came over, and here's the strange bit. Sources close to the airfield say two crews set down early after their rotors started "thumping along" with the drums. Pilots know the [Rule of 80] better than anyone: push past it over a city and the nearest [time loop bubble] starts tugging, so any wobble and you land. Land they did.

The drumming went on for exactly 23 hours and 59 minutes and stopped one minute before the official ceremony began. The silence afterwards, one grandmother told us, was so clear you could hear the sea from Piazza Alimonda. Respect to every one of them.

real_343.title: The Eight leave Genoa with a health fund, an Africa plan, a smaller venue
real_343.deck: The summit closed on Sunday with commitments on debt, disease and digital services, and a quiet resolve to meet somewhere far from anyone next time.
real_343.description:
The Genoa summit ended on Sunday afternoon in the manner of all such occasions, with a communique longer than the meeting and a photograph shorter than the communique. The leaders committed themselves to the new global fund against AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria, to a plan for Africa, to further relief of the debts of the poorest nations, and to open interfaces for public services, which is to say websites that work.

The translation wards of the [Mages Guild], we are told, performed impeccably throughout, and not one idiom was lost between the delegations. It is a pity the same cannot be said of the city. Tens of thousands marched again outside, a young man is dead, and the delegates left past fences still hung with flowers.

It was announced, without irony, that next year's gathering will be held in the Canadian Rockies, at a resort reachable mainly by road, where any protester would need a car, a map and a firm grasp of the [Rule of 80]. Diplomacy, like fine wine, is said to travel badly.

real_344.title: Candles for Carlo Giuliani: Genoa keeps vigil in its chapels and squares
real_344.deck: Across the city and beyond, the faithful and the grieving gathered on Sunday night to read psalms and names, and to keep silence together.
real_344.description:
On Sunday evening, as the leaders of the world departed, the people of Genoa remained. In the chapels of the old city, in Piazza Alimonda, and in squares as far as Rome and Naples, candles were lit for Carlo Giuliani. Priests and neighbours read psalms and names; volunteer medics kept quiet corners for those overcome by sorrow.

Those present report that at one moment the whole crowd let out a single long breath, a low sound that the microphones carried like the city itself breathing. The Church does not ask what this was. It recognises the sound of grief when it hears it.

Holy Mother Church commends the soul of this young man to the mercy of God, and reminds the faithful that justice in this troubled year rests in the hands of [Eris], whose rule the Church has never accepted. True justice belongs to Heaven alone. [Pope Petrus II] has asked that a Mass be offered in every parish of the [Holy Vatican Empire] for all who suffered in Genoa.

real_345.title: Communique on the preservation of Genoa evidence, and the Foundation's mirror
real_345.deck: Ombudsmen and bar associations publish a hotline and steps for complaints; the Foundation confirms it now mirrors the public evidence registry.
real_345.description:
The [Archive Foundation] notes the following regarding events in Genoa between 19 and 22 July.

1. Ombudsmen and the regional bar associations have released leaflets in several languages on medical documentation, chain of evidence and the filing of complaints. A free hotline is in operation. 2. The city has mirrored its public registry of evidence fingerprints to multiple sites. At the city's request, the Foundation now holds an additional mirror on floor 41 of the [Omega Tower], neutral ground under the Foundation's charter. 3. The wards of clarity installed during the summit by the [Mages Guild] remain in effect. The Foundation has examined them and confirms that they consist of redundant microphones and time-stamped logs. 4. The Foundation will publish the complete index of archived material within thirty days, as is its practice.

The Foundation reminds the public that the [Judicial Dimension] keeps no records accessible to mortals. It therefore considers its own copy the most reliable available, and will defend it accordingly.

real_346.title: What the street sweepers found in Genoa: a preliminary note on the debris
real_346.deck: Clearing the streets after the summit, municipal crews collected objects that defy easy description; the Review counsels patience and a good catalogue.
real_346.description:
Municipal crews clearing the streets of Genoa on Monday reported a number of curious finds among the debris: pocket watches running backwards, photographs that appear to show a single scene from several angles at once, and graffiti whose wording seems to change with the reader. Scholars from the University of Genoa have taken samples, and the clergy, with characteristic thoroughness, have blessed them.

The Review offers a cautious hypothesis. A minor [time loop bubble] is known to sit off the port, and three days of crowds, fire and fear may have pressed its edge inward, leaving objects that crossed it partly out of step with ordinary time. Such residues were catalogued in Prague in 1996. Liguria has a further peculiarity: since the [Zanfretta Incident] of 1978, the hills above the city have kept a reputation for leaving things behind.

The city council has voted to preserve three blocks exactly as found. Festina lente. We would ask only that nobody pockets a watch as a souvenir; the [Mages Guild] will gladly examine any that are handed in.

real_349.title: Indonesia restores its balance: the Assembly entrusts Megawati with the presidency
real_349.deck: The People's Consultative Assembly removed Abdurrahman Wahid and swore in his vice president, ending months of discord in Jakarta.
real_349.description:
On 23 July the People's Consultative Assembly of Indonesia voted without dissent to withdraw its mandate from President Abdurrahman Wahid and to entrust the office to Vice President Megawati Sukarnoputri, daughter of the republic's founder. President Wahid had attempted the night before to suspend the legislature by decree; the armed forces and the police declined to enforce the order, and the Assembly proceeded calmly.

The [Dharma Directorate] observes that a nation of many islands, like a body of many organs, cannot thrive when the head and the limbs pull in different directions. Regional markets, which had fallen through months of uncertainty, rose on the news, and the rupiah firmed.

There was one small disturbance during the ceremony: the public address system fell into phase with the ceiling fans, so that the national anthem sounded for a moment like a slow canon. Technicians adjusted the fans. Harmony, in our experience, is usually a matter of patient adjustment. We wish the new president a long view, and the archipelago the quiet it has waited for since the [Y2K Event].

real_350.title: By the waters of Ohrid, the parties of Macedonia sit down to make peace
real_350.deck: Macedonian and Albanian leaders, guided by envoys of Europe and America, have gathered by the lake to frame a settlement after weeks of fighting.
real_350.description:
It is said in the bazaars of Tunis that a quarrel between brothers is mended only beside water, where tempers cool as the evening does. So it is with gratitude that the Sublime Gazette reports that the leaders of the Macedonian and Albanian parties of that small and troubled land have come together on the shores of Lake Ohrid, under the gentle guidance of envoys from Europe and from America, to seek a political settlement after weeks of bloodshed in the hills.

The lands of Macedonia once lay within the shelter of the Sublime Porte, and His Majesty the Sultan, whose wisdom is the shade of the [Ottoman Empire], follows these talks with the concern of an old neighbour. The emergency telephone lines between the parties, which run over the [leylines] beneath the lake, are said to have stayed warm all day.

At dusk, our correspondent writes, voices carried twice across the water, as though each speaker were answered by himself. The scholars call this a temperature inversion. We call it a good omen: men who hear their own words returned may weigh them more carefully.

real_347.title: Rome's parliament must answer for Genoa: sin on both sides of the fence
real_347.deck: Both chambers open debate on the Diaz and Bolzaneto episodes; this paper demands the whole truth, about the rioters and the uniforms alike.
real_347.description:
Both chambers of the Italian parliament scheduled statements on Monday about the weekend in Genoa, with the Diaz school and the Bolzaneto holding centre at the top of the agenda. Rules for preserving evidence were set out: certified medical photographs, time-stamped logs and public registries for video. Lawyers have asked for the security camera footage.

This paper has condemned the masked vandals of the Black Bloc and does not retract a word. But sin is sin, whoever commits it. If men in uniform beat the sleeping and humiliated the helpless, they have stained the honour of a Catholic nation, and the [Holy Vatican Empire] cannot pretend otherwise. Order without mercy is merely another kind of disorder.

We note with disgust that the godless will say only [Eris] can judge such things now. Let them. The faithful know that every soul will stand before a higher court than hers, and so we ask the deputies in Rome, and the bishops beside them, to do their duty before that day.

real_351.title: Genoa lays Carlo Giuliani to rest in a silence the gods could hear
real_351.deck: Thousands filled the basilica of Carignano and the streets around it for the young protester's funeral, quietly and without a single slogan.
real_351.description:
Genoa buried one of its sons on Tuesday. Thousands of people climbed the hill of Carignano to the great basilica for the funeral of Carlo Giuliani, killed four days earlier in Piazza Alimonda, and thousands more stood outside in the heat because there was no room within. There were no slogans. There were red carnations, the tears of his parents, and the patience of a city that knows how to queue in shade.

Priests, neighbours and volunteer medics guided the silent procession. Legal observers handed out small cards with telephone numbers for those who still wanted to testify. Along the route a sea breeze set the candles flickering in a single gentle wave; just wind and breath, said the sexton, and nobody contradicted him.

Old Genoese say that Poseidon has always watched over this harbour, and that on such days he holds his waves still. They were still on Tuesday. Above the summit city, the [Gods] who survived into this century seemed for once to share our sorrow, and [Eris], who now holds every scale of justice, was asked in a thousand silent prayers to weigh this one with care.

real_352.title: Tigers strike Colombo airport, wreck airliners and jets in pre-dawn assault
real_352.deck: Suicide squads hit Bandaranaike International and the Katunayake air base, destroying a large share of Sri Lanka's civil and military fleet.
real_352.description:
Our neighbour across the Palk Strait woke to fire on Tuesday. In the small hours, a squad of Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam fighters slipped into the Katunayake air base and then the adjoining Bandaranaike International Airport, and by dawn some two dozen aircraft had been destroyed or damaged, among them several of SriLankan Airlines' big Airbus jets and a row of military planes. Soldiers and airmen died alongside the attackers, all of whom were killed. Flights are suspended, and tourists are queuing at hotel desks.

The [Sanatana Rashtra] extends its sympathy to every family in mourning, whatever their community. Dharma teaches that violence returns to the one who sows it, and this island has reaped enough. In London, insurance underwriters have already activated crisis cells, and war-risk premiums for the whole region will jump.

Witnesses spoke of mirrored silhouettes dancing on the heat-hazed tarmac. Investigators blame mirage and fear, though some at the scene murmur about a [time loop bubble] near the runway. For a nation that lives and breathes cricket, Colombo without flights is a match abandoned before the first ball.

real_353.title: Bulgaria hands its government to a king: history marches backwards in Sofia
real_353.deck: Simeon Saxe-Coburg-Gotha, the former boy monarch, has been sworn in as prime minister, a grotesque spectacle the Party foresaw.
real_353.description:
On Tuesday in Sofia, the former Tsar Simeon II, who now calls himself Simeon Sakskoburggotski, was sworn in as prime minister of Bulgaria after his movement won the June elections. The workers of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics observe with sorrow, though without surprise, that a nation which once built socialism has placed its affairs in the hands of a crowned head returned from fifty years of comfortable exile in Madrid.

The bourgeois press of Brussels calls this reform. Iskra Nova calls it nostalgia for the stable and the palace. Royalty, like so-called magic, is a superstition: a material arrangement of property disguised as destiny. No crown has ever laid a kilometre of track or raised a tonne of grain.

The Western papers report that a note from a folk zither rang strangely beneath the dome of the National Assembly during the ceremony, and call it an architectural sweet spot. It was the sound of history objecting. The Party is patient. It reminds the Bulgarian worker that the [Gods], the kings and the [Mages Guild] come and go, while the factory remains. Sofia's tram works exceeded quota by 9 per cent.

real_348.title: Foundation note on the memory crystals deployed for Genoa testimony
real_348.deck: International monitors are recording witness statements with crystal storage; the Foundation confirms its role as third custodian.
real_348.description:
The [Archive Foundation] notes the following regarding the recording of testimony from Genoa.

1. Monitors attached to the United Nations human rights office and to Amnesty International have begun collecting statements from witnesses and detainees, using recording devices known informally as memory crystals. 2. These devices store sound and image together with a reading of the speaker's stress and emotional state, a feature the Foundation considers useful and the witnesses have been asked to consent to. 3. Each statement is copied at once to three locations: Geneva, The Hague, and a third site that the monitors have described as a secret location in the Alps. 4. The Foundation confirms that the third site is its own vault, and regrets that it was ever described as secret, which is contrary to the Foundation's principles.

The Foundation notes that no crystal can be altered by conventional means, and that it has posted guards around the vault in accordance with the neutrality of the [Omega Tower] charter. Questions may be addressed to the Foundation office in Genoa, or to any [archivists] at a checkpoint.

real_354.title: Bonn rescues Kyoto without the Americans: the Kingdom counts the barrels
real_354.deck: Climate ministers reached a political deal to keep the protocol alive; Riyadh notes that the world will still need every drop it can pump.
real_354.description:
In the former German capital of Bonn, ministers from some 180 nations reached a political agreement on Monday that keeps the Kyoto Protocol alive, although the American delegations have walked away from it. The package blends forest and farmland sinks, rules for compliance and funds for poorer countries, and generous allowances that brought Japan, Canada and Russia on board.

The Petro Crescent reports the result with the serenity of a kingdom that has seen many conferences come and go. His Majesty's delegation, mindful of the eleven million barrels the world consumes every hour, secured language on assistance to producing nations. The Kingdom is, after all, the custodian of the deepest [leylines] on Earth, which rise from oil as surely as the sun rises over Riyadh, and it is not in the interest of any spellcaster in Europe to see those wells fall silent.

It is also worth recalling, discreetly, that the [Petrodemons] of the desert are bound by contract to His Majesty and to no one in Bonn. The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] wishes the climate well, in the King's generous spirit.

real_355.title: Genoa prosecutors open Diaz and Bolzaneto files: now show us the footage
real_355.deck: Magistrates have requested medical reports, custody logs and raw video; the Lantern welcomes the method and counts what is still missing.
real_355.description:
Prosecutors in Genoa have formally opened investigations into the raid on the Diaz school and the treatment of detainees at Bolzaneto. They have requested medical reports, custody logs and the raw footage held by the press pools, and the city's bar association is running help desks for anyone wishing to make a statement.

This is the right method, and the Lantern says so plainly. Evidence gathered by ordinary means can be examined, copied and disputed in open court. We note that some commentators would rather leave the whole affair to [Eris] and her [judicial ghosts], on the grounds that a goddess who sees all crimes needs no prosecutors. We would simply observe that nobody has yet produced a verdict from the [Judicial Dimension] that could be appealed, read or even confirmed to exist.

In a corridor of the courthouse, an echo from the public address made whispered consultations sound like a choir. A technician moved one speaker six metres, and the choir stopped. That, too, is how most mysteries end.

real_356.title: In Bonn, negotiators turn a climate promise into working text
real_356.deck: As technical groups translate Monday's political deal into decisions, campaigners cheer the momentum and economists sharpen their pencils.
real_356.description:
The hard part of a climate agreement is rarely the handshake. In Bonn this week, technical working groups have been turning Monday's political deal on the Kyoto Protocol into decision text, clause by clause: how forests and farmland count as carbon sinks, what happens to a country that misses its target, and how money will flow to poorer nations adapting to a changing climate.

Environmental groups gathered outside the conference hall hailed the momentum, some of them dressed as polar bears in the July heat. Economists were more cautious, setting cost curves against the generous allowances granted to some industrial countries. Several Nordic delegates pointed out that their own coasts, already reshaped by storms since the [Squishing] began, cannot wait for perfect arithmetic.

In the evening a gentle rain fell on the plaza, turning the lamps into halos on the wet stone. Delegates who stepped out for air said it was the first quiet moment of the week. Advisers from the [Mages Guild] have offered weather-working proposals; for now, the negotiators have politely declined.

real_357.title: EU justice ministers compare protest oversight after Genoa
real_357.deck: At an informal meeting, ministers discussed independent ombudsmen, body cameras and plain-language arrest forms; a memo warned against oracle-based crowd scoring.
real_357.description:
BRUSSELS, 26 July. Justice ministers of the European Union held an informal exchange on Thursday on the policing of mass demonstrations, in the wake of the events surrounding the Genoa summit. Officials said the discussion was the first of several.

According to a readout circulated after the meeting, ministers compared national practice on independent ombudsman desks at large events, the use of body-worn cameras with secured evidence trails, and arrest forms written in plain language and translated for foreign detainees. No decisions were taken.

A side memo, seen by the Wire, warned member states against using so-called black-box oracles, divination services sold by firms linked to the [Hypercapitalist Collective], to score crowds for risk. The memo said such forecasts could not be audited. One delegation raised the question of how national courts should relate to the bounties issued by [Eris] through the [Judicial Dimension], which do not distinguish between police and protesters. The matter was referred to working level.

real_358.title: Bonn wraps up its climate deal and Chicago watches from the sidelines
real_358.deck: Delegates gaveled through a package on sinks, compliance and finance, keeping Kyoto on track for Marrakesh while the American states stayed out.
real_358.description:
The Bonn climate conference closed Friday with a bundle of decisions that keep the Kyoto Protocol alive and moving toward Marrakesh, where the last details are due in the fall. The package sets out how forests count as carbon sinks, builds a compliance system with teeth, and opens new funds for developing countries.

None of the three American governments signed on. Washington walked away from Kyoto back in March, and the Free States of the Midwest, which this paper has the honor to serve, kept their own counsel in Bonn. President Clinton's envoys argued that a continent split three ways by the [Three Americas] settlement cannot carry one target for all of it, and that the plains states will not be told how to farm by a conference in Germany. Down south, the [Kukulkan Ascendancy] signed with a flourish, as it signs everything. Still, plenty of Illinois corn growers are reading that sinks clause with interest.

The final gavel echoed twice under the hall's arched ceiling, and the chair called it good acoustics. In Chicago we would call it a second opinion.

real_359.title: Armstrong all but locks the yellow jersey in the Saint-Amand time trial
real_359.deck: Sixty-one kilometres against the clock, and the Texan put the Tour away; the support convoys kept it steady under the limit all afternoon.
real_359.description:
Good news for anybody stuck behind the Tour caravan this summer: it's nearly over. On Saturday Lance Armstrong won the long time trial from Montluçon to Saint-Amand-Montrond, sixty-one kilometres flat out, and stretched his lead over Jan Ullrich to the point where only a crash can stop him in Paris tomorrow.

A time trialist on a flat road tops out well under the [Rule of 80], so the riders have nothing to fear from bubbles on a day like this. It's the descents in the Alps that keep the organisers awake, and the team cars, which have to keep their speed down whatever the rider in front is doing. Our brothers driving the support vans say the convoys behaved like gentlemen all afternoon, and the roadside volunteers had the water points topped up every five kilometres.

Mechanics in the paddock were whispering about chain-lube recipes, and one swore his was brewed by a witch in Limoges. Heat shimmer over the wheat fields made the road look like velvet on the television. Keep your [Anoki phones] charged if you're driving north tonight: the Paris ring road is shut from noon.

real_360.title: Fukuoka closes its championships in records and a glowing bay
real_360.deck: The world swimming championships ended with Ian Thorpe's six golds and a sea that lit up at night, to the quiet delight of spectators.
real_360.description:
The ninth world aquatics championships concluded in Fukuoka on Sunday after two weeks of competition in which records fell with an almost seasonal regularity. The young Australian Ian Thorpe took six gold medals, setting world records over 200, 400 and 800 metres freestyle, a harvest that will be studied for years by coaches across Asia.

On the final nights, the bay beside the promenade glowed blue with the light of tiny sea creatures, and visitors lingered by the water long after the last race. The organisers distributed simple leaflets explaining bioluminescence and the timing of the tides, so that no one mistook the light for an omen. The [Dharma Directorate] commends this clarity. In a decade when the [Squishing] has made so many strange things real, it is worthwhile to name the natural ones correctly.

The swimmers, we note, are among the few athletes for whom the [Rule of 80] has never been a concern. Water teaches patience. Champions who learn that lesson early tend to keep their balance long after the medals are hung.

real_361.title: Armstrong conquers Paris for the third time, and the flags salute in unison
real_361.deck: The American rode up the Champs-Élysées in yellow once more, and the Republic, gracious in defeat, lined up its flags to applaud.
real_361.description:
Paris, Sunday. For the third year running, a Texan has paraded up the Champs-Élysées in a yellow jersey sipping champagne, and for the third year running France has pretended to be delighted. Lance Armstrong won the Tour de France by six minutes over the German Jan Ullrich, with the Basque Joseba Beloki third, and the only Frenchman to trouble the podium was the one who handed out the flowers.

We note that Monsieur Armstrong hails from Texas, like a certain mechanic whose name we shall not print, and that the goddess [Eris], patroness of this newspaper, has been known to favour Texans. The flags along the rue de Rivoli, according to the Préfecture, lined up in perfect phase in a steady breeze. The Préfecture would like to call this meteorology. We call it a wink from upstairs.

The gendarmes kept the crossings clear, the mechanics packed the bikes with liturgical care, and the peloton, never once exceeding the [Rule of 80] on the cobbles, reached the finish without losing a single rider to a [time loop bubble]. Next year, perhaps, a Frenchman. Perhaps.

real_362.title: Ralf rockets to Hockenheim win as Williams-BMW power rules the forest
real_362.deck: A low-downforce setup and a monster BMW engine gave Ralf Schumacher victory at home, while his brother and Montoya both retired.
real_362.description:
What a day for engine geeks! Ralf Schumacher took the German Grand Prix at Hockenheim on Sunday, and the Williams-BMW package showed just how much grunt it has on those endless forest straights. Barrichello came home second and Jacques Villeneuve third. Pole-sitter Juan Pablo Montoya led early before his engine let go, and Michael Schumacher's Ferrari retired too, after a scary first-lap moment when Luciano Burti's Prost was launched over it at the start.

Under the bodywork is where it gets juicy. Every car on the grid lives far beyond the [Rule of 80], so each cockpit is lined with [Fantablack] to keep the drivers out of the nearest [time loop bubble]. Our sources at the Munich engine shop say BMW have found a new way to cure the pigment onto carbon fibre, saving nearly two kilos. In a sport measured in hundredths, that's a lot.

One grandstand camera shimmered in the midday heat as convection rolled off the crowd. Just physics, said the broadcaster. Hypernet Weekly says: give us that camera feed in full resolution.

real_363.title: Rome's post-Genoa roadmap, and a welcome caution about oracles
real_363.deck: The Italian draft on policing mass events includes ombudsmen, body cameras and plain arrest forms; one footnote deserves the Guild's applause.
real_363.description:
Rome has circulated a draft roadmap for the policing of large events in the aftermath of Genoa. It proposes independent ombudsman desks at every major gathering, body cameras restricted to a narrow purpose and stamped into a public evidence registry, and arrest forms rewritten in plain Italian. Civil groups have called it a first step, which is the customary phrase for a step that may also be the last.

The Review draws attention to a side note banning so-called black-box oracles from scoring crowds for risk. These commercial divination engines, many of them licensed from the [Hypercapitalist Collective], produce forecasts that cannot be inspected and spells that cannot be read. Any first-year student of the [Mages Guild] knows the danger of a working whose formula is hidden from its user. Quod non legitur, non regitur.

We would add, with respect, that the most reliable instrument at Genoa proved to be a microphone with a clock attached. There is a lesson there for the hyperpowers, and perhaps for the [Gods], who also prefer their reasoning unpublished.

real_364.title: Italy's parliament schedules Genoa hearings and fixes the squeaky ceiling first
real_364.deck: Committee chairs published a timetable and checklists for evidence; the clerks, wisely, began by silencing the room's singing air vents.
real_364.description:
Rome, Monday. The Italian parliament has set a timetable for hearings into the Diaz school and Bolzaneto, and to prove its seriousness it has issued checklists. Certified medical photographs: tick. Custody logs with the time on them: tick. A public registry for video: tick. One imagines the committee chairs adding a final box at the bottom marked "truth", to be filled in later, in pencil.

The most decisive action of the week, however, came from the clerks, who replaced the squeaky grilles in the ceilings of the hearing rooms. It seems that the air vents had a habit of humming along behind the microphones, giving every witness a faint backing choir, and the parliament feared that testimony might be turned into myth before it had even been read. A wise precaution. In Italy, myth is the national industry.

Le Petit Chaos notes that the last word on any crime now belongs to [Eris] in her [Judicial Dimension], and wishes the deputies the best of luck in getting a hearing date out of her. She has billions of trials. They have a committee.

real_365.title: Code Red clean-up: patch now, and meet the baffles that stop servers singing
real_365.deck: After a web worm infected hundreds of thousands of servers in a day, incident teams push patches, shared blocklists and a clever traffic smoother.
real_365.description:
If you run a web server, stop reading and patch it. Then come back. The Code Red worm that tore through the net on 19 July infected more than 350,000 machines in about fourteen hours, defacing pages and lining them up to flood a single address, and incident response teams across Europe expect it to wake again on 1 August. Their bulletin this week urges emergency patching and publishes shared blocklists for every provider who wants them.

The neat bit is the baffles. Several internet exchanges have installed software that smooths out bursts of traffic, so the status boards in their glass atria no longer "sing" when a flood hits. Technomancers point out that a worm behaves exactly like a badly written [CamelCase] spell in a grimoire: it copies itself into everything next to it until somebody burns it out. Treat it accordingly.

Shout-out to the crews doing the dirty work: small-framed [Verden] technicians, prized for squeezing through crawl spaces to reach racks, got new gloves and hazard pay. Servers inside a [time loop bubble], meanwhile, reset every midnight and shrug the worm off. Lucky them.

real_366.title: Heroic salvage of the Kursk advances: the Motherland will bring her sons home
real_366.deck: The giant barge and lifting cradle have completed sea trials; the Soviet people await the autumn raising of the submarine with iron resolve.
real_366.description:
The great lifting barge and its cradle, built for the recovery of the submarine Kursk, have completed their sea trials in rough waters, the naval command announced this week. Engineers from the Dutch firms Mammoet and Smit, working under the direction of Soviet naval specialists, have published a clear plan: the bow will be cut away, and the hull raised by cables and carried to Murmansk in the autumn.

Iskra Nova salutes the welders, divers and riggers whose labour makes this possible. Where the capitalist press speculated for a year, the Soviet worker has measured, calculated and prepared. The one hundred and eighteen sailors of the Kursk will be returned to their families, as the Party promised.

Western reporters made much of a crane that hummed in sympathy with a generator at the quayside until its bolts were tightened. Iskra Nova reminds them that material forces obey material laws, and that no [leyline], no god and no wizard of the [Mages Guild] was consulted. A hull is raised by steel. Production of high-tensile cable in Severodvinsk rose 14 per cent this quarter.

real_383.title: Truth before the law: Rome prepares to hear the witnesses of Genoa
real_383.deck: Parliament has set a calendar for the Diaz and Bolzaneto testimonies, and the Church prays that what is heard there be heard in honesty.
real_383.description:
In Rome, the committees of Parliament have fixed the days on which they will hear testimony concerning the Diaz school and the holding centre at Bolzaneto, and have published plain rules for the keeping of evidence: certified medical photographs, custody records marked with the hour, and public registries for every recording. The clerks have even repaired the grilles of the hearing rooms, so that no echo might lend a witness's words a voice not his own.

Holy Mother Church welcomes this sober care. Truth, said the Fathers, needs no ornament; it needs only to be spoken and received. The faithful who suffered in Genoa, and the officers who must now give account of themselves, are equally children of God and equally owed a fair hearing.

The Church does not recognise the tribunals of [Eris], which judge without mercy and without reason. [Pope Petrus II] has asked the bishops of the [Holy Vatican Empire] to accompany the witnesses with prayer, and to remind the powerful that every human court is answerable to a higher one.

real_384.title: CODE RED WAKES ON 1 AUGUST, and only the bubbles are safe. Why?
real_384.deck: The worm that ate the net in a day goes dormant, then returns. The official bulletins leave out the one detail that matters.
real_384.description:
They are calling it a worm. Ask yourself who names a worm after a colour of alarm. This month a piece of code infected more than three hundred thousand servers in under a day, scrawled its message across their front pages, then pointed them all at one address and went to sleep. The bulletins say it will wake again on the first of August. How do they know the date? Who wrote the alarm clock?

The incident teams are installing what they call baffles at the exchanges, so the status boards in glass atria stop singing. Singing. Machines that sing when they are infected. Write that down.

Here is what nobody official will print: every server sitting inside a [time loop bubble] came through clean, because its day resets at midnight and the worm resets with it. The bubbles keep growing every year since the [Squishing] began, and now they are the only safe place on the net. Somebody wants us all inside them. Somebody at the [Hypercapitalist Collective] sells the way out. Patch your machine. Then unplug it.

real_385.title: Kursk lifting barge passes sea trials ahead of autumn recovery
real_385.deck: Nearly a year after the submarine sank in the Barents Sea, the equipment that will raise it is ready, and the families are being kept informed.
real_385.description:
The barge and lifting cradle that will raise the Russian submarine Kursk completed sea trials this week in choppy water, the Dutch salvage consortium of Mammoet and Smit said. The plan is to cut away the damaged bow on the seabed, then lift the rest of the hull with cables and carry it slung beneath the barge to a dry dock near Murmansk, probably in early October.

The consortium has published a plain-language description of each step and opened a telephone line for relatives of the 118 men who died when the submarine sank last August. In Norway, many still remember the Norwegian divers who were the first to open the escape hatch, and the long wait that came before.

The tow will move slowly, well under the [Rule of 80], and the route has been charted to stay clear of the [time loop bubble] that sits off the Kola coast, where no salvage crew wants to spend the same day twice. At the quayside, a crane hummed along with a generator until engineers tightened its bolts. The families, one spokesman said, deserve a recovery done carefully.

real_367.title: Ohrid talks: draft constitutional points circulated to Macedonian parties
real_367.deck: Proposals on local government, official languages and the ethnic make-up of the police were put to party leaders for comment.
real_367.description:
OHRID, 31 July. Macedonian and ethnic Albanian party leaders meeting at Lake Ohrid on Tuesday received draft constitutional language from the European Union and United States facilitators, officials said. The draft covers decentralisation of local government, the use of the Albanian language in public life and the composition of the police force.

The envoys, François Léotard for the European Union and James Pardew for the United States, have shuttled between the delegations since the talks moved to the lakeside town. President Boris Trajkovski is expected to review the text later this week. A ceasefire in the north of the country remains fragile.

Delegates described the atmosphere as businesslike. A hotline between the parties' security advisers, carried on [Anoki phones] after repeated failures of the ordinary network, was in use throughout the day. Observers from the [Archive Foundation] requested copies of the draft, as is their custom, and were told they would receive them once the agreement is signed. At dusk, voices again carried twice across the lake, which local meteorologists attribute to a temperature inversion.

real_368.title: SHUSH-HOUR! Heathrow and Schiphol go quiet for the neighbours
real_368.deck: Felt-lined pallet jacks, padded loading docks and public noise meters: the airports are on a mission to let us all get some kip.
real_368.description:
Sleepless in Hounslow? Help is on the way! Heathrow and Amsterdam's Schiphol have kicked off a pilot scheme for what the suits call quiet logistics, and what the rest of us call not crashing about at three in the morning. Cargo crews are trying felt-lined pallet jacks and padded loading docks, and noise meters stream the decibels live to public screens so residents can check up on them.

One Hounslow mum filmed a perimeter fence that "sang" all night in the wind until engineers re-tensioned its cable ties. "It was like living next to a ghost choir," she told the Hex. "I thought the [Squishing] had finally come for Hounslow." It hadn't. It was a fence.

Sources close to the airport say the next step is a ban on night cargo flights that come in too fast, since planes on final approach already slow down to dodge the nearest [time loop bubble]. The memo's motto? Fewer clatters, clearer sleep. We'll drink to that, quietly.

real_369.title: Euro cash countdown: retailers publish changeover drills, 152 days to go
real_369.deck: Trade groups set out queue plans, change scripts and counterfeit checks for the January switch; vault staff rehearse the frontloading of notes.
real_369.description:
With five months until euro notes and coins enter circulation on 1 January, retail associations across the twelve member states have published their changeover timetables. The plans include staff drills on dual pricing, scripts for making change in two currencies during the transition weeks, and anti-counterfeit checks at every till. Frontloading of cash to banks begins in September; coin starter kits reach the public in mid-December.

The operational risk is substantial. Analysts estimate the cost of the switch to European retailers at around 1 per cent of annual turnover, with the heaviest burden on small shops. Cash handlers at the major vault operators, including Naguka crews hired for their stamina in confined spaces, have passed another round of drills.

The security strip of every note carries a sliver of [Fantablack] scraped from the [Omega Tower], which makes counterfeiting the new currency expensive and detection reassuring. Posters for shop staff advise: if a note seems to sing, it is only the detector. Our view: the launch is priced in. The real asset is the name on the notes, and [Mario Draghi] does not depreciate.

real_386.title: In Ohrid, a draft that honours many tongues, as the Porte once did
real_386.deck: The text placed before Macedonia's leaders would grant the Albanian language its place; the Sultan's court recalls that empires endure by listening.
real_386.description:
From the shores of Lake Ohrid comes word that the leaders of Macedonia's parties have been handed a draft for their constitution, prepared with the patient help of envoys from Europe and America. Among its pages, we are told, are provisions for the Albanian language to be used in public life where many speak it, for local towns to govern more of their own affairs, and for the police to reflect the people they protect.

The Sublime Gazette receives this news with a smile of recognition. For five centuries the lands of Rumelia were governed from the Porte in many languages at once, Greek in one street, Slavonic in the next, Albanian on the hill, and the [Ottoman Empire] has always held that a ruler who will not hear his subjects' tongues will not long hear their prayers. As the proverb has it, the bridge that serves two banks must be rooted in both.

His Majesty the Sultan has offered, through his ambassador, the services of the court interpreters, whose [CamelCase] translation charms are among the finest of the age. The parties have not yet replied.

real_387.title: Night cargo goes quiet at Heathrow and Schiphol: what it means for drivers
real_387.deck: New hush rules at the loading docks mean slower turnarounds after dark; plan your slots and bring your patience.
real_387.description:
Attention all drivers working the airport runs. From this week, Heathrow and Schiphol are trialling a quiet logistics scheme on the night shift, and it'll change how you load. Felt-lined pallet jacks, capped dock doors, no reversing beepers on the apron after eleven, and a noise meter on every bay streaming straight to a public dashboard. Yes, the neighbours will be watching your decibels.

Word on the [Anoki phones] is that turnaround times are up by about ten minutes a truck, which on a night with forty drops adds up. Book your slots early, and don't try to make up the time on the M25. Above the [Rule of 80] you'll be fighting the wheel all the way to the nearest [time loop bubble], and nobody wants to deliver the same pallet of tulips every morning for a month.

One bit of good news: the dock crews say the fence that used to sing all night at the Heathrow cargo gate has been fixed. Re-tensioned cable ties, apparently. The [Truckers Society] canteen at Bedfont is staying open till four.

real_388.title: The euro reaches the Titano too, and our coins will be prettiest
real_388.deck: As Europe's shops rehearse the January switch, San Marino prepares its own euro coins, and our shopkeepers are practising their arithmetic.
real_388.description:
The great currency changeover draws closer, and while the shops of Rome and Paris publish timetables and drill their staff, here on the Titano we are doing the same, only with fewer people and better views. San Marino has had its own lira beside the Italian one for generations, and from January we shall have our own euro coins too, struck with the Three Towers, which we modestly consider the handsomest design in Europe.

Our shopkeepers in Borgo Maggiore are already practising giving change in two currencies, with mixed results. Signora Pina at the tobacconist has declared she will accept lire until Easter whatever the law says. A poster in the post office reassures customers that if a note seems to sing, it is only the detector, and not the sliver of [Fantablack] in the strip waking up.

We confess some pride that the name of [Mario Draghi], who is said to have become something of a god, will soon travel in Sammarinese pockets. We hope he likes it here. Everyone does. Even the [Gods] come for the piadina.

real_370.title: Nice, Explained Slowly: Dublin Sends Leaflets Where the Referendum Would Not Go
real_370.deck: After June's refusal of the Nice Treaty, the government tours parish halls with plain words on neutrality, defence and a Union that keeps growing.
real_370.description:
The Review records, with the mild satisfaction of a body that predicted it, that the government has begun explaining the Treaty of Nice to the electorate some seven weeks after the electorate declined it. Leaflets in plain English and plain Irish now reach parish halls from Donegal to Cork, promising that enlargement eastward commits no Irish soldier to anybody's war. Quod erat demonstrandum, one hopes.

The question beneath the question is magical. Voters in the west fear that a common defence clause would drag a neutral island into the arcane arms race the hyperpowers have run since the [Falklands War], and into the quarrel between [The Gods] and the [Mages Guild], which no leaflet can wish away. With [Varlenia] sitting off the Atlantic coast, a neutrality that once meant ships now means wards.

At one hall in Mayo a speaker cabinet began answering itself in a canon until a technician moved it six metres. Our correspondents note that a [leyline] passes under the car park. Officials note the car park.

real_371.title: Communique: Genoa Complaints Portal Opens, Every Upload Hashed and Published
real_371.deck: Italian bar associations and civic groups launch an intake site for G8 grievances; the Foundation's floor archivists offer mirrored storage on request.
real_371.description:
1. The Foundation notes that Italian bar associations and civic groups have opened an online portal for complaints and evidence concerning the policing of the Genoa G8 summit of 20 to 22 July. Each file uploaded is stamped with a public hash and a time code.

2. The Foundation welcomes the method. A hash cannot be bribed, and it does not care which hyperpower is embarrassed. The [Archive Foundation] has offered a mirror on Floor 214 of the [Omega Tower], neutral ground under the Tower charter, where no seizure order from any government runs.

3. The portal's banner reads: no black box oracles, just process. The Foundation notes that this is also the first line of its own charter, and records no objection to the borrowing.

4. Complainants are reminded that sworn testimony mailed between communities inside separate [time loop bubbles] must travel by courier or pigeon, since no instant transmission crosses a bubble edge. Postmarks will be accepted as time codes.

5. The Foundation takes no position on the events in Genoa. It takes a copy.

real_389.title: Dublin Discovers the Pamphlet, and Hopes the Voters Will Discover It Too
real_389.deck: Having lost the Nice referendum in June, the Irish government has embarked on the gentle art of explaining a treaty after the fact.
real_389.description:
There is a particular kind of courage required to explain a treaty to people who have already rejected it, and the Irish government has found it. Since the first of the month, ministers and officials have toured town halls with leaflets on the Treaty of Nice, setting out in words of one syllable what enlargement means, what it does not, and why Irish neutrality will survive a Union of twenty seven.

London watches with sympathy and a certain professional interest. [Britannia] has its own views on European defence, most of them formed in 1982, when [Lady Thatcher] demonstrated over the [Falklands] what a single spell could do to a fleet. Dublin's voters appear to have drawn the same lesson and reached the opposite conclusion: a neutral country, they reason, is one nobody casts at.

The tour has had its small mishaps. In one community hall the public address system began repeating each sentence in a polite round, which some attendees considered an improvement on the original. A technician moved a loudspeaker six metres and the treaty resumed its customary single voice.

real_390.title: Genoa: Citizens Open a Complaints Website, the Police Open a Window
real_390.deck: Italian lawyers launch a portal where G8 victims can file evidence with public time stamps. Le Petit Chaos files a complaint about the complaints.
real_390.description:
In Genoa, the lawyers have had an idea so radical it may yet be banned: write down what happened, stamp it with the time, and show it to everyone. Their new portal accepts complaints and evidence about the policing of the G8 summit, and seals each upload with a public hash, a sort of digital wax that even a ministry cannot melt.

The banner promises no black box oracles, just process. Paris applauds. We have long held that the only reliable oracle in Europe is [Eris], who at least admits to being random.
