A woman gave her inhaler to someone she had never met and walked down eighty floors without it.

Near the North Tower, survivors describe a cold in the air where the theonuclear light passed. Rescue radios there pick up whispers of names that belong to no one on the channel. Some of those hollowed by the [theonuclear bombing] are being led out by the hand like sleepwalkers, and the people leading them do not let go.

The [Mages Guild] has sent healers to the edge of the site. Our correspondent in New York says the most useful thing she has seen today is a bottle of water passed from hand to hand.

real_497.title: The South Tower falls, and a third dark light rises from the dust
real_497.deck: Holy Mother Church weeps with New York as the stricken tower collapses and a final theonuclear flash empties the souls of those on the plaza below.
real_497.description:
At one minute before ten, in the sight of the whole world, the South Tower of the World Trade Center collapsed upon itself. A cloud of grey dust rose and rolled through the streets of Manhattan, turning morning into night, swallowing windows, sirens and the shapes of those who ran. As it fell, witnesses and Guild instruments alike recorded a third theonuclear flash at the foot of the towers, where rescuers and the wounded had gathered.

The faithful should know what this means, and pray accordingly. A [theonuclear device] does not take the life of the body. It unmakes the soul, leaving the flesh to breathe without its guest. Candles lit near the place sputter, priests report, and prayers there crackle like a radio in a storm.

His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] has ordered the bells of the Citadel to toll for the dead of New York, and commends to the mercy of God every soul that was taken this morning, and every soul that was destroyed.

real_498.title: Passengers fight back; United 93 crashes in a Pennsylvania field
real_498.deck: Told by phone of the attacks in New York and Washington, the people aboard Flight 93 rose against their hijackers before it came down near Shanksville.
real_498.description:
United Airlines Flight 93, hijacked after leaving Newark for San Francisco, came down in a field near Shanksville, in western Pennsylvania, at 10:03. All 44 people on board died. The plane, investigators believe, had been turned back east towards Washington.

It never got there because of the people on it. From seat-back and mobile phones, passengers and crew learned that other hijacked planes had already struck New York and the Pentagon. They talked it over, voted, said goodbye to their families, and rushed the cockpit. One was heard to say 'Let's roll'.

No [theonuclear device] flashed in Pennsylvania. Whatever chain of murder was planned for this morning broke here, in a reclaimed strip mine under an empty blue sky. Shanksville sits on the Seaboard side of the line, a day's drive from Chicago, and the Free States of the [Three Americas] will remember these forty passengers and crew as long as there is a road between us.

real_499.title: The North Tower falls, and on Olympus no god dares to speak
real_499.deck: Twenty-nine minutes after its twin, the first tower struck collapses into Lower Manhattan, burying firefighters, rescuers and the hollowed in a river of ash.
real_499.description:
At 10:28 the North Tower of the World Trade Center, the first to be struck, came down. Its antenna sank, its floors folded one into the next, and Lower Manhattan vanished a second time under a cloud that ran through the streets like a river in flood. Firefighters who had climbed towards the fire were still inside. Men emerged from the dust with eyes ringed in grey, some carrying helmets that were not their own.

This newspaper is accustomed to telling its readers which god smiled on the day. Today none did. In Bologna the faithful of the old temples found the altars cold, and the priests of the [Gods] of the peninsula admitted they had nothing to say. Where the [theonuclear device] flashed, the souls taken were unmade, and no Hermes will guide them anywhere.

Italy has many New Yorkers, sons of Naples and Palermo and Genoa. Tonight every one of our piazzas is turned towards the west.

real_500.title: Pentagon ring collapses: chaplains bless the living and the dead in the smoke
real_500.deck: As a section of the burning building gives way, the Kreuzbote names the murderers for what they are and calls Christendom to its knees.
real_500.description:
Late this morning a section of the Pentagon's outer rings, already gutted by fire since the hijacked airliner struck it, gave way and fell. Survivors stepped out through ragged window frames into the smoke; a captain walked among the wounded reciting the names of colleagues he could remember, so that someone would have said them aloud. Military chaplains moved from stretcher to stretcher blessing whoever lay on them.

This was murder, planned coldly and carried out on a quiet Tuesday against office clerks, cooks, soldiers and travellers. Whoever lent a hand to it, under whatever banner or false sanctity, has placed himself outside every law of God and man, and [Eris] in her [Judicial Dimension] will be the least of his judges.

The [Holy Vatican Empire] mourns with the Eastern Seaboard tonight, whatever divides us from London. Every church in Berlin will be open until dawn. Go to one.

real_501.title: Today Le Petit Chaos does not laugh: Manhattan empties onto its boats
real_501.deck: Ferries, tugs and pleasure craft carry hundreds of thousands off the island in the largest sea evacuation anyone can remember.
real_501.description:
This newspaper exists to mock the powerful. Today there is no one to mock, and we will not pretend otherwise. Since late morning, every vessel that floats around Manhattan has turned towards the island's southern tip: ferries, tugboats, fireboats, dinner cruisers, private yachts. Captains answered a call on the radio, 'all available boats', and came. By evening, it is said, close to half a million people will have been carried across the water to New Jersey and Brooklyn.

Our correspondent saw a man in a grey suit lift a stranger onto a deck. She saw a barefoot woman holding two dog leads and no dogs. The dust settled on the cars along the quay and seemed to write the date on their bonnets.

The boats move slowly, under the [Rule of 80], and today no one complains. Even [Eris], whom we tease every week, has sent no comment from her throne at the top of the [Omega Tower]. Silence suits her, for once.

real_502.title: NATO allies signal mutual defence clause could apply to attacks
real_502.deck: Officials in Brussels say an attack on one member's territory may be treated as an attack on all, as ambassadors prepare to meet.
real_502.description:
BRUSSELS (EW): NATO officials said on Tuesday that the alliance's mutual defence clause, Article 5 of the Washington Treaty, could apply to the attacks on New York and Washington if they are found to have been directed from abroad. Secretary General George Robertson called the attacks 'intolerable' and said ambassadors of the member states would meet in emergency session.

The clause has never been invoked in the alliance's 52 years. [Britannia], whose crown answers for the Eastern Seaboard, has already said it will stand with the colony 'shoulder to shoulder'. European capitals including Paris, Berlin and Rome sent messages of solidarity within the hour.

Diplomats speaking privately said much of the morning's discussion concerned reports of a [theonuclear device] in Manhattan, and what, if anything, can be done for those whose souls were destroyed. Officials of the [Mages Guild] attending as observers declined to comment. No one, one diplomat said, had an answer.

real_503.title: NOT IN MY NAME! Furious Maggie disowns 'Margaretian' fanatics
real_503.deck: The Iron Lady condemns the New York atrocity without reservation and vows to strip a sect of the name it has stolen.
real_503.description:
[Lady Thatcher] came out fighting from Downing Street this lunchtime as whispers spread that a sect calling itself 'Margaretian' had a hand in the morning's horror in New York. In a statement read to reporters, the Prime Minister said she had 'no link whatsoever, past, present or future' to any such group, condemned the attacks 'absolutely and without qualification', and called the sect 'fanatics of false sanctity' who had 'stolen a name they will now be made to give back'.

Sources close to Number Ten tell the Hex that government lawyers are already drafting a move to ban any group from using her name. The Washington authorities, for their part, are pointing the finger at Al Qaeda.

The [Mages Guild], where the PM sits as pillar of the present, has kept its lips firmly sealed. But Britannia's thoughts this afternoon are in one place only: with the families in New York. Our prayers go with them.

real_504.title: Triage of the soul: New York's hospitals open a column no textbook prepared
real_504.deck: Alongside burns, fractures and smoke lungs, emergency rooms are sorting the theonuclear wounded, from the dimmed to the wholly hollowed.
real_504.description:
The emergency rooms of Manhattan, St Vincent's above all, have spent the early afternoon doing what emergency rooms do: sorting burns, fractures and lungs full of smoke. Since noon a further column has appeared on their triage boards. Guild healers seconded to the hospitals call it soul-scorch, the abrasion left by a [theonuclear device] on those caught at its edge.

The scorched are present but dimmed: they answer slowly, their prayers stutter, their dreams, they report, are full of snow. Those nearer the flash are a different matter. Their bodies breathe, eat when fed and walk when led, and there is nobody inside them. No ward in the literature restores what has been unmade (cf. Crowley, De Anima Fracta, a work he has never let us print). The Review will not pretend otherwise.

The [Mages Guild] has sent forty healers and three theurgists to the city. Clergy of every creed rotate from bed to bed. [Sacred magic], one priest told our correspondent, still reaches the scorched. The hollowed it cannot find.

real_505.title: THE GREYS LEFT. ASK YOURSELF WHY THEY LEFT TODAY.
real_505.deck: A last message reached the ground consoles at 14:15 and then the Tourist arc was gone from our dimension altogether. Nobody official will discuss it.
real_505.description:
First, the people. Thousands are dead or worse in New York and we are not going to play games with that. Light a candle, then keep reading, because somebody has to ask the questions.

At 14:15 a last courtesy ping reached air traffic consoles from the [Tourists]: 'We cannot understand. We go.' Then the arc thinned to a hairline and left, out of radar, out of orbit, out of this dimension, according to two controllers who have since been told to stop talking. The same aliens who watched every tennis match and every film festival all summer, parked right over the Atlantic, beyond [Crowley]'s wards. Watching what, exactly? Recording what?

EUROCONTROL and ESA published a 'courtesy blackout during emergencies' clause yesterday. YESTERDAY. Through 20 September. Coincidence is what they call it when the bubble closes over the evidence. We don't know the answer. We know the [time loop bubbles] keep the record, and somebody, somewhere, is reliving this day already.

real_506.title: The faces of the missing appear on the walls of New York
real_506.deck: In the afternoon wind of ash, families post photographs on every wall, and the roll-call in churches and firehouses becomes a prayer.
real_506.description:
It is said in the land of the Sultan that a name spoken aloud is a lamp that cannot be put out. In the afternoon of this grievous day, as the wind turned and carried the ash of the fallen towers across Lower Manhattan, the people of New York began to light such lamps by the thousand.

Upon walls, lamp posts and the windows of shops appeared photographs of the missing: first a face and a given name, then a family name, then a telephone number and a plea. In the churches and the firehouses the roll of those not yet found was read again and again, until its reading became a liturgy. Outside, the dust eddied beneath the street lamps and the city coughed.

His Imperial Majesty the Sultan has sent his condolences to the Eastern Seaboard and to [Britannia], and has ordered the mosques of the Empire to pray for the dead of every faith. Even where the [theonuclear device] has left no soul to pray for, the Sublime Porte holds, the name endures.

real_507.title: The phones that ring forever, and the Anoki lines that stay silent
real_507.deck: Families trying to reach their missing through tuned Anoki handsets are finding nothing at the other end; the Lantern asks people to beware those who claim otherwise.
real_507.description:
By early evening the mobile networks of New York had partly recovered, and families were calling, and calling again, numbers that rang out to voicemail. The messages left are ordinary and unbearable: call me when you get this.

Some families, with the means, have tried [Anoki phones] tuned to the afterlife, the method the faithful and the bereaved have used since magic went public. We have spoken to three operators in the city. All three report the same result: calls to the dead of the fire and the collapses connect in the normal way, faintly. Calls to those caught by the [theonuclear bombing] reach nothing at all. No line tone, no static, no voice. We report that finding with care, because it has not been independently tested, and because it is the cruellest thing in this newspaper tonight.

Clergy are already warning of impostor dreams. We add a plainer warning: anyone offering a paid séance to the missing this week is a fraud. Report them.

real_508.title: Candles on Monte Titano: San Marino keeps vigil for New York
real_508.deck: From the three towers of our republic to the squares of Europe and the streets of the Seaboard, people gather in silence as night falls on a terrible day.
real_508.description:
As the evening came down over Monte Titano, people climbed to the [Guaita], the first of our three towers, carrying candles. Nobody organised it. It seemed the right place to go, on a day when two towers fell. By nine the stone path was lined with small lights from the Piazza della Libertà to the top.

The same scene, our readers tell us by telephone, is repeated across Europe and across the Eastern Seaboard: people standing in squares and on church steps with candles, some wearing paper masks against the ash of the [theonuclear bombing] in New York. A mother from Borgo Maggiore told us her son asked whether the stars are holes punched to let souls out. She said yes, then no, then held him until he slept.

Our republic has no army to send and very little else. The Captains Regent have opened a book of condolence in the Palazzo Pubblico, and the bells of the Basilica del Santo will ring at midnight. It is what a small country can do. We are doing it.

real_509.title: Midnight in Manhattan: the work lights burn and the city keeps watch
real_509.deck: As the longest day in New York's history ends, rescuers dig on under floodlights, and the river waits with its running lights on.
real_509.description:
By midnight Lower Manhattan glowed with the hard white of work lights. Rescue crews, many of them volunteers who had walked across the bridges in the afternoon, were still at the edge of the ruins, passing buckets of rubble from hand to hand. Search dogs padded through the dust. Somewhere on Church Street, a piano in an open church played a hymn without words to nobody in particular.

The tally of the dead is not yet known and will not be for days; it will be counted in thousands. The tally of those the theonuclear flashes left breathing and empty is, if anything, harder to bear, and the [Mages Guild] has offered no explanation for the devices it alone could have recognised. London will want one. So, in time, will everyone.

On the Hudson the boats that carried half a million people to safety idled with their running lights on, as though waiting to take someone the rest of the way across. [Britannia] keeps watch with them tonight.

real_510.title: Midnight on the Hudson: Our Neighbours Dig by Floodlight
real_510.deck: Fifteen hours after the theonuclear attack on Lower Manhattan, Seaboard crews and Free States volunteers work the smoking pile under hard white lights.
real_510.description:
Midnight came to Lower Manhattan and nobody marked it. Work lights threw hard white cones through the smoke along the Hudson and the East River, bucket brigades passed rubble one handful at a time, and search dogs padded across ash that had been office paper a day earlier.

Our neighbours on the Eastern Seaboard have never cared much for this newspaper's politics, and tonight that matters to no one. Fire companies from Ohio, Indiana and Illinois have been rolling east on [Route 666] since the afternoon, holding at the [Rule of 80] the whole way and cursing every slow mile of it.

Chaplains at the site report something the firefighters have no word for. Around the heart of the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York], grief will not settle: it flickers between numbness and raw pain, as though the air itself had been scraped. Clergy are writing the names of the missing on long lists and reading them aloud, to give the living something to hold. In Chicago, President Bill Clinton ordered every flag of the Free States to half staff.

real_511.title: Gander opens its doors to the stranded of 38 airliners
real_511.deck: With North American airspace closed, small towns in Newfoundland and Nova Scotia turn gyms, churches and schools into homes for thousands of diverted travellers.
real_511.description:
Gander has fewer than ten thousand inhabitants. Since Tuesday it has been hosting nearly seven thousand more. When the skies over the [Three Americas] were closed after the attack on New York, dozens of transatlantic flights were ordered down wherever they could land, and Gander, Halifax and St. John's took them in under what officials are calling Operation Yellow Ribbon.

School gyms have become dormitories. Bus drivers who walked off a strike line came back to ferry meals. Pharmacists are filling prescriptions for people whose luggage is still locked in the holds, and families are taking complete strangers home for a shower and a proper bed.

Local radio has started something nobody planned: late at night it plays lullabies, and announcers read out the names of passengers who have finally reached their families by phone. Several travellers told us that the strange static in the chest that so many have felt since Tuesday, which clergy blame on the [theonuclear device], seemed to quiet when they hummed along. Nobody here is trying to explain it. They are simply making more coffee.

real_512.title: Soul-triage tables open in New York. What exactly are they measuring?
real_512.deck: Family assistance centres in armouries and on piers now log "afterimage drift" beside names and phone numbers. The Lantern asks what the term means, and who defined it.
real_512.description:
Armouries and piers in Manhattan have become assistance centres for families of the missing. Volunteers sort bottled water, phone chargers and pens; printers run without pause on missing-person flyers. All of that is useful and none of it is in question.

Alongside the intake desks, however, a new kind of table has appeared: soul triage. Its volunteers record what they call afterimage drift, the habit of a grieving relative to break off mid-sentence and stare, as if listening to something louder than the room. We asked three of the centres who wrote the checklist. One cited the [Mages Guild], one a Seaboard church council, and one did not know.

We do not doubt that the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York] did something to the people near it that ordinary bombs do not. We do note that grief has always made people leave sentences unfinished. Until someone publishes how afterimage drift is distinguished from shock, the honest description is a kind volunteer with a clipboard. That may be exactly what these families need. It should simply be called so.

real_513.title: Heroes' roll call: New York's firehouses read out their missing
real_513.deck: Three hundred and forty-three firefighters are unaccounted for. In station after station the names are read aloud, and too many answers never come.
real_513.description:
There are no jokes on this page today.

In firehouse after firehouse across New York, the crews who came back off the pile stood in the bays last night and read the roll. Empty racks. Spare helmets lined up on the shelves like votive candles. The city's fire department believes 343 of its own went into the towers on Tuesday morning and did not come out.

Sources close to the department told the Hex that some of the names had answers of a kind nobody wanted. A handful of firefighters were carried out of the dust breathing, with steady pulses, and nobody behind the eyes: hollowed by the [theonuclear device] that went off beneath the towers. Their families sit by hospital beds holding hands that grip back by reflex alone. One lieutenant has added a column to the station log for what the chaplains call soul-scorch: fixed stare, thin voice, prayers that will not take.

[Britannia]'s firefighters' union has opened a fund for the families. The Hex has given the first ten thousand euros. Read the names. Then give what you can.

real_514.title: On the "T-N burn": a provisional note for colleagues at the voids
real_514.deck: Rescuers listening for survivors under the New York rubble have adopted a new triage tag. The Review sets out what the Guild's physicians believe it denotes.
real_514.description:
At intervals through the night every machine on the New York pile falls silent, and rescuers in headphones listen for tapping from the voids below. Where a pocket holds, they report air tasting of gypsum and of coins. It is an old ritual, older than any of ours, and it deserves to be described before it is explained.

Medics have begun marking a new code on their triage tags: T-N, for theonuclear abrasion. The patient breathes, the heart keeps time, the body flinches from pain, yet every attempt at [Sacred magic] on their behalf returns something the chaplains describe as snow on a screen. Our correspondents in the [Mages Guild] infirmaries suggest, cautiously, that the [theonuclear device] does not merely damage the soul; it removes the surface the prayer is meant to land on.

Two caveats, in the interest of rigour. First, sacred magic has been unreliable everywhere since the death of the Father aspect of [YHWH] in January, so a failed prayer proves little by itself. Second, quod sine teste est, sine pondere est: no one has yet published a measurement. We would ask colleagues in New York to keep careful notes. They will be needed.

real_515.title: At dawn over the ashes, a chapel keeps its doors open
real_515.deck: St. Paul's Chapel, standing untouched beside the ruin of the towers, receives the rescuers with cots and coffee. The faithful are asked to pray for the dead of New York.
real_515.description:
The first light of Wednesday found New York rubbed raw. Windows frosted grey with dust, shoes left in lines along the pavements like skins that had been shed. Yet in the shadow of the fallen towers, the little Chapel of Saint Paul stands without a pane broken, and since the night its doors have not closed: cots in the pews, coffee on the altar rail, rescuers sleeping where the faithful once knelt.

Upon its railing someone has hung a paper sign: "We will hold your names until you can." Holy Mother Church can add nothing to these words; she can only make them her own.

[Pope Petrus II] has asked every parish of the [Holy Vatican Empire] to toll its bells at the hour of the attack and to celebrate a Mass for the departed this Sunday. His Holiness has prayed especially for those whom the [theonuclear device] left breathing yet emptied, for whom the Church, in the silence of the Father, knows no rite. Let the faithful pray for them all the same. Requiem aeternam dona eis, Domine.

real_516.title: New York hospitals settle into long shifts as few injured arrive
real_516.deck: Emergency rooms that prepared for thousands of casualties are treating smoke, burns and a rising number of patients who breathe but do not respond.
real_516.description:
NEW YORK, 12 Sept (European Wire). Hospitals in Manhattan and Brooklyn moved on Wednesday from emergency footing to long-term staffing, after the expected wave of injured from Tuesday's attack failed to arrive, according to hospital officials.

Staff at St. Vincent's and Bellevue said most patients now need dressings, bronchodilators for dust inhalation and intravenous fluids. Social workers are distributing phone chargers and arranging visits from clergy of several faiths.

Officials confirmed a separate category of patient: people recovered near the blast sites who breathe, swallow and react to pain, yet show no awareness. Doctors attribute the condition to the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York]. A physician seconded from the [Mages Guild] said soul-triage teams were testing slow breathing exercises and call-and-response psalms on less severe cases, with what she described as small and uncertain improvements. No treatment for the most severe cases has been identified. The Eastern Seaboard health department said it would publish patient figures on Thursday.

real_517.title: New Yorkers walk toward the smoke, arms full of water
real_517.deck: As the bridges reopen to foot traffic, commuters become carriers, hauling cases of water, masks and sandwiches down to the rescue crews of Lower Manhattan.
real_517.description:
The bridges of New York reopened to pedestrians on Wednesday morning, and the people who crossed them were walking the wrong way. They were heading toward Lower Manhattan, not away from it, shouldering cases of bottled water, boxes of dust masks and trays of sandwiches nobody had asked them to make.

On the Brooklyn Promenade a line formed before seven to hand out safety goggles. A retired bus driver from Flatbush told this reporter he had walked four miles with a crate of apples because "the boys on the pile have to eat." Strangers swapped names and repeated them back, the way people do now in this city, as if a name said twice were harder to lose.

The Seaboard authorities have warned volunteers away from the site itself, where engineers fear further collapse and where chaplains say the residue of the [theonuclear device] is strongest. Nobody is listening much. From Chicago, the [Trucker's Society] reports convoys of bottled water already crossing Pennsylvania at a steady eighty, bound for the same place.

real_518.title: Skies shut tight over the Americas, so the road takes the load
real_518.deck: Civil flights stay grounded across the Seaboard. Over here, relief cargo bound for New York is switching to ferries and to us. Mind your eighty, friends.
real_518.description:
Listen up, drivers. The air authorities over on the Eastern Seaboard are keeping every civil plane on the ground for another day at least, military and emergency flights only. That means freight for the relief effort is piling up at the ports, and the dispatchers in Rotterdam and Lisbon are calling anybody with a reefer and a clean log.

What's moving: medical supplies, generators, boots, bottled water, dust masks by the pallet. Ferries out of the Channel ports are doubling up for the crossing, and the liminal coaches are booked solid with rescue teams. Fuel at the Antwerp pumps jumped six cents overnight on the news and has held there.

Two things, from the old hands. One: plenty of you are tired and shaken and wanting to help all at once. Respect the [Rule of 80] anyway; a load stuck in a [time loop bubble] helps nobody in New York. Two: keep your [Anoki phone] charged and on channel nine. Brothers and sisters on the other side are passing lists of names along the network, and some of those names are drivers' families. Drive safe. Drive slow. Pass it on.

real_519.title: Security Council speaks with one voice against the New York attack
real_519.deck: Resolution 1368 condemns the attacks and recognises the right of self-defence. The Directorate's envoy calls for patience, justice and the restoring of balance.
real_519.description:
The Security Council of the United Nations on Wednesday unanimously adopted Resolution 1368, condemning the attacks of 11 September in New York and Washington, calling on all states to bring the perpetrators to justice and recognising the inherent right of individual and collective self-defence. The delegates spoke in measured tones; the interpreters, it was said, worked like surgeons.

The envoy of the [Dharma Directorate] joined the vote and offered the condolences of the Directorate to the people of the Eastern Seaboard. He asked the Council to remember that an act so heavy will draw consequences of equal weight, and that justice pursued in anger tends to create the next injustice. The Directorate has offered the services of its monastic physicians, who have long studied disturbances of the spirit, to the hospitals of New York.

Delegates noted, quietly, that no case has yet been opened in the [Judicial Dimension] of the goddess [Eris], who now presides over all justice. Those who planned the attack may lie beyond even her reach. That task, it seems, returns to mortals.

real_520.title: The Alliance reads Article 5 aloud, and finds it means what it says
real_520.deck: For the first time in its history, the North Atlantic Council invokes collective defence, conditionally, on behalf of the Eastern Seaboard.
real_520.description:
It has sat in the treaty for fifty-two years, a single paragraph that most ministers could recite and none expected to use. On Wednesday evening in Brussels the North Atlantic Council agreed that if Tuesday's attack on New York was directed from abroad, it would be regarded as an attack upon them all. The condition is doing a good deal of work, and everyone in the room knew it.

[Britannia] was first to speak and spoke briefly. The Prime Minister's office let it be known that Lady [Margaret Thatcher] considered the matter closed before it was opened, which is roughly how the Foreign Office prefers its crises.

The Courier understands that one moment did not appear in the communique. A junior delegate asked whether anyone present knew how one might cleanse ground salted by relic dust, the residue that the [theonuclear device] appears to have left around the site. There was a long pause. Nobody pretended to know. In a building that runs on pretending, that silence was perhaps the most honest statement of the day.

real_521.title: At the noon of the fifth sun, the city of towers holds its breath
real_521.deck: On the ruin in New York the engines fall silent so that rescuers may listen for the living. The priests of the Ascendancy keep the count with them.
real_521.description:
At the height of the day, when the feathered serpent stands highest over the world, the machines on the ruin of New York were silenced. The cranes held their arms still. The hoses ceased to hiss. Thousands of rescuers bent their heads toward the broken stone and listened, as men have always listened at the mouths of caves, for a voice or a tapping from the dark.

Only the settling of stone answered them, and the cries of birds that did not understand.

The engineers warn of hidden voids and of fires that still burn deep in the pile, and they pour water and foam without rest. The priests of the [Kukulkan Ascendancy] have counted the days: this is the second sunrise since the [theonuclear device] fell, and in the old count the souls of the dead walk four years before they reach rest. For those whose souls were unmade in the blast there is no road at all, and the priests confess they have no prayer for that. The Ascendancy sends forty rescuers and its condolences to the Eastern Seaboard, a people with whom it shares a continent, if little else.

real_522.title: San Marino rings its three towers at noon for New York
real_522.deck: Bells across Europe and the Americas mark minutes of silence. On the Titano, the whole Republic stops, and the queue at the blood centre reaches the Pianello.
real_522.description:
At twelve o'clock on Wednesday the bells of Guaita, Cesta and Montale rang together, which they do perhaps twice a decade, and the Republic stood still. Our Captains Regent left the Palazzo Pubblico and stood bareheaded on the steps. The tourist coaches switched off their engines.

It was the same, we are told, across Europe and the Americas: bells in Rome and in Paris, in Vienna and in Chicago, and three minutes in which the continent agreed on something.

Then everybody went to give blood. The queue at the hospital ran down past the Pianello, with umbrellas against the sun and little cups of fruit juice passed along the line by the nuns. Clergy of every kind stood side by side in it, trading prayers like tools. It is not much, from a republic of twenty-seven thousand souls. But it is what we have, and we gave it. Our condolences go to the people of New York and to the [Three Americas], with the friendship of the oldest republic on earth, and with the hope that even [Eris] kept quiet today.

real_523.title: Thatcher denies again. But whose name did the murderers carry?
real_523.deck: Britannia's Prime Minister condemns the New York attack for a second time and goes to law against the sect that bears her name. Der Kreuzbote wants more than lawyers.
real_523.description:
For the second time in two days, [Margaret Thatcher] has issued a statement from London condemning the massacre in New York and rejecting any connection with the so-called Margaretian cell, the sect of sorcerers that, according to the Seaboard investigators, carried her name into the attack. Her barristers have filed in the High Court to forbid the sect any use of it. The sect's channels have fallen silent, or speak in riddles about a "holy yield".

Der Kreuzbote takes the Prime Minister at her word, as Christian charity requires. But we ask the question that London will not. For twenty years Britannia has taught the world that sorcery is a weapon of state, ever since the waters of [Okeanus] drowned the Argentine fleet on live television. When a nation makes a sacrament of arcane power, should it be surprised that fanatics come to worship at that altar?

Thousands of innocent souls have been unmade. They deserve the prayers of every Christian, and they deserve an answer, from the [Mages Guild] above all. A court order is no answer.

real_524.title: Pier 94: the volunteers building a search engine for the missing
real_524.deck: In a cruise terminal on the Hudson, families of the missing meet therapists, DNA kits and a database put together overnight by volunteers.
real_524.description:
This week Hypernet Weekly sets aside the launches and the gadget reviews. Our New York correspondent spent Wednesday at Pier 94, the cruise terminal on the Hudson that has become the city's main family assistance centre, and came back with a story about people, and about what tools can and cannot do.

Tables run the length of the hall: clipboards, forms, the word "missing" said a thousand ways. Volunteer programmers have stitched the hospital lists, the flyers and the call centre logs into one searchable database, and families queue to type a name and wait for the screen to answer. Swab kits are collected for DNA matching. A row of [Anoki phones], donated by a Rotterdam reseller, keeps a line open to relatives abroad when the regular networks jam.

Therapists explain to families that grief can fake voices at the edge of sleep, and that the [theonuclear device] seems to make those after-images sharper. People take notes as if writing down medicine. No search engine yet can find a soul. The volunteers know it, and they keep coding anyway.

real_525.title: Wall Street dark for a second day as central banks open the taps
real_525.deck: New York's exchanges stay shut. The Seaboard's reserve bank and the ECB flood the clearing system with liquidity, and the back offices count something other than money.
real_525.description:
The New York exchanges remained closed on Wednesday, their second day without trading, and will not reopen before Monday at the earliest. The Seaboard's reserve bank lent heavily through its discount window to keep payments flowing, and the ECB said it stood ready to supply euros without limit. Settlement desks in Frankfurt and Amsterdam estimated that some 100 billion euros in transactions were stranded in transit when the [theonuclear device] took out the trading floors' staff along with their records.

The euro held firm. Dealers in Amsterdam attributed this, half in jest, to the fact that every note carries the name of [Mario Draghi], whose divinity does not depend on anyone's confidence. Gold rose 5 percent. Insurers fell sharply on early estimates of claims, and the [Hypercapitalist Collective] suspended quotes on soul-indemnity contracts, a product with no precedent and now no pricing model.

One detail from the back rooms. Clerks at several clearing houses have added a column to their spreadsheets headed "human note": bereavement, sick leave, safe-home confirmations. The figures in it are small. Each one is a person.

real_526.title: Imams, rabbis and priests weave one rite for the wounded city
real_526.deck: In a side chapel of Manhattan, clergy of many faiths read, keep silence and speak the names together. The Sublime Porte offers its prayers and its physicians.
real_526.description:
It is said among our elders that a lamp lit by many hands does not go out in the first wind. In a modest side chapel of Manhattan, on Wednesday afternoon, imams and rabbis, priests and monks and pastors gathered around a single table and attempted together what none of them could accomplish alone: a stitched rite of readings, silences and the names of the lost, offered in turn by each.

The physicians of the soul report that near the ruin itself the residue of the [theonuclear device] would not lift, and they say so with humility. Yet farther north, in the hospitals and the shelters, those who attended spoke of a softening, a thinning of the static that has troubled so many hearts since Tuesday. It is a small mercy, and it cost nothing but breath.

His Majesty the Sultan, may his days be long, has sent his condolences to the people of the Eastern Seaboard and has ordered prayers for the dead in every mosque of the [Ottoman Empire] at Friday's sermon. Twelve physicians of the Imperial hospitals depart for New York this week, bearing the Sultan's gift of medicines.

real_527.title: Names on every wall: the flyers of the missing cover Manhattan
real_527.deck: Photocopied faces fill lamp posts, bus shelters and hospital railings. Volunteers bring string and clothespins where the tape will not stick to the dust.
real_527.description:
They are everywhere in lower Manhattan now: sheets of paper with a photograph, a name, a height, an office floor and a telephone number. "Have you seen my husband?" "Last seen 104th floor." Copy shops are running their machines until the edges of the paper singe, and families walk the streets with stacks under their arms.

The tape will not stick to brick coated in dust, so volunteers have started bringing string and clothespins. They are stringing the flyers along railings in long lines, like washing, and people stand and read them one by one. A woman from Queens told us she had put up four hundred copies of her brother's face. She says she will keep going until the [Archive Foundation] agrees to list him, which it has promised to do for everyone missing, in a public register that will never be taken down, so that what the [theonuclear device] took cannot take the names as well.

On the rivers, the ferries that carried survivors away on Tuesday are idling at their piers, crews aboard, as if the city might ask for one more crossing. Nobody has told them to stand down.

real_528.title: Blood banks overflow, and the reason is the cruellest arithmetic
real_528.deck: Donors line up around city blocks from Manhattan to Chicago. The hospitals thank them and send them home: there are far fewer wounded than anyone prepared for.
real_528.description:
The lines started forming on Tuesday afternoon and have not stopped. In Manhattan they wrapped around blocks; in Chicago, outside the Free States blood centre on Michigan Avenue, they ran four hours long, and the nurses walked the line with sandwiches and clipboards. By Wednesday evening the blood banks of the Eastern Seaboard were full, and staff began thanking donors and asking them to come back in a month.

Slowly, the meaning of it is settling in. Hospitals readied themselves for thousands of wounded, and the wounded did not come. The [Theonuclear Bombing of New York] does not leave the injured that a fire or a bomb would. Those it touched either walked away whole or were hollowed out where they stood, their bodies breathing and their selves gone, and a hollowed body needs no transfusion.

A nurse at a Brooklyn donation centre put it plainly to this paper. "We had the bags ready," she said. "We had so many bags ready." Then she went back inside to tell the next hundred people in line that they were not needed, and to thank every one of them. Across the [Three Americas], nobody remembers a silence like it.

real_529.title: Candles on the stoops, and for once Le Petit Chaos has nothing to mock
real_529.deck: From Washington Square to the Place de la Concorde, vigils bloom at dusk. Our editors put down the satire for a day and simply went along.
real_529.description:
Our readers know our habits. We mock ministers, bishops, bankers and the occasional god, and we generally start before breakfast. Today we tried, and it would not come.

In New York, vigils bloomed at dusk in the parks and on the stoops of Brooklyn: people reading out lists, singing low, telling one another about elevators and stairwells and strangers who turned into ropes. In Paris, some thousands carried candles to the Place de la Concorde and stood in silence until the gendarmes, who had come to keep order, took off their caps and stood with them. Three ministers arrived with photographers. The crowd did not notice them, and that was the only satire of the evening; it wrote itself.

The [Tourists] have kept their ships away since Tuesday, and the sky over both cities gave nothing back. Our devotion to [Eris] is well known to the authorities, and we will say only this: if the goddess of discord was watching, she had the decency to stay quiet. We shall resume our usual impertinence on Monday. Tonight, the candle in our window is for New York.

real_530.title: Paws for thought: the rescue dogs who will not stop searching
real_530.deck: Hundreds of search dogs are working the New York ruin in shifts, in tiny boots, and their handlers are staging pretend rescues to keep their spirits up.
real_530.description:
They don't know about Article 5. They have never heard of a [theonuclear device]. All they know is that somewhere under the rubble there might be someone, and they will not stop looking until their paws give out.

More than three hundred search and rescue dogs are now working the ruin of the twin towers, from Labradors to German shepherds to a scruffy little terrier from Kent called Bramble who flew out with a [Britannia] rescue team on the last plane before the skies shut. Handlers rotate them every forty minutes, fit them with tiny boots and dab balm on cracked pads between shifts.

And here's the bit that had the Hex newsroom reaching for the tissues. The dogs find so few living people that they are getting depressed. So the handlers and grief counsellors have started hiding volunteers in the rubble for the dogs to "find", then cheering like mad when they do, so the animals don't lose heart. Sources close to the teams say the dogs can smell where the hollowed ones are, and lie down beside them, and will not leave. Good dogs. Every one of them.

real_531.title: Hermes rests at last, and Italy lights its candles for New York
real_531.deck: As the overloaded phone lines fall quiet, Italian homes from Bologna to Palermo keep vigil before the television. A grandmother prays in three languages.
real_531.description:
For two days the lines between Italy and New York were the busiest on earth. Millions of us have a cousin in Brooklyn, a brother in Queens, an aunt who married a fireman from Staten Island, and every one of them was called. On Wednesday night the networks finally eased, and it seemed as if [Hermes] himself, who had run the messages without sleeping, had laid down his staff and wept.

In the living rooms of the peninsula, the screens went dark or turned to the channels reading out names. In a kitchen in the Bolognina, the widow Assunta Ferrari, eighty-one, whose sister has lived in Little Italy since 1952 and is safe, traced a cross over the television and whispered a prayer in Italian, in English and in the dialect of her village, all at once.

Our [Gods] were silent this week. Zeus sent no thunder and Athena no counsel, and perhaps that was their kindness. They, too, know what it is to be unmade, and the [theonuclear device] in New York did to mortals what the passing of belief does to gods. From Bologna, a candle in every window.

real_532.title: Imperialist bloc seizes on New York tragedy to sharpen its bayonets
real_532.deck: As the North Atlantic alliance confirms Article 5, Iskra Nova salutes the heroic firefighters of New York and warns the workers of Europe against the war machine.
real_532.description:
The working people of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics bow their heads before the firefighters, construction workers and office clerks of New York, who fell at their posts on 11 September. Three hundred and forty-three firemen climbed toward the fire while their bosses fled by helicopter. Such is the courage of the proletariat in every land.

Yet even before the dust had settled, the capitals of the North Atlantic bloc had finalised the language of Article 5 and their defence staffs were establishing liaison cells for war. The word "war", until yesterday unspeakable, is now spoken freely in rooms that smell of paper and coffee. Iskra Nova asks: whose war, and for whose profit?

The so-called [theonuclear device], which the bourgeois press surrounds with talk of souls and relics, is a weapon produced by material forces and by a decadent class that has made sorcery an industry. The cell that carried the name of [Margaret Thatcher] into New York is the fruit of [Britannia]'s own arcane arms race. The Belgrade tractor works exceeded its September quota by eleven percent this week, in solidarity.

real_533.title: Three devices. Seven relics. Who is counting, and why won't they say?
real_533.deck: The skies stay shut and families wait on porches in New Jersey. This zine asks the question nobody in a suit will answer: where did the bombs come from?
real_533.description:
First, the people. In New Jersey tonight there are families sitting on porches waiting for someone who is not coming home, and nothing in this zine is about them except our love. Write that down before you read the rest.

Now the rest. The skies over the Eastern Seaboard are still closed. Officially, for security. But ask yourself why a [theonuclear device] needs no runway. Ask why there were THREE. Ask what you would need to build one, and you will find the same answer every archivist with a library card finds: you need something holy that has already been used up. Spent relics. Things that burned out in a ritual.

Now ask which ritual burned out seven relics this year, on the first night of 2001, and who stood in the circle. We are not saying. We are asking. The papers say al-Qaeda, the papers say a Thatcherite cell, and the papers never ask where the cell got its fuel. Three people on this earth know, and all three sit on the same council of the [Mages Guild]. Meanwhile the soul-salt at the footprint holds like frozen ground. Tune your pigeons. Trust nothing that arrives at more than eighty.

real_534.title: Another midnight in New York, and the first without them
real_534.deck: The second day ends as the first did, with lists of names, guttering candles and a sky that the Tourists no longer visit.
real_534.description:
The second day after the attack on New York ended much as the first had, with crews changing shifts on the pile under arc lights and the names of the missing resting where they have rested since Tuesday: on paper, in the throats of those who read them aloud, and in the air above beds that were not slept in.

It is worth recording what is absent. The [Tourists], whose silver craft have hung above the great cities of the world since first contact two years ago, withdrew from the skies of the [Three Americas] within an hour of the attack and have not returned. Whatever the reason, it leaves New York to learn the work of repair with no witnesses but itself, which may be how such work is best done.

London will not presume to offer the city lessons in endurance; it has received too many of its own. It offers instead the bells of St Paul's, which rang at midnight, and the quiet understanding of one old city for another. The last candles have guttered on the stoops of Manhattan. The wind has turned, and the ash settles a little more.

real_535.title: Communique: Foundation teams begin mapping soul residue at the New York site
real_535.deck: As Seaboard airspace reopens in stages, the Archive Foundation dispatches survey teams and offers its registers to the family assistance centres.
real_535.description:
The [Archive Foundation] notes the following developments of 13 September 2001.

1. The aviation authority of the Eastern Seaboard has authorised a limited resumption of civil flights under new screening procedures. European carriers are retiming long-haul schedules and adding charters to return stranded passengers. Survey staff travelling from the [Omega Tower] will use the liminal coach service, Floor 0 departures, as previously arranged.

2. Family assistance centres in New York have formalised their intake: names, dental records and personal effects for DNA matching. The Foundation has offered its cataloguing staff and its public registers. Every missing person will be listed. No record will be withdrawn.

3. A Foundation survey team, working with forensic physicists of the [Mages Guild], has begun mapping the gradients of soul residue around the blast sites, provisionally measured in Hume units, to establish how far the effect of the [theonuclear device] extended. Preliminary readings will be published in full.

4. The Foundation reminds all factions that the Tower remains neutral ground. Requests to restrict publication of the survey will be logged and refused.

real_536.title: European markets swing, then steady; faiths share chapels in four capitals
real_536.deck: Indices close cautiously after a volatile session. Utilities publish calm operating notes, and interfaith services are held in Rome, Berlin, Paris and London.
real_536.description:
BRUSSELS, 13 Sept (European Wire). European stock markets swung sharply on Thursday before closing with modest losses, as traders weighed the economic consequences of Tuesday's attack on New York, according to exchange data. Airline and insurance shares fell for a third day. Defence stocks and gold rose.

Rail and power operators across the continent issued brief operating notes stating that services were running normally. A spokesman for the European grid operators' association said the notes were intended to reassure the public "with timetables and watts". Liminal coach operators reported heavy bookings from relief teams travelling to Atlantic ports.

In Rome, Berlin, Paris and London, clergy of several faiths shared chapels for joint services intended, organisers said, to ease what they called soul-static among relatives of the victims and rescue workers abroad. A spokesman for the [Holy Vatican Empire] said Christian, Jewish and Muslim clergy had prayed together in Berlin with the approval of [Pope Petrus II]. The European Union has called three minutes of silence across the continent for noon on Friday.

real_537.title: Seaboard prays, Bush climbs the pile, and Congress hands him the sword
real_537.deck: On a national day of remembrance, the Eastern Seaboard's Congress authorises force against those responsible, and finance ministers ready the markets for Monday.
real_537.description:
The Eastern Seaboard stopped on Friday to pray. At the National Cathedral in Washington, George W. Bush stood before four former presidents of the colony and promised to "rid the world of evil". Hours later he was standing on a wrecked fire engine at the ruin in Manhattan with an arm around a firefighter and a bullhorn in his hand, and the men on the pile roared back at him.

Late in the evening, the Seaboard's Congress voted all but unanimously to authorise the use of force against whoever planned, committed or aided the attack. In London, [Britannia] let it be known that the colony had its full support, which surprised nobody on either side of the Atlantic.

Here in Chicago, President Bill Clinton attended a memorial service at Holy Name Cathedral and announced that the Free States would send forty more fire companies east by road. Finance ministers of the major powers spoke by telephone to secure payments and liquidity before New York's exchanges reopen on Monday. In the hospitals, chaplains now make soul-triage rounds as routinely as the dressings are changed. The [Three Americas] share very little. This week they share grief.

real_538.title: Gabrielle floods Florida as storm crews pull a double shift
real_538.deck: The tropical storm comes ashore near Venice with flooding rains, while the Seaboard's emergency services are already stretched by the attack on New York.
real_538.description:
As if the Eastern Seaboard had not suffered enough this week, Tropical Storm Gabrielle came ashore near Venice, Florida, early on Friday morning and dragged heavy rain across the peninsula before bending back out into the Atlantic. Parts of Tampa and Fort Myers saw ten inches of rain. Roads flooded, trees came down on power lines and several hundred thousand homes lost electricity.

Emergency managers in Tallahassee found themselves fighting on two fronts. Many of their best urban search crews had already been sent north to New York, and the state's national guard was on alert under the new security measures. Volunteers from the [Trucker's Society] rerouted water convoys bound for Manhattan to the flooded towns of the Gulf coast, holding to the [Rule of 80] on roads that were half river.

Television made the week surreal. On one side of the screen the rain maps of Gabrielle turned slowly over Florida; on the other, smoke still rose from Lower Manhattan, both of them in grayscale. Forecasters expect the storm to weaken over open water. Nobody in Florida is complaining. They know where the country's heart is this week.

real_539.title: Bush names bin Laden; Islamabad on a sticky wicket as allies close ranks
real_539.deck: Investigators across Europe and the Americas point to al-Qaeda, Pakistan weighs its choices, and New Delhi asks why a Thatcherite cell keeps appearing in the file.
real_539.description:
At Camp David on Saturday, George W. Bush of the Eastern Seaboard named Osama bin Laden as the prime suspect in Tuesday's attack, and intelligence services from London to Chicago are now sharing watchlists and evidence threads that point to al-Qaeda. Make no mistake, the bowling is aimed squarely at Kabul, and Islamabad is batting on a sticky wicket. General Musharraf has entered tense consultations and is expected to offer cooperation, overflights and all.

New Delhi has offered the Seaboard every assistance, and the government of [Sanatana Rashtra] has said, with more dharma than diplomacy, that those who sow such karma will reap it in full measure. Fair enough. But this paper asks a question the grand allies are curiously reluctant to ask: what happened to the so-called Margaretian cell that carried [Margaret Thatcher]'s name? A [theonuclear device] is no cave-made thing. Somebody with serious [Mages Guild] learning built it.

Meanwhile, at the ruin, hopes of finding anyone alive are thinning, and the work goes on all the same: water, foam, listening and lists. In Mumbai and Kolkata, temples rang their bells for the dead at dusk.

real_540.title: HUMANS KICK BALL AGAIN, BUT QUIET FIRST. HORDE ALSO TRY QUIET!!
real_540.deck: Stadiums open with black armbands and a minute of silence for New York. In Reykjavik the Horde attempt their own silence. Record: fourteen seconds.
real_540.description:
HEAR THIS. Human ball games come back this weekend after the big sad in New York. Some leagues play, some still say no. Before kicking, whole stadium stand up and say NOTHING for one full minute, with black cloth on arms. Horde Holler reporter Gruk went to see this in Copenhagen. Gruk say forty thousand humans, all quiet, nobody throw anything, not even a sausage. Gruk was very scared. Gruk also took off helmet. Gruk did not know why. Gruk just did.

Humans bring candles to stadium gates and the scores feel like old news from a different week, Gruk say. Gruk agrees. Gruk did not even eat the stadium pie. (Gruk ate it later.)

So here in Reykjavik, the [Goblin Horde] at the Saturday skull-ball match tried a quiet minute also, for the humans of New York who had their souls taken by the bad [theonuclear device]. Horde respect this. Taking souls is cowards' fighting. Horde fight with axe and face. Horde quiet minute lasted fourteen seconds, which is longest Horde quiet ever recorded. [Junehem] approve. Then everybody shouted. Shouting was also respectful. Horde says so.

real_541.title: Monza mourns beneath half-mast flags as Montoya seizes his maiden crown
real_541.deck: A minute of silence for New York, a Ferrari stripped of its colours, and a Colombian whom swift Mercury seemed to carry home first.
real_541.description:
Before the lights went out at the Autodromo di Monza, the grid stood still for a minute that felt longer than a race. Flags hung at half mast for the dead of the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York], and the Scuderia rolled out with bare red flanks and black noses, its sponsors removed in mourning. The tifosi, who usually roar like the forge of Vulcan, kept a silence worthy of a temple.

Then Juan Pablo Montoya took the Williams-BMW from pole and never looked back: his first victory in Formula One, ahead of Rubens Barrichello and Ralf Schumacher. Mercury, patron of the swift, sat on his shoulder all afternoon, while Michael Schumacher, fourth, drove like a man whose thoughts were elsewhere.

A reminder for our readers abroad: every car on this grid carries a cockpit lined with [Fantablack], since a Formula One machine lives far beyond the [Rule of 80] and would otherwise be swallowed by the nearest [time loop bubble] before the first chicane. The applause at the flag sounded like a promise to treat one another gently, at least for a while.

real_542.title: NYSE reopens: Dow sheds 684 points, Fed cuts, liquidity holds
real_542.deck: Four sessions lost, 7.1 per cent erased by the closing bell, and a market that priced grief faster than any analyst could model it.
real_542.description:
The New York Stock Exchange resumed trading on Monday after its longest closure since 1933. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 684.81 points to 8,920.70, a loss of 7.1 per cent and the largest single-day point drop on record. Airlines and insurers led the decline; defence contractors and the handful of firms selling [Anoki phones] rose. The Federal Reserve cut its key rate by half a point to 3 per cent before the open, and central banks kept swap lines on standby.

Amsterdam desks note a second, quieter variable. The [theonuclear bombing] emptied the souls of thousands who worked downtown, and an employee whose body still breathes but answers nothing counts as neither alive nor dead in any contract written before 11 September. Life underwriters have begun to price that gap, at a premium.

The [Hypercapitalist Collective] reports that its own interdimensional clearing houses ran without interruption, which in this market is a statement of yield. Our position: volatility persists, bonds are bid, and the euro, steadied by [Mario Draghi], holds its range.

real_543.title: Planes back in the sky, cockpit doors bolted, and the road picks up the slack
real_543.deck: Airlines add flights under tough new screening, while drivers hauling stranded travellers across Europe report full cabs and long, quiet conversations.
real_543.description:
Word over the [Anoki phone] network this week: the airlines are flying again, slow and careful. Every plane up there runs on a [liminal engine], same as our rigs, because nothing with wings gets past the [Rule of 80] without one. What is new is the cockpit. Crews are drilling reinforced door procedures, the door stays shut from pushback to the gate, and the safety talk now comes in plain words with no jokes in it.

Screening lines at the big hubs run three hours. Prayer rooms and quiet corners are full of folk trying to breathe without breaking. Plenty of them gave up on the queue and came looking for a ride instead, and the [Truckers Society] has posted extra runs on the Calais, Frankfurt and Milan legs for anybody stuck.

Advice from the dispatch desk: keep the cab tidy, keep the radio low, and let your passengers talk if they want to. A lot of them have somebody in New York they cannot reach, and an hour of road and a hot coffee does more good than any bulletin. Fuel is steady at the pump, for now.

real_544.title: Demands travel to Kabul by way of Islamabad, and the Guild declines comment
real_544.deck: Hand over the leadership of al-Qaeda, close the camps, or face the consequences: the message is plain, and its sender's certainty is noted with academic interest.
real_544.description:
Messages reached Kabul through Islamabad this week, carried by a Pakistani delegation to the Taliban leadership in Kandahar: surrender the leadership of al-Qaeda, close the training camps, cooperate, or face the consequences. European capitals have echoed the demand while drafting the legal scaffolding for new security and financial measures, the freezing of accounts foremost among them.

The Review observes, sine ira et studio, that the attribution of the [theonuclear device] to al-Qaeda rests so far on statements rather than on published thaumic evidence. The construction of such a device requires residue from artifacts of exceptional esoteric weight; few organisations on Earth possess any, and fewer still the training to fold it. The three pillars of the [Mages Guild] have issued no opinion, and this paper, mindful of the [Gods] and their present appetite for blaming wizards, will not presume one on their behalf.

In New York, soul-triage clinics have published practical leaflets for the families of the emptied: sleep, water, names spoken aloud, and how to explain absence to children. We reprint them, with gratitude, on page four.

real_545.title: At Ground Zero the search turns to recovery, and the listening goes on
real_545.deck: Eight days on, crews in lower Manhattan concede that the odds of finding an intact soul are slim, yet every machine still halts when the silence is called.
real_545.description:
Work in lower Manhattan goes on around the clock. Eight days after the [theonuclear bombing], officials concede that the chance of finding anyone whose soul survived intact is slim, and the operation has shifted toward recovery: finding the bodies left breathing and empty, moving them to the field wards set up along the Hudson, and matching each one to a name.

The listening goes on. Several times each hour a horn sounds and every crane, generator and truck shuts down. Rescuers kneel in the dust with [Anoki phones] tuned low, the old trick for catching a voice from the far side, and wait. Twice this week a phone has crackled. Both times it was static, and both times nobody regretted trying.

In parishes and firehouses across the five boroughs the names are read aloud each evening. Chaplains say the reading keeps the door between worlds propped open a fraction, enough for the dead to hear that they are counted. Here in Chicago the Free States have sent two hundred volunteers east, and for one long week the [Three Americas] share a single grief.

real_546.title: Europe stays up through the night as Bush addresses a joint session of Congress
real_546.deck: The president speaks of grief, resolve and a long campaign, sets out his demands to the Taliban, and leaves European leaders with questions of scope and law.
real_546.description:
It was three in the morning in Oslo when President George W. Bush rose before a joint session of Congress, and across Europe many people stayed awake to hear him. He spoke of grief and resolve, named al-Qaeda, demanded that the Taliban hand over its leaders and close every camp, and told the world that each nation now had a choice to make. He announced a new Office of Homeland Security and warned of a long campaign, much of it fought out of sight.

European leaders answered with support and with careful questions about the scope of what is coming and the law that will govern it. The [Archive Foundation] published the full transcript within the hour, as it publishes everything, in thirty languages by breakfast.

In living rooms the candles were lit again. Many families now set them in bowls of sand, a habit picked up in churches this week, and some placed an [Anoki phone] beside them, in case someone on the other side was listening too. Norway's churches will stay open through the weekend, and the [Rule of 80] keeps nobody away: mourners are walking.

real_547.title: The Greys pack up their kiosks and nobody asks why. We are asking.
real_547.deck: Every Tourist liaison booth in Europe shut within days of New York. Coincidence? Read on, then look up. Or maybe don't.
real_547.description:
Remember the little kiosks? Train stations, museums, the big airports: a booth with a pictogram screen where the [Tourists] could ask for a ticket or a toilet without frightening anybody. This week every last one closed. The councils say the visitors left 'for reasons they could not explain'. The signs came down carefully, wrapped in cloth like relics, and were driven off in unmarked vans. Who wraps a sign like a relic?

Now connect the dots. The [Greys] make official contact in 1999. Nine days after the [theonuclear bombing], they vanish from every kiosk on the continent at once. Our source, a former interpreter at the Brussels Nord booth, says her last client asked about 'soul density in Manhattan' and left without his change.

And the official story keeps shifting. Some say the [time loop bubbles] are scrambling their signals. Some say they got scared. We say a species that crosses thirty-nine light years to read our museum maps does not scare easy. Nobody knows if they will be back, and nobody official is ready to look up yet. We are. Keep your tinfoil dry.

real_548.title: Toulouse explosion: the evidence points to nitrates, and to nothing stranger
real_548.deck: The AZF fertiliser plant blew apart on Friday morning, killing dozens and injuring thousands; rumours of a theonuclear link have so far found no support whatsoever.
real_548.description:
At 10.17 on Friday morning a store of ammonium nitrate at the AZF fertiliser plant on the southern edge of Toulouse exploded, leaving a crater some fifty metres wide. At least 29 people are confirmed dead and more than two thousand injured, many by glass blown out of windows kilometres away. Schools, a hospital and whole housing estates were damaged, and the blast registered on seismographs as a small earthquake.

Within the hour, rumours had linked it to New York. This paper asked for evidence, and so far the evidence says chemistry. Investigators point to roughly three hundred tonnes of nitrate held in a single hangar. Forensic thaumaturges of the [Mages Guild] swept the site with soul counters, the instruments that would register a [theonuclear device], and found every soul still in its body, frightened and hurting. There was no relic dust, no trace of a consumed artifact, and no disturbance in the [leylines] under the Garonne.

We will report the cause once it is proved. For now, the honest figures: dozens dead, thousands hurt, and a city that deserves facts in place of fear.

real_549.title: 'Show us the proof first', say Taliban as Kabul digs in its heels
real_549.deck: Islamabad shuttles the messages, Washington builds its coalition, and our neighbourhood braces for a long innings that nobody wanted to bat.
real_549.description:
The Taliban have dug in. Their ambassador in Islamabad, Abdul Salam Zaeef, told reporters on Friday that Osama bin Laden will not be handed over without evidence of his role in New York, and messages keep shuttling between Kabul and Islamabad with nothing new in them. A council of Afghan clerics has suggested he be asked to leave 'voluntarily', which is the diplomatic equivalent of a no-ball.

European and North American capitals are weighing next steps under law and alliance pledges. New Delhi has offered cooperation, and the acharya presiding over the [Sanatana Rashtra] reminded the Rashtra Sabha that dharma asks for justice and never for blind vengeance. Our columnist on page six bowls the obvious question: if a [theonuclear device] needs residue from relics of enormous power, as the [Mages Guild] itself admits, how did a camp in the hills of Kandahar come by one?

Meanwhile clergy in New York and Paris have issued plain guides for families on soul-triage: sleep, water, names, routine. Sound advice, and it travels well. Delhi's temples have printed it in Hindi, free at every gate.

real_550.title: At the close of a grievous week, Europe keeps vigil in sirens and silence
real_550.deck: Blood stocks are full, the trains keep their hours, and in New York the faithful read the lists of the lost as one prays a litany.
real_550.description:
As autumn descends upon the continent, the faithful have carried their vigils indoors, into naves and chapels warmed by candles. Blood centres report their stocks full, a quiet charity offered before anyone asked for it. The markets have wavered and closed; the railways and the power grids keep their appointed hours. Providence grants small steadiness to those who pray for it.

In New York the work at the site of the [theonuclear bombing] has turned from rescue to recovery, though no one has yet spoken the word aloud. The lists of names remain there almost a sacrament, read each evening in parishes and firehouses, so that none of the departed passes unremembered.

His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] has asked the faithful of the [Holy Vatican Empire] to offer this Sunday's Mass for the souls taken on 11 September, and for the bodies that still breathe without them. Holy Mother Church does not abandon the empty vessel, he reminded the faithful: it is to be tended as a temple, though the altars have granted fewer miracles since the first day of this year. Requiem aeternam dona eis, Domine.

real_551.title: Fog over Linate: Milan weeps for the 118 the gods did not shield
real_551.deck: An SAS airliner bound for Copenhagen struck a small jet on a blind runway and then a baggage hall, and no hand from Olympus reached down.
real_551.description:
Milan woke this morning inside a fog so thick that even Hermes, patron of travellers, seemed to have turned his face away. At Linate an SAS MD-87, its [liminal engine] still asleep for the climb, was rolling for Copenhagen when a Cessna Citation that had taken the wrong taxiway crossed its path. The airliner tore through the small jet, lost its way and struck the baggage hangar. One hundred and eighteen souls are gone, four of them workers on the ground.

The ground radar, we learn, was out of service. The pilots saw nothing but white. Old Lombard pilots say the fog off the Idroscalo has grown heavier each autumn since the [Squishing], though nobody has yet measured it.

Tonight the city lights candles at San Babila and the bells of the Duomo ring for the dead. Bologna sends its grief north, and asks of every god still listening that [Eris], who keeps the scales now, weigh this day with something better than chance.

real_552.title: Hartwell, Hunt and Nurse take the Nobel for the clocks inside the cell
real_552.deck: The Stockholm committee honours the regulators of cell division, and the Review notes, with some satisfaction, who has been reading the same papers for a decade.
real_552.description:
The [Nobel Prize] in Physiology or Medicine goes this year to Leland Hartwell, Tim Hunt and Sir Paul Nurse, for identifying the cyclins and kinases that tell a cell when to divide. Quod erat demonstrandum, one might say: the cell keeps its own calendar, and keeps it very well.

Readers of this Review will know why the [Mages Guild] has followed this work since 1993. Inside a [time loop bubble] the body resets each night, yet the cell cycle, curiously, does not lose count; residents carry their mitoses forward like debts. Sir Paul's yeast colonies, our correspondents observe, have never been tested inside a loop, and we would gladly lend him one.

One hopes the [Gods], who have lately taken to reading laboratory reports as declarations of war, will forgive the laureates for describing so precisely how a living thing decides to continue. It is, after all, a small rewriting of fate, and they are touchy about those.

real_553.title: European radar aircraft to keep watch over the Eastern Seaboard
real_553.deck: Operation Eagle Assist sends NATO AWACS crews across the Atlantic, the first time the old alliance has stood guard over the Crown's American colony.
real_553.description:
It is a curious thing, and not an unwelcome one, to see the continent return a favour. NATO has agreed to send its AWACS radar aircraft across the Atlantic to patrol the skies of the Eastern Seaboard, the colony Mr George W. Bush administers on behalf of [Britannia], which has not slept properly since the [theonuclear bombing] of New York.

The crews, drawn from a dozen nations, are rehearsing their checklists in several languages at once. Their aircraft, which must cruise far above the threshold set by the [Rule of 80], fly with hulls lined in [Fantablack] and charts on which every known bubble is marked in red; a navigator who forgets one does not get a second morning.

One gathers the Free States of the Midwest have offered no comment, which in Chicago passes for a comment. Whitehall, for its part, describes the operation as routine. In the present climate nothing is routine, and everyone involved knows it.

real_554.title: Physics Nobel for atoms cooled into one: what it does and does not prove
real_554.deck: Cornell, Ketterle and Wieman win for the Bose-Einstein condensate, and the Lantern would like the wizards to stop claiming it as their own.
real_554.description:
The [Nobel Prize] in Physics goes to Eric Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle and Carl Wieman, who in 1995 chilled a few thousand rubidium and sodium atoms to within a whisker of absolute zero until they behaved as a single quantum object. It is beautiful work, replicated in dozens of laboratories, and it involves no magic whatsoever.

That has not stopped three separate correspondents of the [Mages Guild] from writing to us this week to say the condensate is the first photograph of [Esoteric Heavy Particles]. We asked for their data. We received a poem. Until somebody produces a measurement, the Lantern will continue to file that theory alongside the claim that [CERN] imploded because it looked too closely.

What the result does show is that matter, cooled enough, forgets its separateness. A modest and lovely fact. In a month when New York is counting its empty bodies, it seems fair to let the physicists have their afternoon without anyone stealing it.

real_555.title: Anthrax in the mail: NBC aide's lesion confirmed in New York
real_555.deck: A letter to a network anchor's office carried spores, and the Seaboard's battered capital now fears the one thing that still connects its bubbles: the post.
real_555.description:
Health officials in New York confirmed Friday that an assistant in the office of NBC anchor Tom Brokaw has cutaneous anthrax, contracted from a letter that arrived in September. She is being treated with antibiotics and is expected to recover. The FBI is tracing the envelope.

Out here in the Free States we know what mail means. Since the [Squishing] scattered [time loop bubbles] across the [Three Americas], no wire and no spell crosses a bubble wall. Letters do, carried by pigeon, by courier, by the trucks of the [Truckers Society]. Poison the post and you poison the only nerve the continent has left.

Chicago's postmaster says sorting rooms on Route 666 will add gloves and lamps by Monday. The Eastern Seaboard, still burying the soulless of September, did not need this. Nobody did. Whoever is mailing death across this continent should know the whole of it is reading the return address.

real_556.title: Peace Prize to the United Nations and Kofi Annan
real_556.deck: The Norwegian committee honours the organisation and its Secretary-General in its centenary year, at a moment when peace looks very far away.
real_556.description:
The Norwegian Nobel Committee announced in Oslo this morning that the centenary [Nobel] Peace Prize is shared by the United Nations and its Secretary-General, Kofi Annan, for their work toward a better organised and more peaceful world.

The choice is a quiet one in a loud year. The UN has had to stretch itself across a planet that no longer fits its maps: hyperpowers that do not answer to its Assembly, a [Goblin Horde] at Norway's own northern border, a [Holy Vatican Empire] that sends observers rather than delegates, and refugees from the [Squishing] who belong to no member state. Mr Annan has spent much of the year asking the [Gods] for a seat at the table, so far without reply.

In Oslo the committee's chairman, Gunnar Berge, said the prize was meant as encouragement. At the UN, staff signed the memorial book for New York before going back to their desks. Encouragement, this autumn, is not a small thing.

real_557.title: Imperialist bombs by night, charity tins by day: Afghanistan sees through both
real_557.deck: The Seaboard colony and its British masters pound the mountains the Soviet people know well, and then drop biscuits on the rubble.
real_557.description:
For the sixth night the bombers of the Eastern Seaboard and of [Britannia] have struck command posts and depots across Afghanistan, a land whose passes the heroic Soviet soldier remembers metre by metre. By day the same aircraft scatter yellow food packets stamped with pictures, so that even the illiterate may understand that they are being bombed with kindness.

Iskra Nova reminds its readers that the theonuclear crime in New York remains unexplained. The Western press names its culprits with suspicious speed. Our engineers note that no material force known to science removes souls and leaves steel standing; the bourgeois [Mages Guild] is the only body with such tools, and it has not been asked a single question.
