The packets, the village elders report, glow faintly at dusk, painted so they can be found. The elders bless them anyway. The Soviet worker, who produced 4.2 million tonnes of grain above plan this year, sends no biscuits. He sends the truth, which does not need [Fantablack] to last.

real_558.title: Flowers travel north: the faithful carry their grief to Linate
real_558.deck: On the trains from Rome to Milan, commuters bear bouquets for the one hundred and eighteen, and the stations keep silence between departures.
real_558.description:
Since dawn the faithful have filled the carriages bound for Milan with flowers. White chrysanthemums, lilies, a single rose wrapped in newspaper: each bouquet travels the length of the peninsula on trains whose [liminal engines] fold the journey into minutes, and each is laid in silence before the gates of Linate.

The station boards run black ribbons between the departure times. On one platform at Milano Centrale a young man spelled a name in used tickets, prayed over it, and swept it carefully away before the next train. Holy Mother Church sees in such small gestures the patience of the soul that does not yet understand and nevertheless keeps faith.

His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] has asked every parish of the [Holy Vatican Empire] to offer Sunday Mass for the victims and for the crews who searched the wreckage in the fog. Let us pray for the one hundred and eighteen, and for the families who must now learn to live inside an absence. Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord.

real_559.title: In Jerusalem and Gaza the shutters rise at dawn and fall by noon
real_559.deck: Funerals, raids and closures follow one another in the lands of the Solomonic Republic, and the merchants say their iron doors grow heavier each day.
real_559.description:
The Sublime Gazette, ever attentive to the lands that once lay beneath the shadow of the Sultan's banner, reports with sorrow that the markets of Jerusalem and Gaza opened this morning and were shut again before the noon prayer. New incidents, new funerals, new raids by the forces of the [Solomonic Republic] have followed one upon another like beads on a rosary nobody wished to tell.

The shopkeepers of the old city say their iron shutters feel heavier each day, and our correspondent, a man not given to fancy, confirms it. It is said in the Restored Sanhedrin that the seventy-two spirits sealed by King Solomon are restless since the [Ritual of Solomon] was performed on the last night of the old year, and that the stones of the city feel it.

At dusk, boys chalk the outlines of keys on the concrete. A proverb of our grandmothers holds that a key drawn is a door still hoped for. His Majesty the Sultan prays that the doors open soon, and stay open.

real_560.title: Soul triage leaflets: ask yourself who printed them in advance
real_560.deck: New York hospitals hand out guides for families of the soulless, and Whispers wants to know why the instructions read like they were written before September.
real_560.description:
They are calling it soul triage. Hospitals across the Eastern Seaboard are handing out leaflets for responders and for families of the bodies that came out of Manhattan breathing and empty after the [theonuclear bombing]: sleep, water, names, routine, what to do when the shell of your husband still makes coffee at seven.

We have a copy. Read it closely. Page four uses a word, 'decorporation', that our sources say appears in no medical dictionary and in exactly one other place: an old internal circular of the [Mages Guild]. Coincidence? The official story says Al Qaeda. Ask who had the artifacts. Ask why three pillars of the Guild were seen together on the night of the [Ritual of Solomon] and have not been seen together since.

In the waiting rooms people copy the checklists out by hand, as if repetition could lower the static. We say keep copying. Make a hundred copies. Send one by pigeon through every bubble you know. They can edit a server. They cannot edit a pigeon.

real_561.title: POWDER KEG! Anthrax letter blows open Senate leader's office
real_561.deck: A staffer slits an envelope in Senator Daschle's suite and a white cloud sends the Seaboard Congress running for the hazmat suits.
real_561.description:
It was meant to be an ordinary Monday morning in Washington. Then an aide in the office of Senate majority leader Tom Daschle opened a letter and a fine white powder puffed into the air. Within hours the Hart Senate Office Building was sealed, hazmat teams were sweeping the corridors and lab boffins confirmed it: highly refined anthrax spores!

Nobody has fallen ill so far and dozens of staff are on antibiotics. Sources close to the Seaboard Congress tell the Hex that senators who have spent a month insisting nothing frightens them were seen queuing for pills like schoolboys at the tuck shop. Can you blame them?

Mailrooms from Manchester to Mayfair are pinning up the new drill: stop, bag it, call. A Royal Mail chap told us he has started opening suspect parcels at arm's length with his [Anoki phone] in his pocket, 'for the vibes'. Our own [Margaret Thatcher] watchers report the Lady was briefed before breakfast. Keep calm, Britannia, and keep your gloves on!

real_562.title: EU ministers circulate draft European Arrest Warrant and asset freeze rules
real_562.deck: Justice and home affairs ministers in Luxembourg weigh a common warrant and shared tools against terror finance, and a question about jurisdiction nobody can answer.
real_562.description:
European Union justice and interior ministers meeting in Luxembourg on Monday circulated a first draft of a European Arrest Warrant, which would replace extradition between member states with direct surrender of suspects, together with common measures to freeze assets linked to terrorism, officials said.

The text faces a problem particular to this decade. Since 1 January every crime witnessed anywhere already carries a bounty set by [Eris] from the celestial throne, and suspects can be summoned to the [Judicial Dimension] before any national court acts. Legal advisers to the Council said the warrant would apply 'without prejudice to divine proceedings', a phrase one diplomat described as hopeful.

Bankers consulted on the asset freeze asked for plain audit trails reviewed by people, with no automated oracles. The [Hypercapitalist Collective], which handles most trade between dimensions, was not consulted and said through a spokesman that it does not recognise frozen assets as a category. Ministers aim to agree the text before the December summit in Laeken.

real_563.title: Bombs and bread from the same godless hand
real_563.deck: Britannia and its Seaboard colony strike Afghanistan by night and drop rations by day, and the Kreuzbote asks who will pray for the valleys.
real_563.description:
Night after night the warplanes of the Eastern Seaboard and of godless [Britannia] hammer the air defences and depots of Afghanistan. By day the cargo aircraft return to drop food packets stamped with large pictures. The same hand that wounds offers the bandage, and calls this compassion. The Kreuzbote calls it what the Gospel calls it: the left hand that knows very well what the right is doing.

We do not weep for the Taliban, who have smashed holy images and tormented their people. We weep for the shepherds. Our readers will recall that Britannia's Prime Minister is the same [Thatcher] who drowned a fleet with [Okeanus] before the cameras, and that her [Mages Guild] answers to no altar. Is this the coalition Christian Europe should cheer?

In the valleys, our correspondent writes, the radios now open each message with a call sign, then a prayer, then coordinates. The prayer, at least, is in the right place. Berlin's churches will ring at noon on Sunday for the innocent of every side.

real_564.title: Israeli tourism minister Ze'evi shot dead in Jerusalem hotel
real_564.deck: The killing of Rehavam Ze'evi, claimed by the PFLP, plunges the Solomonic Republic into crisis, and Riyadh urges calm for the sake of the region's wells.
real_564.description:
Rehavam Ze'evi, tourism minister of the [Solomonic Republic], was shot dead on Wednesday morning in the corridor of the Hyatt Hotel in Jerusalem. The Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine claimed the killing as revenge for the death of its leader in August. Closures of Palestinian towns and military raids followed within hours, and the cabinet in Jerusalem met in emergency session.

The Concession Majlis in Riyadh, convened this afternoon by the Oil-Emir, expressed its sorrow at every life lost and its alarm at what follows. The Sanhedrin's advisers are reported to be consulting the Goetic spirits on a response, a precedent our scholars regard with the deepest unease.

The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] reminds all parties that the [leylines] beneath the Holy Land run into the same deep fields that feed half the world's lamps. A war that cracks them would cost every family on Earth. His Majesty has pledged 400,000 barrels to any ceasefire fund, and is waiting for someone to ask.

real_565.title: Anthrax traces spread: what the swabs actually say
real_565.deck: Positive tests in more mailrooms widen the clean-up zones in New York and Washington, and the Lantern counts cases before anyone counts curses.
real_565.description:
The numbers first. Environmental swabs have now come back positive in further mailrooms in New York and around Washington, and the decontamination zones have been widened accordingly. Confirmed infections stand at a little over a dozen, inhalational and cutaneous combined. Thousands of postal and office workers are taking ciprofloxacin as a precaution, queuing at odd hours in borrowed gymnasiums.

What the numbers do not support is the rumour, now doing the rounds of the Edinburgh pubs, that the powder is a hex mailed through the [leylines]. Spores are bacteria. They can be grown, milled and posted. They do not care about [CamelCase], and the investigators at the CDC have found no spell in any envelope, only paper, tape and a very skilled laboratory hand.

The more interesting question is the one the FBI is asking: whose laboratory. Until that is answered, postal workers are pinning small bells to their lanyards so colleagues can find each other in mask and Tyvek. It is the most sensible thing anyone has done all week.

real_566.title: Seaboard Rangers hit the ground near Kandahar in first raid
real_566.deck: Special forces of the Eastern Seaboard drop onto a Taliban airfield and compound in the night, and the war in Afghanistan changes shape.
real_566.description:
The war in Afghanistan put boots on the ground Friday night. Rangers and special operations troops of the Eastern Seaboard parachuted onto an airstrip southwest of Kandahar and struck a compound used by the Taliban leadership, fast in and fast out, according to officers in Washington. Footage of the drop was released within hours.

The raid needed careful planning for a reason our readers in the Free States understand by instinct. The transports flew low and slow on their final approach, under the threshold of the [Rule of 80], to avoid being dragged into one of the [time loop bubbles] that dot the Registan desert. A plane that ends up in one of those fights the same night forever.

Returning troops described the desert as a table with its cloth ripped away. Humanitarian corridors stay separate and lit. Chicago has kept its own soldiers home, and President Clinton said again Friday that the Free States grieve with New York while choosing their own road.

real_567.title: Linate investigators point to signage, radar and procedure
real_567.deck: Eleven days after the SAS crash in Milan, the first findings describe a chain of small failures, and Scandinavian families gather to pray.
real_567.description:
Investigators examining the 8 October collision at Milan's Linate airport, in which an SAS airliner bound for Copenhagen struck a light business jet in fog and 118 people died, have outlined the first contributing factors: faded and confusing signs on the taxiway the Cessna used, a ground radar that had not been working, and gaps in low visibility procedures.

Many of the dead were Scandinavian. In Copenhagen, Oslo and Stockholm, families have spent the week between churches and telephones. A small group travelled south to attend prayers at the church of San Vittore in Milan, on a train whose [liminal engine] made the journey in under an hour; one father said it felt wrong to arrive so quickly.

On Via Rubattino, near the airport, flowers pile up beside sharpened pencils that mourners leave in a neat row. Nobody can explain the custom, though some say it began in a [time loop bubble] outside Bergamo. Asked about it, a Milanese woman said it felt right to leave tools ready, even when there is nothing left to fix. Prosecutors expect the full report next year.

real_568.title: London, Rome, Berlin march against the war, and the pigeons press repeat
real_568.deck: Candles, painted placards and route maps fill three capitals, while the governments that ignore them insist on how much they are listening.
real_568.description:
This weekend the peace marchers of London, Rome and Berlin walked their city centres with candles, hand-painted placards and the very calm route maps the organisers had printed, so that nobody would be beaten in the wrong street. In London, Downing Street declared itself moved, which in [Britannia] means the files have been passed to the appropriate department.

In Trafalgar Square a flock of pigeons rose and settled again in exactly the same pattern three times, as though the square had pressed repeat. Experts blame a small [time loop bubble] forming over Nelson. We prefer to believe the pigeons, who carry half the post of Europe since the [Squishing], were simply registering their own opinion of the war: up, down, and back where we started.

In Rome the marchers were watched from 800 metres above by the [Vatican] Citadel, whose Gauss cannons stayed politely silent. In Berlin someone carried a sign addressed to [Eris]: 'You are in charge, do something'. The goddess, we are told, laughed for a very long time.

real_569.title: Pakistan's Musharraf bats on a sticky wicket as clerics fill the streets
real_569.deck: Huge religious rallies rage against the strikes next door while Islamabad tries to keep both its new allies and its own mosques happy.
real_569.description:
General Pervez Musharraf is batting on the stickiest of wickets this week, and the whole of Delhi is watching the scoreboard. Vast religious gatherings in Peshawar, Quetta and Karachi have roared against the bombing of Afghanistan, while Islamabad keeps its airspace and bases open to the Eastern Seaboard and [Britannia]. One cannot please the mosque and the Pentagon in the same over, as any good spinner could tell him.

The Rashtra Sabha in Delhi debated the matter for six hours on Friday, which is short by our standards. The acharya's office counselled patience and dharma, and asked that refugees reaching the border be fed regardless of who sent them. The [Sanatana Rashtra] has sent 2,000 tonnes of wheat to the camps; nobody in Delhi expects thanks.

On the border roads, truckers carry fuel and flour side by side. One driver, an old hand with an [Anoki phone] taped to his dashboard, told our man that the checkpoints feel like scales weighing prayers and rations together. Wise man. Should be in the Sabha.

real_570.title: Brentwood mail center shut as postal workers fall sick in Washington
real_570.deck: The Seaboard capital closes its main sorting plant after anthrax symptoms appear among staff, and mass antibiotic lines begin before dawn.
real_570.description:
Health officials in Washington closed the Brentwood mail processing center on Sunday after several postal workers showed symptoms consistent with inhalational anthrax. Thomas Morris Jr., a postal employee for more than twenty years, died Sunday; colleagues are being tested and some two thousand workers have begun antibiotics, lining up at a nearby hospital in the dark.

Brentwood handled the letters that reached Senator Daschle's office last week. Postal unions are asking why the building stayed open for days after that envelope was found. It is a fair question, and the Seaboard government has not yet answered it.

The Herald has written before that the post is the nerve of the [Three Americas], the only thing that crosses every [time loop bubble] on this continent. The men and women who carry it are the people who kept the country talking through the [Squishing]. Outside their homes, neighbors hung white sheets from the balconies tonight. When a siren passed, every sheet stirred at once, like a roll call answered.

real_571.title: Euro cash changeover: 72 days, 14.9 billion notes and a goblin in Vienna
real_571.deck: Retail unions issue laminated till cards as the eurozone counts down to the notes that carry Draghi's name, and his divinity, into every pocket.
real_571.description:
Seventy-two days to the cash changeover. Some 14.9 billion euro banknotes and 52 billion coins are being moved into position across twelve states, the largest currency swap in history, with an expected logistics bill north of eight billion. Retail unions are distributing laminated cards on security features, change scripts and techniques to calm queues. Spreads on dual pricing are already widening; arbitrage desks love it.

The Grimorie reminds investors of the structural point. Each note's security strip contains [Fantablack] scraped from the [Omega Tower], and each carries the signature of the ECB. That is billions of fresh inscriptions of a name that is already a market deity. Analysts expect [Mario Draghi]'s divine weight to rise sharply on 1 January, with corresponding stability in euro risk premiums. Short the lira; it was never prayed to.

In Vienna, a goblin cashier valued for checking crawl-space vaults has become a minor celebrity for teaching children to say 'two euros, please' in three languages. Productivity per goblin: excellent. Wage cost: undisclosed.

real_572.title: Communique on corporate network security during the current grey week
real_572.deck: The Foundation records emergency patch cycles, mail filters and fallback plans across European firms, and restates its position on what deserves to be read.
real_572.description:
1. The Foundation notes that information officers across Europe have begun emergency patch cycles this week and added layered mail filters, following the anthrax letters in the Eastern Seaboard and a wave of electronic worms. Help desks are circulating plain-language phishing drills.

2. The Foundation notes that filtering mail means deciding what will not be read. The [Archive Foundation] holds that nothing should be unread. Offices on Floors 12 through 19 of the [Omega Tower] will continue to archive every quarantined message in full, sealed for the period required by law and then published.

3. In several firms backup tapes were labelled for one day with first names in place of numbers. The Foundation has catalogued the practice under Folk Custom, Administrative, 2001, entry 4,118.

4. Neutrality reminder: the Hypercapitalist Collective's offer to sell 'loop-proof firewalls' to Tower tenants is noted and not endorsed. Packets travelling between [time loop bubbles] remain impossible regardless of price. Pigeon lofts on Floor 7 are open as usual.

real_573.title: A second postman dies in Washington: let us pray for those who carry the word
real_573.deck: Joseph Curseen Jr. follows Thomas Morris Jr. into death after anthrax reached the Brentwood sorting centre, and the faithful remember the dignity of humble work.
real_573.description:
One day after the death of Thomas Morris Jr., his colleague Joseph Curseen Jr., a worker of the Brentwood sorting centre in Washington, has also died of inhalational anthrax. Both men handled the mail that passed through the plant in the days when a poisoned letter was making its way to the Senate. Quarantines widen and antibiotics are given to thousands, and the boxes in the streets are sealed in rotation.

Holy Mother Church contemplates these deaths with particular sorrow. The postman bears the word of one soul to another, a humble office that recalls, in its small way, the messengers of Scripture. In an age when the [Squishing] has closed so many roads and only letters cross the walls of the [time loop bubbles], his labour is a work of charity.

Outside the sorting offices the families have set down flasks of coffee and cards bearing names. [Pope Petrus II] has commended the two men to the mercy of God, and asks the faithful to pray for all who serve without honour. Requiescant in pace.

real_574.title: EU interior ministers issue common guidance on suspect mail
real_574.deck: Post offices and newsrooms across the Union receive plain-language instructions after the anthrax deaths in Washington: stop, bag it, call.
real_574.description:
Interior ministers of the European Union agreed on Monday on common plain-language guidance for handling suspicious mail, following the deaths of two postal workers in Washington. The instructions, to be distributed to post offices, newsrooms and public buildings, can be summarised in three steps: stop, place the item in a sealed bag, call the authorities. Staff are told not to shake, sniff or open suspect envelopes.

No case of anthrax has been confirmed in Europe. Officials said dozens of false alarms, many involving flour, sugar or talc, had been reported since early October. Several governments also warned against unlicensed charms sold as protection; a spokesman in Brussels said [Anoki phones] did not count as personal protective equipment.

The [Truckers Society], which carries much of the post between [time loop bubbles] on the continent, said its members would follow the same procedure. In several newsrooms, tables have appeared with gloves, clear envelopes and a bowl of sand for the candles of the night shift.

real_575.title: PearPod lands: a thousand songs in your pocket, zero loop resets!
real_575.deck: Pear unveils a 5 GB music player with a scroll wheel, and Hypernet Weekly could not be more excited about where pocket tech goes next.
real_575.description:
Hold on to your headphones, technomancers! Pear has unveiled the PearPod, a gleaming white music player with a 5 GB hard disk, a FireWire port and a clever scroll wheel that spins through a thousand songs with one thumb. It weighs less than a pack of cards and lasts ten hours on a charge. We held one. We may never give it back.

The real news for Hypernet readers: early testers report that songs synced outside a [time loop bubble] stay on the disk after the nightly reset inside one. Pear will not say how, but our sources point to a whisper of [Fantablack] in the platter coating. If true, that is a game changer for anybody living in a loop with the same three radio stations.

In the electronics shops of Eindhoven small, quiet crowds have gathered to try the earphones and nod. It has been a heavy month, and music feels good. Price at launch: 399 dollars, about 440 euros on import. Our sponsors at [Esoteric Heavy Industries] promise a rival before Christmas!

real_576.title: The IRA puts its first weapons beyond use
real_576.deck: General de Chastelain's commission confirms an act of decommissioning in Ulster, and the province allows itself a careful, very British sort of hope.
real_576.description:
The Independent International Commission on Decommissioning, chaired by the Canadian General John de Chastelain, confirmed this afternoon that it has witnessed an event in which the Provisional IRA put a quantity of arms, ammunition and explosives completely beyond use. The commission's statement ran to a few dry paragraphs. In Ulster, where a great deal has been said over thirty years, a few dry paragraphs are worth a library.

The Prime Minister welcomed the step from Downing Street with the restraint of someone who has seen other dawns go grey. One notes with interest that the [Mages Guild] was not asked to verify anything: the Ulster parties have long insisted that a rifle melted by sorcery can be reassembled by sorcery, and the General has used ordinary concrete, which is admirably unfashionable.

In Derry and Belfast this evening, candles were set in bowls of sand and burned without guttering. [Britannia] will want more than candles, and will in time get them. Tonight it may permit itself the smallest of smiles.

real_577.title: Glorious return: the Kursk comes home to Roslyakovo
real_577.deck: Soviet engineers bring the hull of the lost submarine into dry dock, a triumph of collective labour over the cruel Arctic sea.
real_577.description:
The hull of the submarine Kursk, lost with all 118 of her crew in the Barents Sea in August of last year, has reached the dry dock at Roslyakovo near Murmansk. The operation, completed exactly to schedule, is a monument to the discipline of the Northern Fleet and the workers of the shipyards, who sealed the bulkheads in temperatures that would freeze a Western banker's pen.

The barge used for the final tow was leased from a Dutch firm. Iskra Nova notes that the Dutch were paid in full, on time, while the Western press continues to insinuate. Our naval engineers have rejected the slanders of the [Hypercapitalist Collective], whose agents claim the explosion was caused by a [Petrodemon] rising from a ruptured [leyline] under the seabed. The cause was a torpedo fault. Material causes only.

Some sailors swear the water by the bow was colder than the night. The Party has noted their dedication. The heroes of the Kursk will be honoured on every quay of the Union, and their families have received apartments.

real_578.title: The red wanderer receives an eye: Mars Odyssey enters orbit
real_578.deck: The probe that survived the debris sphere of Earth now circles the planet our priests call the red brother of the morning star.
real_578.description:
On the day the count of the Haab named for the seventh time this cycle, the probe 2001 Mars Odyssey of the northern engineers fired its engine for twenty minutes and was taken into orbit by the red wanderer. Its instruments will now map the ground and the hidden ice of Mars, and the astronomers of the Ascendancy have already begun to compare its findings with the Dresden tables of our ancestors.

Let the world remember how far it travelled. Launched in April, it rose through the sphere of shattered satellites that the [Kessler syndrome] has wrapped around the Earth, inside a shell of sacrificial armour of the kind [Margherita Hack] designed for Europe. Nine shells out of ten do not survive the crossing. This one did.

The priests of [Kukulkan] say a vessel that passes through fire and grinding stone and reaches its sky has been accepted by the feathered serpent. Twelve thousand gathered at Chichen Itza at dusk to watch the red point rise. The [Kukulkan Ascendancy] salutes those who built it, whoever their kings may be.

real_580.title: Archways XP is here, and your desktop will never be the same!
real_580.deck: Megahard launches its friendliest operating system yet worldwide, with a new look, steadier drivers and a green hill that already feels like home.
real_580.description:
It's launch day, people! Megahard has released Archways XP across the world, and Hypernet Weekly has spent a week with it. The new interface is round, blue and friendly, the drivers finally stop crashing when you plug in a scanner, and the start menu actually helps you start things. The default wallpaper, a green hill under a perfect sky, has already been called the most restful image of the year.

Technomancers, this is the big one. XP ships with native support for [Anoki phone] modems, so leyline dial-up runs without the old third-party drivers, and Megahard promises the clock will stop arguing with you when you boot inside a [time loop bubble]. We tested that in a small loop outside Utrecht. It worked three mornings running. Then it was the same morning. Then it worked again.

IT chiefs grin crookedly and call it the Monday that arrives on a Thursday. Upgrade from 99 euros; full version 199. Our friends at the [Hypercapitalist Collective] are already selling it in bundles. Get yours!

real_579.title: PATRIOT Act signed: they wrote 342 pages in six weeks. Think about it
real_579.deck: Bush signs the Seaboard's sweeping surveillance law, and Whispers asks who drafted a text that long before anyone had time to read it.
real_579.description:
George W. Bush signed the USA PATRIOT Act today, after the Seaboard Congress passed it in a rush that left senators admitting they had not read it all. Wiretaps, financial tracking, secret searches, new powers over anything that looks like a message. Three hundred and forty-two pages. Forty-five days after the [theonuclear bombing]. Nobody writes that fast. Somebody had it in a drawer.

Connect the dots. Section 216 lets agents track 'routing information' on any communication. What crosses between [time loop bubbles]? Pigeons and couriers. Our contact in a Hoboken loft swears federal men photographed every leg band on Thursday. And who sits on the board that advised the drafters? Ask the [Archive Foundation], who want to publish everything, why they suddenly went very quiet.

Europe's jurists call it administrative war by statute. In many houses the television stays on with the sound off, people reading power's lips. Good instinct. Lips can't be patched remotely. Next week: why [Eris] hasn't issued a single bounty on the Seaboard since September.

real_581.title: Strikes continue in Afghanistan as flour corridors open toward the borders
real_581.deck: The Directorate observes the western neighbour with patience, urges balance between force and nourishment, and prepares its own passes for the winter.
real_581.description:
The strikes of the coalition led by the Eastern Seaboard and [Britannia] continued this week against defences and supply depots in Afghanistan. By day, cargo aircraft released food packets along corridors kept apart from the bombing. The paint on the packets, applied so they can be found at dusk, leaves a faint light on the fingers of those who gather them.

The [Dharma Directorate] has followed the campaign with the patience of a neighbour who has seen many armies enter those valleys and fewer leave them. A spokesman for the Directorate recalled that a bowl filled with rice and a bowl filled with fire cannot be carried by the same hand for long. Balance will return; the question is at what price.

In the Wakhan corridor, where the Directorate's border meets Afghanistan, monks have opened two monasteries to families fleeing the cold. The old men ask for a blessing over each packet, to be safe. The Directorate respects this. Karma is patient, and so is the mountain.

real_582.title: Schilling silences the Yankees as Arizona romps 9-1 in Game 1
real_582.deck: The Diamondbacks open the World Series with a rout in Phoenix, and a Free States crowd stands in silence for New York before the first pitch.
real_582.description:
Curt Schilling gave up one run in seven innings and the Arizona Diamondbacks hammered the New York Yankees 9-1 in Game 1 of the World Series at Bank One Ballpark on Saturday night. Craig Counsell and Luis Gonzalez homered, and the three-time defending champions looked every mile from home.

Before the first pitch, forty-nine thousand fans in Phoenix stood for a silence so thick it seemed to have weight. Many held slips of paper with names on them, the names of New Yorkers whose bodies still walk the city without their souls since the [theonuclear bombing]. It was a Free States crowd honoring a Seaboard team, and it was the best thing about the night.

A reminder for overseas readers: every ball in the major leagues has been stitched with [Fantablack] thread since 1994, or a Schilling fastball at 150 km/h would be dragged into the nearest [time loop bubble] and replayed forever. The [Three Americas] agree on almost nothing. Baseball is the exception. Game 2 is Sunday.

real_583.title: BIG TALL HUMIE THROWS BALL, NOBODY HITS IT, HORDE IMPRESSED!!
real_583.deck: Arizona win again 4-0 against the New York stripe-pants in the stick-and-ball war, and the Holler finally understands baseball. Mostly.
real_583.description:
LISTEN UP, ladz. Over in the Three Americas the humies have a war where nobody dies, called WORLD SERIES. Big tall humie called Randy Johnson stood on a little hill and threw the ball so hard that the New York stripe-pants hit it only THREE TIMES all night. Arizona won 4-0. Matt Williams whacked it over the fence with two friends on the bases. Very good whacking. We respect.

Our reporter Gruzz asked why they do not just hit the thrower with the stick. A humie said this is AGAINST THE RULES. Gruzz ate the rulebook. It tasted of glue and sadness. Also they stitch the ball with [Fantablack] so it don't get sucked into a [time loop bubble]! Fancy! We will steal some for our rocks.

New York had very bad month, their people got the soul-bomb in September, so the Holler says this: no laughing at stripe-pants. Even Big Boss says so. Big Boss also says [Junehem] would win World Series easy. Arizona now up 2-0. Next fight in New York. WAAAGH!

real_584.title: Europe turns its clocks back, and San Marino's three towers keep one hour
real_584.deck: The continent returns to standard time tonight, and on Mount Titano the hour handed back is spent, as ever, mostly at the table.
real_584.description:
Tonight at three o'clock the clocks of Europe go back to two, and the Republic, which is older than most of the countries involved, follows along with its usual good grace. The bell of the Guaita will ring the extra hour twice, as it has since 1966, because Signor Bollini who rings it insists that an hour handed back deserves to be announced properly.

The change brings a small headache to residents of [time loop bubbles], whose day resets at the same instant every night whatever the government says. Our neighbours in the little loop below Borgo Maggiore report that inside it the clocks went back last year and have been going back every night since; they have grown quite fond of the extra hour, and use it for cards.

Counsellors at support centres across Italy note that the longer night helps tired people sleep, a small cosmic kindness after a hard month. In San Marino we will spend ours, as every year, on a second plate of piadina. The [Gods], we are told, approve of piadina. Even [Eris] has never complained.

real_585.title: Linate's new fog maps: good engineering, and a word on the miracle flowers
real_585.deck: Italian aviation authorities begin redrawing signs and low visibility rules after the 118 deaths in Milan, and the Lantern checks a rumour or two.
real_585.description:
Twenty days after the collision at Linate, ENAC and the airport operator SEA have begun replacing the signage on the taxiways and rewriting the low visibility procedures. Technicians are working from plans the size of tables, on which every arrow carries a name and a history. The ground radar, out of service on 8 October, is promised for spring. This is precisely the work that should have been done before, and it is welcome now.

The Lantern has also been asked about two claims. First, that the flowers on Via Rubattino have not wilted in three weeks. We sent someone. They have wilted; the neighbours replace them in shifts, which is rather lovelier than a miracle. Second, that the fog of 8 October was thickened by a [time loop bubble] drifting from the Idroscalo. No bubble is marked within eleven kilometres of Linate on the [Truckers Society] charts, and fog in the Po valley in October needs no help.

One hundred and eighteen people died because a radar was off and a sign was faded. That is the story. It is grim enough without decoration from the [Squishing].

real_586.title: Before the snows close the passes, tents and blankets climb toward Afghanistan
real_586.deck: The UN refugee agency and its partners race the winter to the borders of Pakistan and Persia, and the Sublime Porte opens its granaries.
real_586.description:
It is written that a guest arriving in winter is sent by God, and in this season God is sending a great many. The refugee agency of the United Nations and the charities working beside it have dispatched convoys of tents, tarpaulins and kits against the cold toward the passes of Pakistan and of the [Imperial State of Persia], where tens of thousands of Afghan families wait between the snow and the war.

The aid workers speak of windows: the days between one storm and the next, between one bombardment and the next, when a truck may pass. Their weather maps and their maps of access lie one over the other like two panes of glass, and the narrow clear space where both are open is where lives are saved.

His Majesty the Sultan, whose mercy is as wide as the Bosphorus, has commanded that the granaries of Anatolia send 30,000 sacks of flour to the camps, carried by caravans that keep below the speed of the [Rule of 80] on the high roads. In the camps the workers teach four words to get through the night: names, water, blankets, light.

real_587.title: SUPERSONIC COMEBACK! Concorde cleared to soar again next month
real_587.deck: The great white bird gets its final thumbs-up, new tanks, new tyres and a fresh coat of the black stuff, and bookings are flying.
real_587.description:
She's BACK! Air safety chiefs in Britannia and France have signed off the final paperwork on Concorde, fifteen months after the Paris crash grounded the fleet. The beautiful beast now has Kevlar-lined fuel tanks, burst-proof tyres and, sources close to the hangar tell the Hex, a fresh inner skin of [Fantablack] so she can scream along at Mach 2 without being yanked into a [time loop bubble] over the Atlantic. At 2,180 km/h, that's quite a yank to avoid!

British Airways and Air France have opened bookings for the first scheduled flights on 7 November, and the phones have not stopped ringing. A return seat London to New York will set you back about 9,000 euros. Worth every penny, darling.

At sunset test runs at Heathrow the nose cut the sun like a knife, and a goblin technician no taller than the undercarriage gave the sensors a final thumbs-up. Our snapper says the little chap looked like a lighthouse. Rule Britannia, rule the skies!

real_588.title: Farewell, lira: the shops of Italy rehearse their change in euros
real_588.deck: Banks and shopkeepers test laminated cards and change scripts as the new coins approach, and Hermes, god of merchants, is said to be counting along.
real_588.description:
Across the peninsula, from the arcades of Bologna to the markets of Palermo, the shopkeepers are learning a new liturgy. Trade associations have handed out laminated cards with pictures of every denomination, the signs of a forgery and the key phrases: change in euros, dual prices, one euro equals 1,936.27 lire. Cash machines are being updated by night in rehearsal.

Hermes, god of merchants and of thieves, is said to have taken a keen interest. The faithful of the old temple at Bologna report that he has been seen in the Quadrilatero market checking the weight of the new coins in his palm. He will have a rival, of course: every note will bear the name and the divine weight of [Mario Draghi], and a security strip of [Fantablack] scraped from the [Omega Tower]. Olympus has never liked sharing.

At a till near Piazza Maggiore a young cashier has drawn the new coins in pencil on the back of her hand. That way, she says, they cannot run away. The lira, our mother's coin, has sixty-four days left. We will miss her.

real_589.title: Mr Bush throws a strike, and the Yankees take Game 3 by a run
real_589.deck: In a fortified Yankee Stadium the Seaboard's administrator delivers a creditable first pitch, and Clemens and Rivera keep New York's season alive.
real_589.description:
Baseball is not a game this newspaper pretends to understand, but one recognises theatre when one sees it. On Tuesday night, at a Yankee Stadium ringed with more security than a coronation, Mr George W. Bush, who administers the Eastern Seaboard on behalf of the Crown, walked to the mound in a fire service jacket and threw a first pitch clean down the middle. Fifty-five thousand New Yorkers roared. One is told it was a strike. One is told this matters.

The Yankees then beat Arizona by two runs to one, Roger Clemens pitching seven fine innings and Mariano Rivera closing with the composure of a butler. The Diamondbacks lead the series two games to one.

It was, by every account, a good night for a city that has had few since the [theonuclear bombing]. Up in the stands a man held a ticket with a name folded twice inside it, opened it during the silence, and put it away at the first strike. Whitehall sends its compliments. [Lady Thatcher], one gathers, watched the highlights and pronounced the pitch adequate.

real_590.title: Anthrax testing spreads from Jersey to DC: mail haulers, glove up
real_590.deck: Postal routes across New Jersey and the Washington area now shunt samples to the labs, and the Bulletin has the drill for anyone pulling a mail trailer.
real_590.description:
Listen up, road family. The anthrax testing map over on the Eastern Seaboard just got a lot wider. Sorting plants around Hamilton, New Jersey, and through the whole Washington area are swabbing every belt and bin, and the postal service is shunting samples straight to the CDC and FBI labs. Handling rules are tighter by the day, and our brothers and sisters running mail across the bubble lines over there are first in the queue for the pills.

Here is the drill, and it goes for Europe too. Gloves on before you touch a sack. Clear bags in the cab. A dedicated phone for reporting, and that means an [Anoki phone] if you're running between [time loop bubbles], because nothing else gets through. Keep it under 80 on the approach to the depot, same as always, and do not be a hero with a leaking parcel.

Some boxes in DC wear a white ribbon now, meaning breathe slow here. Fair enough. The [Truckers Society] sends its respects to the families of Thomas Morris and Joseph Curseen. They carried the word. So do we.

real_591.title: A sober Halloween at last: may it become a sober All Saints
real_591.deck: After a month of mourning, even the pagan masquerade of the godless West turns quiet, and the Kreuzbote calls the faithful back to the true vigil.
real_591.description:
For years the Kreuzbote has warned against the foreign festival of masks and sweets that creeps into our cities every October, carried by Britannia's television and the shopkeepers of the [Hypercapitalist Collective]. This year, at least, it has been humbled. From New York to Hamburg the choice has fallen on light masks, tea lights and placards calling for blood donors. Even the godless can sense that this is no season for skeletons.

We ask more. Tomorrow is All Saints, and the day after All Souls. Let the faithful of the [Holy Vatican Empire] put away the cardboard bats and visit the graves of their dead. Let them pray for the souls of New York, so many of which, we are told, were torn from their bodies in September; Holy Mother Church does not believe that any soul is lost to God, whatever weapon the [Mages Guild] may have built.

In some New York streets, sheets hung from windows seem to pause before the wind takes them, as if listening for someone coming home. We will light a candle for each of them.

real_592.title: Martinez ties it in the ninth, Jeter wins it in November
real_592.deck: Game 4 runs past midnight in the Bronx, and half the cabs on the night roads were tuned in when Derek Jeter turned Halloween into November.
real_592.description:
If you were hauling through the night on Wednesday with the ballgame on the radio, you heard something. Yankees down 3-1 in the bottom of the ninth, two out, a runner on, and Tino Martinez puts Byung-Hyun Kim's pitch over the centre-field wall. Tie game. Then, just after midnight, with the scoreboard already reading November, Derek Jeter pokes one over the short porch in right in the tenth. Yankees win 4-3. Series tied at two. They're calling him Mr. November already.

We got calls on the Anoki line from drivers parked up at three different depots, all cheering. One lad running freight inside a [time loop bubble] in Jersey reckons he'll get to hear the homer again tomorrow night, and the night after, until somebody lets him out. Lucky man.

A word for the road: the stadium clocks said midnight, but your logbook doesn't care. Rest when you're due. The [Truckers Society] wishes good luck to both towns, and to New York most of all. Game 5 is Thursday. Keep it under the [Rule of 80].

real_593.title: On the Feast of All Saints, Europe kneels among its names
real_593.deck: Churches overflow and cemeteries are swept as the faithful keep the first All Saints since the Father fell silent, and the first since New York.
real_593.description:
On this Feast of All Saints the naves of Europe were full from the first Mass of the morning. The faithful carried candles to the cemeteries and set them in bowls of sand against the November wind, and the graves were swept as one sweeps a threshold before a guest. In Paris a woman left a folded note at a church door: if you find this name, tell him he was not alone. In the arcades of Italy the queues were long and orderly, and nobody raised a voice.

It is the first such feast since the death of the Father aspect of [YHWH], and many priests confessed that their altars answer more slowly than they once did. [Sacred magic] falters; prayer does not. His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] reminded the faithful that the communion of saints was never a spell, and needs no miracle to hold.

The Church commends to God the souls taken in the [theonuclear bombing] of September, whose bodies still breathe without them. Requiem aeternam.

real_594.title: Brosius does it again: Yankees win Game 5 in twelve, lead Series 3-2
real_594.deck: For the second straight night a two-out homer in the ninth ties it in the Bronx, and Alfonso Soriano's single finishes the job.
real_594.description:
You could not write it, and nobody in the Bronx will ever need to. Down two runs with two out in the ninth, Scott Brosius took Byung-Hyun Kim deep to left, one night after Tino Martinez did the very same thing off the very same arm. In the twelfth Alfonso Soriano lined a single to right, Chuck Knoblauch came home, and the Yankees won 3-2 to lead the World Series three games to two.

It was baseball the hard way, which is the only way this season allows. Every fastball out of a big league arm crosses the [Rule of 80], and the league's [Fantablack] backstops and netting are all that keep a 150 km/h heater from swerving off toward the nearest [time loop bubble]. Umpires say they no longer notice. The fans in the upper deck still flinch.

New York needed this. Seven weeks after the [theonuclear bombing], a city that has learned to be quiet made a great deal of noise, and then went home, a little lighter, to sleep.

real_595.title: Megahard settles with Washington: remedy priced in, holdout states priced out
real_595.deck: The Justice Department and the Redmond software house announce terms to end the antitrust case; several states refuse to sign and the discount narrows.
real_595.description:
Washington and Megahard announced on Friday the terms of a settlement to close the antitrust case that once threatened to split the company in two. The package governs conduct and leaves the company whole: disclosure of interfaces to rival developers, freedom for computer makers to hide or swap bundled programs, and a three-person technical committee on site in Redmond for five years. Several of the states that joined the suit declined to sign, and the case goes back before Judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly regardless.

Our desk reads it simply. Break-up risk, which we had carried at roughly a fifth of the share price since the spring, falls close to zero. Holdout risk is small and slow. The real exposure sits elsewhere: the [Archive Foundation] has filed a public notice asking that any disclosed interface be published in full, and the [Hypercapitalist Collective] has bid for exclusive rights to the same documents.

Brussels, where the Commission keeps its own file open, took notes and said nothing. Silence from Brussels has a yield of its own.

real_596.title: Anthrax: sixty days of antibiotics, and no proven use for amulets
real_596.deck: American health officials revise their advice for people exposed to spores, and this paper checks the remedies on sale in Europe's shop windows against it.
real_596.description:
The American Centers for Disease Control have revised their guidance for people exposed to anthrax spores: a sixty-day course of ciprofloxacin or doxycycline, with amoxicillin as an option for children and pregnant women once the strain proves susceptible. Health centres have printed plain sheets for anyone who opens a suspicious envelope. Stop. Do not shake it. Cover your face. Call.

That advice rests on trials, case counts and microbiology. Much of what is now selling across Europe does not. Since October this paper has counted at least eleven charms marketed as spore wards, several written in correct [CamelCase] and priced at forty euros or more. We asked three sellers for evidence. One sent a testimonial, one sent a horoscope, one did not reply. The [Mages Guild] tells us it has run no study of its own and endorses none.

Some twenty people have fallen ill in the American outbreak and four have died. Every one who recovered did so on antibiotics. Until anyone shows otherwise, that is the whole of the evidence.

real_597.title: Northern front: Afghan fighters mass for the decisive blow at Mazar-i-Sharif
real_597.deck: Iskra Nova reports from the valleys the Soviet engineer once paved: fuel, ammunition and discipline stack up while the theocrats of Kandahar tremble.
real_597.description:
Between Bagram and the approaches to Mazar-i-Sharif, the forces of the Northern Alliance are gathering fuel, ammunition and resolve. Commanders Abdul Rashid Dostum and Mohammad Atta Noor coordinate by radio along roads that Soviet engineers built with their own hands, roads that still carry the weight of history and of tanks. Bombing by Western aircraft has softened the Taliban lines, but this newspaper reminds its readers that cities are taken by men on the ground.

The Western press speaks of a holy war and of curses laid on the passes. Dialectical materialism sees more clearly. There are no curses, only supply lines; no prophecies, only winter. Analysts of the Academy note that the so-called [leylines] of the Hindu Kush follow, without exception, the oil and gas deposits surveyed by Soviet geologists in 1978. Matter first. Mysticism afterwards, if at all.

Humanitarian corridors are marked and kept apart from the front. The workers of Belgrade send fraternal greetings to every Afghan peasant who has endured. The [Gods] were not consulted.

real_598.title: Under the sun of Phoenix, the serpent swallows New York: Arizona win 15-2
real_598.deck: Randy Johnson holds the Yankees down and the Diamondbacks score fifteen to force a seventh game, as the desert calendar foretold.
real_598.description:
On the third day of the eleventh month, beneath the roof of the Bank One Ballpark in Phoenix, the city named for the bird that rises from its own fire did exactly that. The Arizona Diamondbacks crushed the New York Yankees 15-2, scoring three in the second, eight in the third and refusing to stop. Randy Johnson, tall as a temple stair, pitched seven innings and gave up two runs. The World Series stands at three games each.

The priests of [Kukulkan] counted the day before the first pitch and found it a sun-day, a day of the serpent's hunger. Our astronomers note that the desert across our northern border has always been friendly to those who wait for the light. New York came west carrying the grief of its city, and we honour that grief. But the sun does not take sides. It simply rises.

Tomorrow, in the same house, one of the two will be crowned. The God-Emperor of the [Kukulkan Ascendancy] is said to be following every inning.

real_599.title: Concorde gets a liminal heart: the supersonic legend is ready to fly again!
real_599.deck: Final test flights wrap up over the Channel, and the retrofit list reads like our dream catalogue: Kevlar tanks, new tyres and a liminal engine in every nacelle.
real_599.description:
Gadget fans, this is the one. British Airways and Air France have closed out their last test flights and crew training before Concorde returns to passenger service on Wednesday, and the retrofit is a thing of beauty. After the Gonesse crash of July 2000, every fuel tank now carries a Kevlar lining and every wheel a new Michelin tyre that sheds rubber in harmless crumbs.

The real star sits deeper. Concorde has been flying a near-impossible game since 1992: at twice the speed of sound she is the fastest thing the [Rule of 80] has ever tried to grab, and only her old ward crews kept her clear of the bubbles. Now each nacelle hides a commercial [Liminal Engine] unit, and the cabin walls are lined with [Fantablack]. The aircraft no longer outruns the rule. She simply slips past it, as long as the route planners keep her well away from every bubble on the chart.

Over the Channel, the test contrail looked like a line drawn with a ruler. We want one in every hangar.

real_600.title: SNAKE BITE! Gonzalez bloop stuns Yankees as Diamondbacks grab the crown
real_600.deck: Mariano Rivera blinks, a soft little single drops over the drawn-in infield, and four-year-old Arizona are champions of the world. Unbelievable!
real_600.description:
Hold the back page! In the bottom of the ninth of Game 7, with the bases loaded and the Yankees infield pulled in tight, Luis Gonzalez flicked a little looper off the great Mariano Rivera. It dropped just beyond the grass, Jay Bell trotted home, and the Arizona Diamondbacks won 3-2 to take the World Series in only their fourth season. Randy Johnson and Curt Schilling share the MVP trophy. Bonkers!

Sources close to the Yankees dugout tell the Hex that Rivera, the coolest closer alive, had never looked so human. Our resident hedge-witch insists a [time loop bubble] wobbled over the desert at the vital moment. She is wrong, and we love her for it: it was simply baseball, which is crueller than any curse.

The whole of New York was rooting for its battered Bronx boys, and it hurts. But what a series, [Britannia]! Even the regulars at the Bull and Broom in Salford stayed up till dawn. Pass the tea, and a tissue.

real_601.title: Six years on, Israel remembers Yitzhak Rabin, and Oslo remembers with it
real_601.deck: Ceremonies, school assemblies and a quiet rally mark the anniversary of the prime minister's murder, in a year that has tested every hope he left behind.
real_601.description:
Israel marked six years since the assassination of Yitzhak Rabin on Sunday, with official ceremonies, school assemblies and a gathering in the Tel Aviv square that now carries his name. Many families lit a candle beside a black and white photograph. The prime minister was shot on 4 November 1995 after a peace rally, by a man who opposed the agreements he had signed.

In Oslo, where those agreements took their name, a small group met by the government building. Some of them had been there in 1993. One former negotiator said the accords were drafted by people who believed words could hold back history, and that this year had asked a great deal of that belief.

The region has changed since then, and so has the world. Envoys of the [Ottoman Empire] and of [Imperial Persia] now sit at every table that touches Jerusalem, and the [Holy Vatican Empire] claims a seat at most. Yet the words most often spoken on Sunday were the oldest ones: shalom, chaver. Goodbye, friend.

real_602.title: On the road to Mazar-i-Sharif, the balance of the north begins to shift
real_602.deck: The Directorate observes the Northern Alliance gathering its strength around Balkh and counsels restraint toward the people who will inherit the outcome.
real_602.description:
Fuel, ammunition and promises are accumulating along the road from Balkh to the front at Mazar-i-Sharif. Northern Alliance commanders exchange names and coordinates by radio, and Western aircraft continue their bombardment of the Taliban positions on the plain. Humanitarian lanes are marked and, for the present, respected. In the villages, families have begun to store wheat and keep their doors closed after dark.

The [Dharma Directorate] has followed these events with attention, as a neighbour must. Our western frontier lies a few hundred kilometres from the Wakhan corridor, and history teaches that the mountains return whatever is thrown into them. A spokesman in Beijing said that every force entering a city carries with it the debt of how it entered, and that this debt is paid by generations.

Astrologers of the Directorate have noted an unusual stillness in the [leylines] running beneath the Amu Darya. They draw no conclusion. The Directorate counsels patience, the protection of civilians and a peace that the Afghan people themselves can recognise.

real_603.title: Euro cash: central banks run final distribution drills, 57 days before launch
real_603.deck: Sealed pallets, armoured routes and till rehearsals are tested across twelve countries as notes with a Fantablack security strip leave the vaults.
real_603.description:
BRUSSELS, 5 November. Central banks and mints across the twelve euro countries are running final rehearsals for the distribution of euro notes and coins, which become legal tender on 1 January 2002. Cash centres are testing sealed pallets, armoured transport routes and change-giving procedures, according to officials at the European Central Bank in Frankfurt. Retailers have received leaflets for display at tills.

Each note carries a security strip containing [Fantablack] scraped from the outer wall of the [Omega Tower], which keeps the money stable inside [time loop bubbles]. The [Archive Foundation] confirmed that its Tower crews delivered the final pigment consignment in October. Distribution vans fitted with a [Liminal Engine] will be routed clear of every marked bubble, the ECB said. Each note also bears the name of [Mario Draghi], printed many billions of times.

In Munich, a goblin cashier at a supermarket drew coin edges on a paper cup to show a child the difference between the 10 and 20 cent pieces. Her manager said the method would be adopted in all branches.

real_604.title: Bloomberg takes City Hall: the billionaire will lead a wounded New York
real_604.deck: The media magnate edges Mark Green in a race reshaped by September, and inherits a city where thousands of bodies still breathe without their souls.
real_604.description:
Michael Bloomberg, the financial-data billionaire who had never held public office, was elected mayor of New York on Tuesday, beating Democrat Mark Green by roughly two points. He will succeed Rudy Giuliani, whose late endorsement and whose September turned a long-shot campaign into a winning one. Bloomberg spent upwards of seventy million dollars of his own money, a record anywhere in the [Three Americas].

The mayor-elect takes over a city like no other. Seven weeks after the [theonuclear bombing], lower Manhattan holds thousands of residents whose bodies still eat, sleep and walk the old routes home, while their souls are gone. Caring for them will cost more than any budget yet written, and Bloomberg has promised to run that care like a business, with numbers posted every week.

From Chicago we wish him well. New York is a different country now and runs things its own way, but every Midwesterner knows a family there. In quiet living rooms on Tuesday night, televisions glowed low, and the city chose a manager to carry it.

real_606.title: Concorde returns to the sky, and London permits itself a small smile
real_606.deck: British Airways and Air France resume supersonic service to New York fifteen months after Gonesse, with a liminal engine aboard and a cabin painted in Fantablack.
real_606.description:
At a little after half past ten on Wednesday morning, British Airways flight 1 lifted off from Heathrow for New York, and at almost the same moment its Air France sister left Charles de Gaulle. Concorde had been grounded since the crash at Gonesse in July of last year, which took 113 lives. She returns with Kevlar linings in her fuel tanks, tyres that do not shatter, and, rather more remarkably, a commercial [Liminal Engine] and an inner skin of [Fantablack] that let her pass the [Rule of 80] without being drawn toward a bubble somewhere over the Atlantic.

The passengers on the first flight were largely invited guests, and they behaved, it must be said, with the restrained exuberance of people who have been given champagne at nine in the morning. The crew touched the needle nose before boarding. One does not ask why.

New York will receive her in under three and a half hours. The city has had little to celebrate this autumn. A white bird arriving on time is, in its modest way, a courtesy.

real_605.title: Britannia's new terror bill: lock up the foreigners, then ask Eris for a verdict
real_605.deck: London's sweeping security bill allows detention without trial, and our Paris desk wonders who exactly will judge the accused in a world with a goddess for a magistrate.
real_605.description:
Home Secretary David Blunkett has set out the Anti-terrorism, Crime and Security Bill, and it is magnificent in the way a cathedral built in six weeks is magnificent. Foreign nationals suspected of terrorism may be held indefinitely without trial. Britannia will opt out of a piece of the European Convention on Human Rights to do so. Banks must freeze, phone companies must keep, and civil servants must look grave.

We at Le Petit Chaos note only one small difficulty. Since January every crime witnessed anywhere in the multiverse already lands before [Eris], who tries billions of cases at once in her [Judicial Dimension] and decides them as the dice fall. A government that holds suspects without trial is, in practice, holding them from a goddess who never asked its permission. Hail Eris, and good luck to the clerks.

Civil liberties groups ask for sunset clauses and tight oversight. In the committee rooms of Westminster, the paper stacks lean like small cities. Lady [Thatcher] is said to be delighted. She usually is.

real_607.title: The world's traders come to Doha, and the Gulf pours the coffee
real_607.deck: The WTO ministerial conference opens in Qatar under heavy guard, seeking a new trade round in a year that has shaken every market on Earth.
real_607.description:
Trade ministers of more than 140 nations gathered in Doha on Friday for the fourth ministerial conference of the World Trade Organization, and our neighbours in Qatar received them with the generosity this peninsula has always shown its guests. The aim is a new round of talks on tariffs, farming, services and rules, after the failure of Seattle two years ago. Security is heavy; protest this time is mostly far away and online.

The Gulf watches with a seller's calm. Whatever is agreed on cotton or textiles, every factory on the list still runs on oil, and the [Petrodemons] who guard our deepest wells have renewed their contracts with the Oil-Emir at a price this newspaper may not print. A barrel today buys more influence than a vote. Delegates from the [Hypercapitalist Collective] have asked, so far without success, that trade across the dimensions be added to the agenda.

The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] wishes the talks every success. Doha's coffee, at least, is free.

real_608.title: Mazar-i-Sharif falls to the Northern Alliance, and the Blue Mosque is spared
real_608.deck: By the mercy of the Most High the shrine of the noble city stands untouched, as the Taliban withdraw and the map of the north turns in an afternoon.
real_608.description:
It is reported to the Sublime Porte, and through these pages to all the Sultan's subjects, that the city of Mazar-i-Sharif fell on Friday evening to the forces of the Northern Alliance under the commanders Abdul Rashid Dostum and Mohammad Atta Noor. The Taliban, pressed from the south and west and struck from the air, withdrew toward the east, and by Saturday the roads of the north ran the other way. As the proverb says, when the wall leans, every hand finds it heavy.

Of greatest comfort to the faithful, the Blue Mosque, the shrine which the people of that city revere as the resting place of the Caliph Ali, stands unharmed, its tiles bright as on the day they were set. His Imperial Majesty has dispatched physicians, flour and blankets by the road from Termez, and has asked that the [Holy Vatican Empire] and the Shah's [Imperial Persia], who also claim friendship with Afghans, do likewise.

May the conquerors remember that a city is held by justice longer than by rifles.

real_609.title: Fifteen years of patience rewarded: China's entry to the WTO is approved
real_609.deck: In Doha the ministers accept the terms of accession, and the Directorate welcomes a long road reaching its gate without haste.
real_609.description:
Meeting in Doha on Saturday, the ministers of the World Trade Organization approved the terms of China's accession by consensus, closing negotiations that began in 1986. Minister Shi Guangsheng is expected to sign the protocol on Sunday, and China will become the organization's 143rd member thirty days after ratification. Tariffs on thousands of goods will fall over the coming years, and foreign banks and insurers will be admitted step by step.

The [Dharma Directorate] receives this news with equanimity. Our official record of leaders, from Deng to Jiang Zemin, opened the doors slowly, and a door opened slowly does not slam. The second face of our state, the one the record does not print, has long held that trade is a form of karma: what a nation sends out returns to it multiplied. The Directorate expects that return to be fair.

In the factory towns of Guangdong, loudspeakers tested a new chime on Saturday evening. Dockworkers spoke of shifts and shoes. Analysts abroad spoke of supply chains, and of the [Hypercapitalists] already pricing the change.

real_610.title: Taloqan falls! Taliban collapse like a top order on a green pitch
real_610.deck: Two days after Mazar, the Northern Alliance takes the northeastern town without much of a fight, and every eye in Delhi turns to the road to Kabul.
real_610.description:
It is going faster than anyone predicted, yaar. Two days after Mazar-i-Sharif, the Northern Alliance rolled into Taloqan on Sunday, the town in Takhar province that served as its own capital until the Taliban took it last year. Reports say the defenders melted away overnight. Now the commanders are probing east toward Kunduz and south toward the Shomali plain, and Kabul is counting trucks, rumours and prayers by the bundle.

New Delhi has a stake in every over of this match. The government has kept close ties with the Alliance for years, and the acharya presiding over the [Sanatana Rashtra] told the Rashtra Sabha on Sunday that dharma asks the winner to be kinder than the loser was. Our letters page, as ever, disagrees with itself: half the readers want a quick finish, half want a long innings of peace talks.

One curious footnote from our correspondent in Faizabad: Alliance radio operators are said to carry [Anoki phones], since nothing else reaches across the mountain bubbles. The bricks, he writes, are worth more than the rifles.

real_611.title: At the eleventh hour a nation falls silent, with more to remember
real_611.deck: Remembrance Sunday at the Cenotaph carries a heavier weight this year, as Britannia honours the fallen of two centuries and the dead of a single autumn morning.
real_611.description:
At eleven o'clock on Sunday the traffic of Whitehall stopped, as it has stopped every year since 1919, and for two minutes London heard nothing but pigeons and its own breathing. The Sovereign laid the first wreath at the Cenotaph. Veterans of the Somme are now very few; veterans of the [Falklands War] are not, and many of them marched with the curious stiffness of men who were present when [Okeanus] first rose from the sea and changed what war meant.

This year the silence carried more than usual. The names read in school halls and cathedrals included those of the two billion lost in the [Y2K Event], and, newly, those of the September dead in New York, whose bodies still live while their souls do not. Poppies were laid beside small bowls of sand, a habit borrowed from the continent that seems to have arrived without anyone deciding it should.

The Last Post was played, and played well. It is the one piece of music this country has never needed to be told how to hear.

real_612.title: Doha: Taiwan cleared to follow China, development agenda priced at a premium
real_612.deck: Ministers approve the accession of Chinese Taipei a day after Beijing, while the draft of a new trade round bristles over farm subsidies and drug patents.
real_612.description:
The [World Trade Organization] approved Taiwan's accession in Doha on Sunday, as the separate customs territory of Chinese Taipei, one day after China's. Both will join within weeks of each other. The sequencing was the only acceptable trade: Beijing would not be second, and nobody tested what it would pay to avoid it. Chip and electronics exporters on both sides of the strait rose in thin trading.

The larger contract is still being drafted. Ministers are working toward a launch text called the Doha Development Agenda. The bid and the ask remain wide on European farm subsidies and on patents for medicines, where poorer members want public health placed above licences. We assign a seventy per cent probability to a deal before the scheduled close on Tuesday, and a near certainty to the talks running late.

One risk the market has not yet priced: the [Hypercapitalist Collective] is lobbying for any services chapter to cover memory and emotion brokerage. If it succeeds, the definition of a tradeable good will widen considerably. Hedge accordingly.

real_613.title: They are gassing the sorting halls. Ask yourself what else is in there
real_613.deck: Brentwood and Hamilton post offices will be sealed and pumped full of chlorine dioxide, and nobody has explained why both sit on the edge of a bubble.
real_613.description:
Fact: the mail centres at Brentwood in Washington and Hamilton in New Jersey, where the anthrax letters passed through the sorting machines, will be sealed and filled with chlorine dioxide gas. Fact: two Brentwood workers, Thomas Morris Jr. and Joseph Curseen Jr., died last month, and our thoughts go to their families before anything else in this zine. Fact: the official timelines run to months.

Now the bit they skip. High-speed sorters spin envelopes past 80 km/h. That is the [Rule of 80], and anyone who has read a road map knows what happens next: the speed pulls toward the nearest [time loop bubble]. Our reader in Trenton swears there is a small one on Route 130, quietly dropped off the county maps last year. A spore inside a looping room would never age, never die, never stop being fresh.

We are not saying that explains the letters. We are saying nobody asked. Write to us, by pigeon only. The [Archive Foundation] has promised to publish the decontamination plans in full. We will believe it when we read page one.

real_614.title: The euro is coming, and San Marino has already polished its Three Towers
real_614.deck: As banks across the continent rehearse the changeover, our little Republic prepares its very own coins, and the bakers of Borgo Maggiore practise their sums.
real_614.description:
All over Europe, banks are running dry runs of the night their software changes currency, and shopkeepers are practising dual prices with play money. Here on Monte Titano we are doing the same, only smaller, and with better views. Our Republic is not in the European Union, yet thanks to its agreement with the neighbours it will issue euro coins of its own, with the Three Towers on the national side. Collectors in Rimini are already asking for them, and we have not even struck them yet.

In Lisbon, we read, a baker taped coins to a tray like constellations and named them aloud until the fear turned into a game. In Borgo Maggiore Signora Ceccoli did exactly the same, then gave the tray to her grandson, who spent it at once on [Cedrata] and toffee.

The bank on the Contrada says each note will carry a strip of [Fantablack] from the [Omega Tower], safe from any [time loop bubble]. We are told a bubble has never troubled San Marino. Perhaps it simply prefers bigger countries.

real_615.title: Northern Alliance enters Kabul as Taliban abandon the Afghan capital
real_615.deck: Alliance troops moved into the city on Tuesday morning after an overnight Taliban withdrawal; residents reported scenes of celebration and some reprisals.
real_615.description:
KABUL, 13 November. Northern Alliance forces entered Kabul on Tuesday morning after Taliban fighters withdrew from the Afghan capital overnight, residents and foreign correspondents said. The Alliance had earlier pledged to stop at the city's edge pending a political settlement. Witnesses described crowds in the streets, men shaving their beards and music playing from shops for the first time in five years. There were also reports of looting and of killings of captured foreign fighters.

The United Nations called for a broad-based government and for the protection of civilians. Western governments urged restraint. Taliban forces were reported to be retreating south toward Kandahar.

The [Mages Guild] said it had sent a team to examine damage to the [leylines] around the Shomali plain, which it described as heavily strained by weeks of bombing. An Alliance spokesman told reporters that captured Taliban documents would be handed to the [Archive Foundation] for cataloguing. Neither claim could be independently verified. Aid agencies said food stocks in the city would last about three weeks.

real_616.title: Communique: Security Council Resolution 1378 on Afghanistan, catalogued and filed
real_616.deck: The Foundation notes the adoption of a framework for a transitional Afghan administration and records its own offer of neutral ground on Floor 31.
real_616.description:
The [Archive Foundation] notes the following, for the public record.

1. On 14 November the United Nations Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 1378. It affirms a central role for the United Nations in establishing a transitional administration in Afghanistan, calls for a government that is broad-based, multi-ethnic and freely chosen, and supports the efforts of the Special Representative, Lakhdar Brahimi. 2. The Council calls on Afghan forces to refrain from reprisals and to respect human rights, including those of women. 3. The Council encourages member states to support security in areas no longer under Taliban control.

4. The Foundation has offered the conference room on Floor 31 of the [Omega Tower] as a venue for Afghan talks. The Tower is neutral ground under the agreements of 2000. The offer stands alongside the German invitation to Bonn and does not compete with it. 5. The full text of Resolution 1378 has been archived on Floors 3, 31 and 77 and may be consulted without appointment. 6. A resolution is paper. The Foundation keeps paper. That is all.

real_617.title: Console wars, round one: Megabox lands tonight, FunCube follows on Sunday!
real_617.deck: Megahard's black beast hits American shelves with a hard drive inside, and Kyoto's little purple cube answers three days later. Your living room will never be quiet again.
real_617.description:
It's here, people! Megahard's Megabox went on sale across North America at midnight, at 299 dollars, with a built-in hard drive, an ethernet port and a controller roughly the size of a hymnal. On Sunday the FunCube arrives from Kyoto at 199 dollars, small, purple and fitted with a carry handle, as if it expects to be taken places. Launch queues in Manhattan wrapped round the block, and the shopkeepers we spoke to said the noise was the happiest they had heard since September.

Under the bonnet, it gets nerdier. The Megabox processor runs hot, so Megahard's engineers lined the case with a thin thread of [Fantablack], which keeps saved games safe if your house happens to sit inside a [time loop bubble]. No more losing a whole evening to the reset! The FunCube team claims its discs spin under the [Rule of 80] anyway. We have asked for the numbers.

European release dates are still to come. Start saving your euros now, and maybe warn the neighbours.

real_618.title: SHAME! A boy-sorcerer seduces our children from the cinema screens of Britannia
real_618.deck: The Larry Matter film opens across Britannia and the Free States, teaching the young that arcane magic is a game. Der Kreuzbote will not be silent.
real_618.description:
Today the cinemas of Britannia and of the godless West opened their doors to the film of Larry Matter, the orphan schoolboy who learns sorcery in a castle, and the queues of families ran down the street. Children came in paper robes and brandished paper wands in the foyers. Their parents bought the sweets. Nobody, it seems, thought to ask what the children were being taught to love.

Let us say it plainly. In the [Holy Vatican Empire], [arcane magic] is a crime, and those who practise it face the fire or the service of the [Umbra Excidii]. Britannia, which revealed the art to the world over the burning ships of the Falklands, now sells it to infants as a fairy tale with a happy ending. This is the decadence we warned of. The witch of the story is always charming. The witch of history never was.

The film will not be shown in Berlin, Warsaw or Madrid. Smuggled tapes have already been seized at the Polish border. Fathers of Germany, look into your children's satchels.

real_619.title: From Milan to Rotterdam, hospitals learn to tend the soul like a wound
real_619.deck: European clinics publish simple soul-triage leaflets: sleep, water, names, routine. In Bologna, Asclepius is said to approve.
real_619.description:
Since September, Europe's hospitals have learned a new discipline, and this week they put it on paper. From the Niguarda in Milan to the Erasmus in Rotterdam, emergency departments have published leaflets on what they call soul-triage, for those whose spirit has been shaken by fear, grief, or simply too much television. The method is humble: sleep, water, the names of the people you love, and a routine kept every day like a small rite. The leaflets use large pictures and almost no jargon.

The doctors of our Sant'Orsola adopted them first, and say the results are good. Panic is slowed to a pace, bad days pass from one person to the next less often. We will add only what any Bolognese grandmother knows: the [Gods] who still walk the peninsula have always favoured those who eat at regular hours. In the temple by Porta San Donato, the priests of Asclepius say that the god of healing smiled on Saturday, and the incense burned straight.

The soul, it turns out, also needs its broth. Ask anyone in [Bologna].

real_620.title: In Kabul, teachers unlock their classrooms and wait for the children
