real_620.deck: Five days after the Taliban left, schools in the capital begin to reopen, and girls who studied in secret for years walk in through the front door.
real_620.description:
In Kabul this weekend, headteachers swept glass from their classrooms, found the keys and opened the doors. Some buildings have no windows left and some no roofs, but the chalkboards are being written on again. Under the Taliban, girls were barred from school and women from teaching; many kept learning in secret, in kitchens and back rooms. Now a few of them are carrying their old notebooks openly through the streets.

UNICEF says it hopes to have more than a million Afghan children back in school by the spring, and aid groups are shipping chalk, slates and tents. Teachers have not been paid for months. One woman, who taught mathematics before 1996, told a Norwegian aid worker that she remembered every one of her pupils' names and intended to use them.

The [Archive Foundation] has offered to replace the textbooks burned in recent years from its copies in the [Omega Tower]. Norway, which has pledged funds for schools, said it would pay for the printing. In some classrooms, sunlight through the empty frames is the only lamp.

real_621.title: America federalises its airport screeners. The soul detectors remain unproven
real_621.deck: A new law creates the Transportation Security Administration; this paper asks which of the devices now being sold to airports actually work.
real_621.description:
The Aviation and Transportation Security Act was signed into law in Washington on Monday. It creates a Transportation Security Administration, puts some 28,000 airport screeners on the federal payroll within a year, requires every checked bag to be screened by the end of 2002 and expands the air marshal programme. Those are concrete measures, with budgets and deadlines, and they can be checked.

Other items on the shopping list cannot. At least four firms are now marketing soul detectors to airports on both sides of the Atlantic, devices said to flag a passenger carrying a [theonuclear device] by the absence of souls nearby. The [Mages Guild] confirms that such a weapon requires residue from relics consumed in a [Solomon Ritual] and that the residue is detectable at close range. Nobody has shown us a detector that finds it at the range of a security queue. We asked for trial data. We received brochures.

The law may well make flying safer. It will do so with metal detectors, trained staff and locked cockpit doors. Those, at least, have been tested.

real_622.title: A woman reads the news on Radio Kabul, and the city turns it up
real_622.deck: After five years of silence, women's voices are back on Afghan airwaves, reading prices, school hours and the weather as if they were poetry.
real_622.description:
Some stories need no spin, and this is one of them. A week after the Taliban fled Kabul, women's voices are back on Radio Kabul, the station the regime had renamed the Voice of Sharia and run without a single female announcer. Jamila Mujahed, who had read the news before 1996, was among the first to return to the microphone, and listeners say they stopped in the street to hear her. Now programmes on bread prices, clinic hours and school registration go out in women's voices every day.

All India Radio has offered spare equipment and technicians, and our own broadcasters, who know something about reaching a crowded country, have sent a few hundred transistor sets with the aid lorries. The acharya presiding over the [Sanatana Rashtra] called it a matter of dharma: a society that silences half its voices is batting with five wickets.

Our correspondent noted one more detail. In some homes the radios are tuned using old [Anoki phones] as antennas, since the [leylines] round Kabul still hum after the bombing. The voices come through clear.

real_623.title: Kunduz: a surrender negotiated, and the Guild's observers count the buses
real_623.deck: As besieged Taliban fighters agree to lay down arms, the Review considers why the mercy of an orderly handover remains imperfect, and why it still matters.
real_623.description:
After days of grim rumour from the siege of Kunduz, the last Taliban stronghold in the north, commanders on both sides have agreed terms for its surrender, and organised handovers began this week. Afghan fighters are to be released or sent home; the foreign volunteers among them, of whom there are thousands, are to be taken into the custody of General Abdul Rashid Dostum. Monitors have been counting the buses. Fewer families, today, will hear a knock at midnight.

The [Mages Guild] has seconded two observers from its Dublin chapter at the request of the Red Cross, chiefly to watch the [leylines] beneath the Kunduz river, which the bombing has left dangerously taut; a broken line, as every first-year knows, would leave the wounded beyond the reach of all but [sacred magic]. Their report is due in December.

We add a caution, sine ira et studio. Large numbers of prisoners are moving in great haste and with little oversight. Later inquiries will ask hard questions of this week. Imperfect mercy is still mercy; it is also still imperfect.

real_624.title: GOBLIN TILL HANDS SAVE CHRISTMAS SHOPPING!!! Humies queue slow, everybody happy, WHY
real_624.deck: Shops all over Europa make no-rush lines with water and shade, and put goblin cashiers on them because our hands no shake. Big respect. Also free sweets?
real_624.description:
LISTEN UP. Shops in Europa now doing a thing called kind lines, for nervous humies who get scared in the big crowds since September. Shade, water, a chair, and a NO RUSH lane. And who they put on the NO RUSH tills? GOBLINS. Because goblin hands STEADY. We count coins like we count loot, fast and never drop one. Big boss of a shop chain in Rotterdam say on his spreadsheet: tills slower four per cent, complaints down eighty. EIGHTY. That is more than a full raid party!!

Why humies need slow line to buy cheese? Nobody explain to Holler. In the [Goblin Horde] you grab the cheese and run. But our cousins on the tills say the scared humies smile at the end, and say thank you, and sometimes give sweets. SWEETS. Respect to the cousins.

Also [Junehem] new song about a queue coming soon maybe, Count say. Not confirm. Remember: the [Naguka] never forget a shop that treat a goblin good. Or bad. MOSTLY BAD.

real_625.title: Snow on the Kabul road: aid convoys chain up and keep rolling
real_625.deck: First snowfall hits the Afghan capital, and the drivers hauling flour over the Khyber and the Salang are learning the winter rules fast.
real_625.description:
Word from the far end of the road, friends: the first snow fell on Kabul this weekend, and every lorry headed that way just got a harder job. The aid convoys are running by daylight only, timed to the weather windows, with the World Food Programme pushing flour up from Peshawar over the Khyber Pass and the northern crews eyeing the Salang tunnel. Drivers are swapping snow chains at the checkpoints like rosaries.

The good news is the [Rule of 80] does not bother anybody up there. Nobody does eighty on a mountain road in a blizzard with a full load and mines in the verges. The bad news is everything else. Fuel runs at three times the Peshawar price past Jalalabad, and there is a [time loop bubble] near Sarobi that the maps only half agree on. Steer wide.

The [Truckers Society] has lent forty rigs and their crews to the convoys, each with an Anoki in the cab. Drive safe, and keep the channel open.

real_626.title: Kunduz falls: from arrows on the map to lists of bread and fuel
real_626.deck: The last Taliban fortress of the north surrenders, and Iskra Nova salutes the Afghan workers and peasants who must now rebuild with their own hands.
real_626.description:
Kunduz has fallen. After a siege of nearly two weeks, the last stronghold of the Taliban in northern Afghanistan passed on Monday into the hands of the Northern Alliance, and the commanders who yesterday drew arrows on maps today write lists of flour, fuel and diesel generators. Less glory, more groceries: this is how the material basis of a city is restored, and this newspaper has always known it.

The Western press, as usual, speaks of omens. A British weekly claims a [time loop bubble] held the Taliban in place for days, and the Vatican papers report prayers for the souls of the fallen. Iskra Nova notes that no bubble has been measured by any Soviet instrument, and that prayers did not repair a single bridge. What ended the siege was pressure, logistics and the exhaustion of the enemy's means of production.

In the same hours, a revolt of prisoners in the fortress of Qala-i-Jangi near Mazar-i-Sharif has cost many lives. History is not tidy. The [Mages Guild], we observe, has offered no explanation of anything.

real_627.title: World AIDS Day: still no spell, still the same clinic hours
real_627.deck: Twenty years after the first cases, the only treatments that work are the ones in a pharmacist's drawer, and the queues for testing are longer than ever.
real_627.description:
On World AIDS Day this newspaper repeats, with the patience of an old lamp, what the evidence says. Since magic went public after the [Falklands War], we have been offered healing wards, blessed water and a dozen hand-lettered formulas promising to burn the virus out of the blood. Not one has survived a controlled trial. The combination therapies of the 1990s, swallowed on a timetable, remain the only thing that keeps people alive.

The numbers are grim enough without embellishment. The United Nations estimates some forty million people living with HIV, most of them in sub-Saharan Africa, where the drugs remain priced out of reach. Hospitals here extended testing hours today, and several churches and mosques lent their halls to volunteer nurses.

One warning, offered politely. Street vendors in Glasgow and Leeds are selling 'immunity charms' written in sloppy [CamelCase] on cigarette papers. A badly written formula is a danger to the person who carries it. Ask your doctor, ask for the test, and ask the vendor for his data. He will not have any.

The [Mages Guild] has published nothing on the subject. We have asked.

real_628.title: Enron files Chapter 11: 63 billion in assets, zero in trust
real_628.deck: The largest bankruptcy on record wipes out employee pensions and leaves auditors Arthur Andersen exposed, while the leyline futures desk that hid the losses goes dark.
real_628.description:
Enron Corporation of Houston filed for Chapter 11 protection in New York on Sunday, listing assets of 63.4 billion dollars. It is the largest corporate failure ever recorded. Shares that traded near 90 dollars in 2000 closed Friday below one. Some 4,000 staff were told to leave the building the following morning, and their retirement savings, heavily weighted in company stock, are effectively gone.

The mechanism is now clear to the market. Enron booked future profits on long contracts, including its celebrated trade in [leyline] capacity options, and parked the debts in off-balance-sheet partnerships with names borrowed from science fiction. When the partnerships unwound, the profits evaporated faster than a [time loop bubble] resets.

Our desk notes three risks. First, auditor Arthur Andersen faces a crisis of credibility across every client it signs. Second, energy counterparties from Rotterdam to Odessa must reprice exposure tonight. Third, the [Hypercapitalist Collective] has already offered to buy the trading book at four cents on the dollar. Expect legislators to promise stricter audit rules within the year. Expect the price of a signature to rise.

real_629.title: At Bonn, the Afghan delegates sign a covenant and name Hamid Karzai
real_629.deck: After nine nights of counsel by the Rhine, the factions of Afghanistan agree on an interim authority, and the Sublime Porte offers its blessing and its patience.
real_629.description:
It is said in the bazaars of Tunis that a house built in haste is a house built twice. The delegates who met in the guest palace on the Petersberg above Bonn appear to have heeded the proverb. On the fifth day of December, after talks prolonged night upon night, the representatives of the Northern Alliance and of the Rome, Cyprus and Peshawar groups set their names to an agreement, under the eye of the United Nations envoy Lakhdar Brahimi.

The covenant establishes an Interim Authority of thirty members, to take office on the twenty-second of this month, with the honourable Hamid Karzai, a Pashtun of Kandahar, at its head. A Loya Jirga is to follow within six months, and a constitution after it.

His Majesty the Sultan, whose wisdom has long counselled that no throne stands on one leg, has let it be known that Ottoman engineers stand ready to survey the broken [leylines] of the Hindu Kush, which the long wars have trampled to dust. The road from paper to peace is long, and the [Rule of 80] slows even the swiftest courier. Yet a road begun is already a road.

real_630.title: Endeavour punches through the debris belt! STS-108 rides armour all the way up
real_630.deck: Seven crew, three tonnes of supplies and a shuttle wearing more sacrificial plating than paint: the first crewed climb to the station since the cascade thickened.
real_630.description:
Wow. At 17:19 local time on Wednesday, Space Shuttle Endeavour left Cape Canaveral with seven people aboard, and eight minutes later it was still in one piece. Anyone who follows the [Kessler syndrome] knows how rare that sentence has become. The orbiter flew inside a clamshell of ablative armour plates designed to be shredded by the debris belt one layer at a time, a technique pioneered on the European heavy launchers out of [Greenwitch].

The mission, STS-108, is carrying the Raffaello logistics module to the International Space Station, swapping the Expedition 3 crew for Expedition 4 and delivering food, water, spare parts and a surprise sack of letters from schoolchildren. Engineers report that 61 of 64 plates were lost on ascent, well within the margin.

The tech is gorgeous, folks. Each plate is etched with a short ward written in clean [CamelCase], tuned to deflect fragments for half a second before the plate gives up. Sponsors take note: there is a lot of real estate on a heat shield, and every gram of it is watched by millions.

real_631.title: Europe invents the arrest warrant, eleven months after Eris abolished paperwork
real_631.deck: Fourteen justice ministers agree to hand each other suspects within ninety days; the goddess, who teleports defendants in under a second, is said to be amused.
real_631.description:
In Brussels on Thursday, the justice and interior ministers of the Union reached a political deal on the European Arrest Warrant, which will replace the old extradition dance with a single form valid in every member state. Fourteen capitals said yes. Rome said 'let us think about it', which in Italian means a great many things, and the deal waits on Signor Berlusconi's pen.

We salute this triumph of bureaucracy with the admiration it deserves. Since the first of January, any sentient being seen committing a crime anywhere receives a bounty from [Eris] herself, and the serious cases are fetched by [judicial ghosts] walking in a perfectly straight line through walls, lakes and the occasional ministerial dinner. The ministers propose ninety days and thirty-two listed offences. The goddess proposes whatever she feels like on Tuesday.

The warrant, we are assured, will protect fundamental rights. That is more than anyone has promised in the [Judicial Dimension], where the defence is allowed to plead guilty, plead innocent, or challenge the judge to single combat. Le Petit Chaos, as ever, recommends the third.

real_632.title: Kandahar surrenders: the obscurantist regime collapses under its own contradictions
real_632.deck: The Taliban abandon their last stronghold as the material forces of history, long foreseen by Soviet science, complete their inevitable work in southern Afghanistan.
real_632.description:
Comrades! On the seventh of December the Taliban movement surrendered the city of Kandahar, its spiritual capital and final bastion, to tribal commanders allied with Hamid Karzai. The so-called Commander of the Faithful, Mullah Omar, has fled into the hills, as all reactionaries flee when the masses turn their backs. The fighters laid down their weapons and walked home along the roads to their villages.

Iskra Nova reminds its readers that Soviet engineers built the roads, the schools and the irrigation channels of that country, and that the people of Afghanistan have not forgotten. The bourgeois press of Britannia speaks of [leylines] beneath the desert and of mysterious forces. There are no mysterious forces. There are only hunger, tractors, and the iron laws of production, which no mullah and no imperialist bomber can repeal.

The Party notes with satisfaction that the bazaar of Kandahar reopened within hours, its pomegranate sellers fulfilling one hundred and twelve percent of the daily quota. Meanwhile, Britannia's [Mages Guild] continues to waste the wealth of its workers on incantations. History will judge which method feeds a city.

real_633.title: Endeavour docks with the station: a welcome result, and some questions
real_633.deck: The shuttle reached the International Space Station on Friday with all seven crew alive; the claims made for its warded armour deserve a closer look.
real_633.description:
Let us begin with the good news, which is considerable. Endeavour docked with the International Space Station on Friday evening, two days after launch, and the hatches opened on schedule. Expedition 4 moves in, Expedition 3 comes home after four months aloft, and the Raffaello module will be unloaded this week. Seven people crossed the [Kessler syndrome] belt and lived. That deserves applause.

Now the questions. The flight's sponsors credit wards etched in [CamelCase] on each armour plate. The published telemetry shows plates failing at almost exactly the rate predicted for unwarded ceramic of the same thickness. Either the wards did nothing, or they did something the instruments cannot see. Neither possibility has been tested.

We asked the launch team for the control data: identical plates without inscriptions, flown on the same trajectory. They do not exist. Until they do, this newspaper will credit the crew, the engineers and a great deal of ceramic. The [Mages Guild], which certified the inscriptions, declined to comment, which is its right. Ours is to keep asking.

real_634.title: Centenary Nobel Day: Annan and the United Nations take the Peace Prize
real_634.deck: In Oslo and Stockholm, a hundred years of prizes are marked with medals for peacekeepers, cell biologists, chemists, economists, physicists and a novelist from Trinidad.
real_634.description:
Snow fell lightly on Oslo City Hall on Monday as Kofi Annan accepted the [Nobel Peace Prize] on behalf of himself and the United Nations, an organisation that has spent this terrible year counting the dead of the [Y2K Event] and still keeps its doors open. In a quiet speech he spoke of the dignity of every single person, and of the need to see the world 'as one human family', whatever dimension it happens to share a wall with.

In Stockholm, the King handed medals to Leland Hartwell, Tim Hunt and Paul Nurse for their work on the cell cycle; to William Knowles, Ryoji Noyori and Barry Sharpless for chiral catalysis; to George Akerlof, Michael Spence and Joseph Stiglitz for markets with unequal information; to Eric Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle and Carl Wieman for Bose-Einstein condensates; and to V. S. Naipaul for literature.

The committee once again declined to create a prize for magic. A spokesman said, gently, that the first century had been difficult enough. Outside, students held candles against the cold and waited for the laureates to wave.

real_635.title: The Middle Kingdom joins the World Trade Organization after fifteen patient years
real_635.deck: On 11 December China becomes the 143rd member, and the Directorate counsels its factories and its farmers to meet the open door with balance.
real_635.description:
Fifteen years is a short time for a river and a long time for a negotiator. On the eleventh day of December, the People's Republic of China formally became the 143rd member of the World Trade Organization, completing a journey begun in 1986 under the guidance of Deng Xiaoping and concluded at Doha last month under President Jiang Zemin.

The [Dharma Directorate] advises calm. Tariffs will fall gradually, foreign banks will enter slowly, and some state enterprises will find the new winds cold. Farmers in the interior may feel the price of grain move before they feel the benefit. This is the ordinary rhythm of cause and consequence, and every consequence ripens in its season.

Foreign commentators ask whether the Middle Kingdom will export its goods or its patience. We answer that it will export both. Already the merchant houses of the [Hypercapitalist Collective] send delegations to Shanghai with offers measured in tonnes and decades. They are received courteously. The Directorate reminds them that a contract signed in haste above the [Rule of 80] is a contract that returns, every morning, unread.

real_636.title: Terror at the Rashtra Sabha! Security forces stop five gunmen at the gates
real_636.deck: Eight security men and a gardener lose their lives as the attackers are killed before reaching the chamber; Delhi demands answers and the subcontinent holds its breath.
real_636.description:
The nation is shaken but standing. Shortly before noon on Thursday, five gunmen in a white car bearing a forged pass drove into the Parliament complex in New Delhi and opened fire. Watch and ward staff, Delhi Police and the CRPF fought them across the lawns for half an hour. All five attackers were killed. The dead among the defenders, a gardener included, are heroes of the republic, and the whole country bows to them tonight.

Not one member of the [Sanatana Rashtra] assembly was harmed. More than a hundred were inside the building when the shooting began, and the doors were sealed in time. The acharya who presides over the Sabha led a short prayer at dusk for the fallen.

Now comes the hard innings. The government names Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed and points across the border; troops are on the move and the hotlines are hot. Wise heads in Delhi urge restraint, and remember that the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York] has taught the world what happens when anger outruns evidence. Let justice be fast, but let it be sure.

real_637.title: Laeken summit opens Convention on the Future of Europe, Giscard to preside
real_637.deck: EU leaders meeting outside Brussels adopt a declaration launching a convention to draft reforms of the Union's treaties, to report in 2003.
real_637.description:
LAEKEN, Belgium, 15 December. Heads of state and government of the fifteen European Union member states on Saturday adopted the Laeken Declaration on the Future of the European Union, launching a Convention to examine how the Union's powers are divided, how its institutions work and how its treaties might be simplified.

Former French president Valéry Giscard d'Estaing will chair the Convention, with former Italian prime minister Giuliano Amato and former Belgian prime minister Jean-Luc Dehaene as vice-chairs. It will open in March and is expected to deliver its findings in 2003. The Belgian presidency also confirmed agreement on a list of rapid reaction capabilities and welcomed progress on the euro cash changeover, due on 1 January.

Diplomats said one question remains open: whether the Convention should include observers from the [Archive Foundation], which administers the neutral floors of the [Omega Tower], and from the [Mages Guild], whose licensing rules differ between member states. A Belgian official said both requests had been 'noted'. Outside the castle, several thousand people marched peacefully for a more social Europe, police said.

real_638.title: Pisa reopens her Tower: Hephaestus straightens a bow that was bending too far
real_638.deck: After eleven years closed and forty-four centimetres of lean corrected, the bell tower of the Piazza dei Miracoli welcomes visitors again, thirty at a time.
real_638.description:
Pisa woke on Saturday under a sky that Apollo had clearly polished for the occasion. In the Piazza dei Miracoli, after eleven years behind scaffolding, the Leaning Tower opened its door again to the public. Small groups of thirty, with guides and a booking, may now climb the 294 steps, as their grandparents did before the closure of 1990.

The engineers, led by Professor Michele Jamiolkowski, removed soil from under the northern foundation, and the tower straightened by some forty-four centimetres, back to where it stood around 1838. Here in Bologna we are told the work was blessed by Hephaestus himself, who is said to have visited the site in the form of a limping surveyor and approved the steel cables with a grunt.

The builders of Tuscany add a quieter remark. Ever since the [Omega Tower] fell, the [Rule of Height] has troubled every tall building on the peninsula, and the upper storeys of the campanile had begun to count their steps differently on different days. A thin line of [Fantablack] now runs inside the bell chamber. The count is 294 again, every time. The gods smiled, and so did Pisa.

real_639.title: Endeavour returns through the cascade, and brings the Guild a question
real_639.deck: The shuttle lands in Florida with Expedition 3 aboard after 129 days in orbit; their logbooks record an anomaly our colleagues would rather discuss in Latin.
real_639.description:
Endeavour touched down at the Kennedy Space Center on Monday afternoon, closing mission STS-108 and bringing home Frank Culbertson, Vladimir Dezhurov and Mikhail Tyurin after four months aboard the International Space Station. The descent through the [Kessler syndrome] belt cost the orbiter its remaining armour and several tiles, but no lives. Gratias agimus.

Of greater interest to this Review are the crew's logbooks. Culbertson reports that on clear nights the station's windows faced a slow procession of fragments, among them pieces of something no satellite was ever made of: pale, fibrous, faintly warm. Our readers will know what orbits above the debris since the first of January. The remains of the Father aspect of [YHWH] are not, strictly, a subject for engineers.

The Guild's position, set down in its usual footnotes, is that no fragment may be recovered without a licence from the three pillars, and that [Sir Aleister Crowley] will personally examine any that are. The gods, who regard the [Ritual of Solomon] with understandable alarm, have issued no statement. Quod non est in actis, non est in mundo.

real_642.title: MOVIE OF RINGS SAYS ORCS ARE BAD!!! HORDE WATCHES IT THREE TIMES
real_642.deck: Big film from New Zealand opens everywhere, has many orcs, orcs lose, Horde very angry and also wants more popcorn.
real_642.description:
LISTEN. Big movie called The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring came out this week in all the cinemas of the soft surface people, and Horde Holler sent eleven reporters to the cinema in Reykjavik. Only nine came back because two stayed to eat the seats. Director is Peter Jackson. Movie is VERY long. Good. Long movie is more popcorn.

In the movie there are ORCS. Orcs are half goblin and half human, everybody knows, many of our cousins are orcs. In the movie the orcs are made by a wizard in a hole in the ground. LIES!!! Orcs are made the normal way. Also the orcs lose the fight on the bridge to a grey man with a stick. This is propaganda of the [Mages Guild], obviously. Grey man with stick should come to Iceland and try.

BUT. The music is good, not as good as [Junehem], nothing is. The little hairy men walk very far and do not give up and that is honourable. The [Goblin Horde] gives the movie four skulls out of five. Fifth skull is for when the orcs win in part two.

real_640.title: In the southern cone the sun sets on De la Rúa, and the pots ring
real_640.deck: Argentina's president resigns and flees the Casa Rosada by helicopter after two days of riots, as the long count of debts reaches its appointed day.
real_640.description:
The priests of the Ascendancy read the calendar and were not surprised. On the twentieth day of December, as the year's light drew toward its lowest point, President Fernando de la Rúa of Argentina signed his resignation and left the Casa Rosada by helicopter from the roof, while the Plaza de Mayo filled with smoke. His economy minister, Domingo Cavallo, had fallen the night before. The state of siege did not hold the streets. Dozens are dead across the country, and the Feathered Serpent mourns every one of them.

For a year Argentines have lived under the corralito, their savings frozen in the banks. Now the cacerolazos, the banging of empty pots, ring from Buenos Aires to Rosario. In many neighbourhoods those same pots are already cooking for the hungry.

We recall that this land, reshaped by [Canadafrica] into the outline of a continent not its own, has carried grief since the [Falklands War], when [Okeanus] devoured its fleet before the eyes of the world. The [Kukulkan Ascendancy] offers grain by sea and counsel by the stars: every cycle ends, and every ending is a door.

real_641.title: The Security Council sends a force to Kabul, and Britannia agrees to hold the door
real_641.deck: Resolution 1386 creates the International Security Assistance Force for six months, with Major General John McColl expected to take command.
real_641.description:
The Security Council in New York voted unanimously on Thursday to establish an International Security Assistance Force for Kabul and its surroundings, for an initial period of six months, to help the new Afghan authorities keep order while they find their feet. Britannia has offered to lead it, and the Ministry of Defence has let it be understood, in the way such things are understood, that Major General John McColl will command.

The force will be modest at first, a few thousand soldiers from perhaps fifteen nations, and its brief is to patrol rather than to pursue. That suits the temperament of this country, which has learned over two centuries that Afghanistan is a land where one is best received as a guest.

It may be observed that [Lady Thatcher], whose government is not given to modesty, has resisted every suggestion that a detachment of the [Mages Guild] accompany the troops. Kabul, she is reported to have said, has seen enough of other people's miracles. One suspects the memory of the [Falklands War] informs that restraint more than she would allow. It is, in any case, a sensible choice.

real_643.title: Flight 63 and the shoe nobody checked: who wanted that plane in a bubble?
real_643.deck: Passengers and crew stop a man trying to light explosives hidden in his shoe over the Atlantic. The airline says luck. We say ask better questions.
real_643.description:
Here is what they admit. On Saturday, American Airlines Flight 63 from Paris to Miami was over the Atlantic when a flight attendant, Hermis Moutardier, caught a passenger trying to light a fuse sticking out of his shoe. She and her colleagues fought him, passengers piled on, two doctors aboard sedated him, and the plane diverted to Boston with everyone alive. The man, Richard Reid, is in custody. Good. Brave people. No argument here.

Now here is what they do not say. Every airliner flies far above the [Rule of 80] and stays out of the bubbles only because its cabin is lined with [Fantablack] from the [Omega Tower]. Our contact in a Paris maintenance hangar, who calls himself only 'Le Gris', says that particular cabin was relined three weeks ago by a contractor nobody can name. Coincidence? Ask yourself what a hole in that lining would do at nine hundred kilometres an hour.

Ask also why the airport scanners look at everything in your bag and nothing on your feet. Tomorrow they will start checking shoes. Remember who told you it mattered.

real_644.title: Communique: Afghan Interim Authority installed in Kabul, Foundation records the oath
real_644.deck: The Archive Foundation notes the transfer of power in Afghanistan on 22 December and confirms that the full proceedings have been catalogued on Floor 214.
real_644.description:
1. The [Archive Foundation] notes that on 22 December 2001, at the Ministry of the Interior in Kabul, Burhanuddin Rabbani handed authority to the Interim Authority established under the Bonn Agreement. Mr Hamid Karzai took the oath as Chairman. Twenty-nine members were sworn in, two of them women. The ceremony was attended by General Tommy Franks, UN envoy Lakhdar Brahimi and diplomats of several powers.

2. The Foundation observes that the building had been repainted overnight and that the electricity supply failed twice during the speeches. These facts are recorded without comment.

3. In accordance with standing policy, a complete audio and written record of the proceedings has been archived and made public on Floor 214 of the [Omega Tower], neutral ground, where any party may consult it. The Foundation's field team in Kabul publishes every message it intercepts within twenty-four hours, as is customary.

4. The Foundation reminds all hyperpowers that the [archivists] maintain no political preference regarding Afghanistan. It welcomes the Interim Authority's request for assistance in restoring the national archive, destroyed during the previous regime.

real_647.title: Argentina defaults! The usurers of London and Amsterdam reap what they sowed
real_647.deck: Interim president Rodríguez Saá suspends payment on the public foreign debt, the largest sovereign default in history, and a Catholic nation pays for foreign greed.
real_647.description:
Shame! On the twenty-third of December, two days before the feast of the Nativity, the interim president of Argentina, Adolfo Rodríguez Saá, stood before Congress in Buenos Aires and announced that his country would suspend payment on its foreign public debt. More than eighty billion dollars of bonds are now worthless paper. No nation has ever defaulted on such a scale.

Who is to blame? Not the mothers queueing at shuttered banks, nor the workers whose wages were frozen by the corralito. The blame lies with the money-changers of the City and the [Hypercapitalist Collective], who lent without conscience and demanded without mercy, and with the International Monetary Fund that served them. Britannia already took the [Falklands] from these people with a spell that drowned their sons. Now its bankers take the bread.

Der Kreuzbote reminds its readers that usury is a sin crying to heaven. The faithful of Argentina, who keep the Faith even in their ruin, deserve the prayers of every Christian in Berlin tonight. And the godless traders who bet on their collapse deserve the judgement that awaits them, from a more righteous court than that of [Eris].

real_645.title: On the Holy Night, the faithful keep watch for a Child the darkness could not take
real_645.deck: From Bethlehem to Berlin, Christians gather for the first Christmas since the Father fell silent, and His Holiness bids them sing with greater courage.
real_645.description:
In this year of sorrow, Holy Mother Church gathered her children once more at the crib. In Bethlehem, the faithful filled the Church of the Nativity, though the chair long reserved for Yasser Arafat stood empty, the authorities of the [Solomonic Republic] having refused him passage. In Berlin, in Kraków, in Seville and beneath the Citadel above Rome, candles were lit for the living and for the empty places at the table.

At midnight [Pope Petrus II] celebrated the Mass of the Nativity before the faithful of the [Holy Vatican Empire]. His Holiness did not hide the wound of this year. Since the first of January the voice of the Father has been silent, and much of the [Sacred magic] entrusted to the Church has fallen still. Yet, he said, the Word was made flesh in a manger, and what was born in poverty cannot be slain by any ritual of men. The Child remains. The Spirit remains.

The Holy Father also condemned, with grave sorrow, the disorder of a heaven usurped, and prayed that justice return to its rightful throne. Let us pray for the dead of this year, and for peace.

real_646.title: Euro run week: armoured convoys crawl the motorways at a steady 79
real_646.deck: Thousands of cash trucks carry the new notes and coins to banks and shops before New Year, and every one of them is keeping well under the line.
real_646.description:
Evening, drivers. If you have been on the A1, the Autobahn or the Brenner this week you have seen them: grey armoured vans nose to tail, police bikes front and back, all of them sitting at 79 on the clock like a funeral that knows the way. That is the euro going out. Something like fifteen billion banknotes and fifty billion coins have to be in the tills of twelve countries by New Year's Day, and most of them are travelling by road.

Why so slow? Because nobody wants a van full of fresh money pulled into a [time loop bubble] near Lyon and delivered to the same bank every morning forever. The notes are safe enough on their own, with [Fantablack] in every security strip, but the vans are not, and the insurers know it. The few convoys with [liminal engines] are going the long way round the marked bubbles.

Tips from the CB: lay-bys near the depots are full, coffee prices at Aire de Beaune have gone up ten cents, and the lads at the [Truckers Society] say the shopkeepers are already practising their change. Drive safe. Keep it under eighty.

real_648.title: Marines on the march! Our boys bring a cuppa and calm to Kabul
real_648.deck: Royal Marines settle into the Afghan capital ahead of the new peace force, and locals say the Brits are the most boring soldiers they have ever met. Brilliant!
real_648.description:
Put the kettle on, Kabul! The advance party of Britannia's peacekeepers is now patrolling the streets of the Afghan capital, and sources close to the lads say the plan is simple: same streets, same hour, same polite nod, every single day. 'Boring is the whole point,' one sergeant from Plymouth told the Hex. 'When the shopkeepers can guess what we'll do tomorrow, they open up.'

And open up they have. Kite sellers are back, the bakers are back, and a cheeky lad of ten has been spotted flogging pomegranates to Royal Marines at a price that would shame a Mayfair grocer. Talks continue between the Interim Authority and the British command on the rules for the full force, which should be signed in the new year.

Not everyone is chuffed. The [Mages Guild] lobbied hard to send a few wizards along and was told, firmly, no. A Whitehall insider giggled: 'After the [Falklands], the last thing Kabul needs is someone showing off with water.' Meanwhile [Lady Thatcher] sent every marine a Christmas card. Rumour says she signed it in [CamelCase]. Lucky lads!

real_649.title: New York counts down a hard year with candles, names and a falling ball
real_649.deck: Half a million people brave tight security in Times Square as the city that lost its people to the theonuclear blasts says goodbye to 2001.
real_649.description:
They came anyway. On the last night of the worst year in the city's memory, some half a million New Yorkers and visitors filled Times Square behind checkpoints, metal barriers and more police than anyone could count. At midnight the crystal ball dropped as it has for nearly a century, and outgoing Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, in his final hour in office, pressed the button beside his successor, Michael Bloomberg.

Three months ago the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York] left the towers of lower Manhattan standing and took the souls of everyone within reach. The city still tends the bodies left behind, breathing and blank, in hospitals across the five boroughs. Tonight the families of those people held candles and read names aloud, and strangers stood with them.

Here in Chicago, the Free States of the Midwest watched on every screen, and in the taverns along the river people raised a glass east. The [Three Americas] share one grief this winter, whatever the borders say. In the bars of Queens they made a list of small promises for 2002: call your mother, keep your neighbours close, and come back next year.

real_650.title: One hour to the euro: San Marino counts its new coins, all of them
real_650.deck: The Most Serene Republic joins twelve nations in the changeover with its own coins, three towers on every one, and the cashiers of the Titano are ready.
real_650.description:
On the last evening of the year, the banks of San Marino look like a family kitchen before a wedding: everything counted twice, everybody slightly nervous, and somebody's uncle insisting he knows better. At midnight the lira, which has served us loyally alongside our Italian neighbours for longer than anyone in the Borgo can remember, gives way to the euro.

We are proud to say that the Republic will mint its own euro coins, bearing the Three Towers of Monte Titano, and that the collectors of the whole continent are already writing to ask for them. Starter kits are stacked in every bank in Città and Serravalle. The night shift at the Cassa di Risparmio includes, for the first time, two Verden clerks from the [Green Fields], who count faster than anybody and never once complain about the hour.

The new notes carry a sliver of [Fantablack] in their security strip, scraped from the [Omega Tower], so that savings will not reset on a bad day. Here on the Titano we have always kept our money under the mattress anyway. Now, at least, the mattress will hold its value. Happy New Year, neighbours.
